Or, even if they do yield, we will also bend in accordance with how we try to believe, love, and put it into practice in the coming times. Other than this, we are not going to get any opportunity from such matters to specifically say, know, or think anything about the destruction that is going to befall our lineage.

People might tell us about the great merits they achieved in times past. Whatever that may be, we must be convinced that there is a great blunder before us. Who are we in the karma spoken of by the many thousands of Gurus and more than twenty-five prophets who have come and gone? How will we theorize all these? How much have we been able to accomplish in the same measure as the karma they performed in their times? If we did accomplish it, what did we transform it into? To what extent were we able to merge into it?

If we can ponder this slowly and adopt it over time, the first thing we must understand is that we have a flaw. What is this flaw? In what era did it occur? How did it come about? We stand having been born in an era where these things can be clearly known, and with the karmic capacity to find a solution for it. Having understood this, can it be taken up as a karma; will that dharma be attained through that experience; can this dharma be undertaken in a way that is free from karmic blemish? This is what you should think about. Otherwise, if you go about listening to, thinking about, and saying many things, you will have no foundation in anything. You do not know how to retrieve and preserve anything. Nor do you know what karma is to be preserved the most.

What needs to be preserved the most is our character in life. What has mostly accumulated in life are entanglements. We must see that those entanglements are karmic attributes clinging to our soul. Within that karmic attribute itself, this karma can be prepared and contained. If that karmic attribute is made to repent, what are the good things that can come to us? You should at least have an idea to know this much. Only then will you feel that this is worth taking up. And that too, without rejecting anything.

The guidance that has reached the karmic path of the human world up to this day must have surely reached the extent of the karmic attribute of this entanglement. If there is no doubt about it, one only needs to look at what that aspect is. That is the Shaiva, Shakta, and Vaishnava traditions. For the Shakta, that is supreme; for the Shaiva, that is supreme; for the Vaishnava, that is supreme. Besides, there are thousands of its branches. In this special dharma that we have been practicing, seeing, knowing, and speaking of in these traditions, how much merit-acquiring karma have we been able to perform? It has been lost in such a way that our families, our countrymen, let alone the Vedic religion or any notable prophetic religion, are unable to perform this dharma. If asked how this loss occurred, they will only evade the question.

We can only live in accordance with the dharma and karma of the parents we got. Otherwise, what else can we do but get caught in some karma that the land and its people characterize as good or bad, and take on and foster that karmic blemish. We have a history of karmic blemishes that cannot be exhausted no matter how much is said. But that is not our resolve, is it?

What is it that we require? What constitutes the realm that falls within the divine ordinance? How can we assume this responsibility? The human world requires a disposition that comprehends this. We cannot progress by exhaustively studying the system of the Trinity and the Manu system that prevailed for numerous epochs prior to it. There is only one core subject for this. If one fails to comprehend it, it remains a subject prone to the gravest errors. In what manner have the great souls of the past demonstrated this? One might have heard of deeds encompassing certain extraordinary mystical powers. The common populace cannot achieve anything by merely relying on these mystical abilities. For example, suppose an individual ascended to heaven in their physical body. What do we gain from such an occurrence? Would we derive any tangible benefit by merely recounting this narrative and offering our reverence?

This is what we must comprehend: during our lifetime, we must discern the virtues and vices of bygone eras. We must understand the reasons why these virtues and vices have become a burden upon us. To realize this, we must trace our steps backward. Having been born absorbed in the karmic legacy that our ancestors revered and worshipped, we cannot arbitrarily discard it or abruptly transform it into something entirely different. However, we can deduce one fundamental truth. The Divine cannot manifest in a paradigm that assigns a separate deity to each caste. Do men and women have distinct gods?

We remain ignorant of how the karmic force, which has purportedly manifested as distinct deities for men, women, and various castes, is sustained. Consequently, our entire understanding is restricted to a lineage that chased miracles and exhibited extraordinary mystical powers. We have not comprehended these mystical powers as a systematic discipline of knowledge. Instead, we have misconstrued them as a distinct form of spiritual wisdom. If an individual resides somewhere and offers solace to a few people, society immediately questions whether he is a mystic. We have erroneously equated the term mystic with an enlightened being. We remain completely unaware of the fundamental truth that a mystic is not necessarily an enlightened being.

What is the karmic course that astonishes us by performing Jinn worship and displaying the frenzy of various devotional spectacles, or the karmic course of a Brahmarakshas yearning to merge with Brahman? There is a story told regarding this Brahmarakshas. A Yaksha summoned gods like Agni, Vayu, and Varuna and placed a blade of grass before them. But these gods could not stir or move it. Agni could not burn it, nor could Vayu blow it away. What can we understand about this blade of grass? We evaluate this miracle from within the confines of a karmic potential that has been subjected to the passage of time in mythology. What is the meaning in saying, "I do not respect this"? There is a fact that this was once revered. Do we disrespect it because it does not exist, or because we have too much knowledge, or because we lack knowledge? Therefore, we must comprehend a matter in accordance with our knowledge. Otherwise, you will face great ruin. Let this be understood first.

What constitutes your knowledge? "Yesterday, I went to such-and-such places. Today as well, I went. Now I am returning." Expressed differently, "I went, came back exhausted, lay down, and slept well." How does one know that he slept? Sleeping is a transformation of the life force. The individual himself knows the state of sleeping well. However, what is the cause? We require the karmic capacity to recover and understand what the cause is. If what is seen in the waking state appears in the dream state, and what is seen in the dream state appears in deep sleep, there is a mechanism that grants liberation to the deep sleep state. The term deep sleep is generally understood as a state of sleeping without knowing anything. However, that is not the case. There is a dimension where one sees without physical eyes during deep sleep. So, which is this eye that sees? It is that which perceives within the core of the mind. That is the karmic course we cultivate. How will that dharma reach us?

In the nature of this mind's eye, the karmic course of billions of years is being dragged before us. That was never done by me. It was not done by my ancestors. Then who did this? What we observe here is a karma that remained hidden behind some flawed action. If you do not completely understand this, you will find it difficult to grasp. What you assume is that if you invoke God, you must become wealthy tomorrow. Or you must become the greatest ruler. Or you must attain happiness by roaming freely and living as you please without any illness. Which of these is good? All are indeed good. But you must understand one thing. We possess a certain familiarity that our ancestors believed, knew, and communicated. We must realize where this will lead us. How does this manifest before us in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states? We have been made an instrument for this.

We are gradually observing and comprehending what ripens in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states one by one. What is this waking, dream, and deep sleep? In the waking state, the eyes may be closed, or they may be open. Whether the eyes are closed or open, there is a nature of seeing. Even while sleeping, that special attribute does not leave us. Furthermore, one perceives while remaining in a silent, motionless state where the nature of space and time is indiscernible. This is another facet of deep sleep. It is difficult to comprehend how this comes to us. If one begins to count its seeds, another problem arises. Did the seed come first or the mango? What answer can be given to this? By standing on a sense of dharma that rationalizes certain things which can be dismissed through logic by asking such questions, who can we become? We will become no one.

If you accept a title such as Guru, Deva, Rishi, or Sanyasi, you must understand one thing. What did we gain from the actions of about twenty-five prophets of the past? Similarly, what will you gain by hearing, knowing, and reading about sages who have come and gone across epochs, and about a Guru who emerged as the controller of miraculous deeds by displaying numerous mystic powers and miracles? That is not it; what you need is a center of faith that grasps these past occurrences. What will you observe in this karma that stands capable, having seen and grasped the actions of various epochs? This is what must be seen in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states. When it thus occurs and is experienced in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states, one must be able to recognize what it is. There are some individuals here who are capable of knowing this. So, what should we do? We must attain the karmic capability to grasp the cause, through which we became eligible to attain it. That cause, which guides us to retrieve both the good and the bad, can only instruct us on the capability to attain this path. That must be instructed in accordance with each individual's knowledge. Otherwise, one might be bewildered, assuming that one's own actions are entirely perfect, and love may manifest as a reflection of ego, resulting in nothing being accomplished. The love of God is not this. It is a karmic course that traverses thousands of paths that we have crossed, walked, known, and acted upon. It cannot be acquired merely by hearing, knowing, or speaking about it. It only guides you by explaining that what you see and hear is precisely this, in accordance with your understanding. Before a Guru who imparts such teachings, everything—all the enlightened beings, yogis, gurus, and prophets from all the traditions that have existed hitherto—must assemble. You should only accept such a person as your Guru. Otherwise, you will commit a grave error. You will fall to the ground like someone who loses their grip. How should you perform your karma by incorporating life, having understood at least this much? You will not incur any harm merely because you did not contemplate on God. However, you will not receive its benefits either.

What is meant by faith in God? The ancestral curse of many predecessors, who waited for prosperity and wealth by making vows and offerings, building numerous pavilions, and constructing grand temples, remains within us. How can this curse be removed? You need not wander aimlessly for any of this. No matter where you wander, it will not work. What you need is a Guru who is capable of liberating everything that you and your ancestors have previously worshipped. Whether one is a prophet, or someone who has demonstrated brilliance by recounting various legendary riches while standing in the path of the prophets, or someone who has advanced far in mystical practices and attained the power of levitation, all of them must come before this Guru for the sake of their lives. Unless you surrender and pray to such a Guru, you will not gain any special benefit.
Guruvani
July 2002

We have an outdated worshipping habit of getting things done by offering something insignificant to God. This is not the way; we should worship God to seek His grace. What should be done to attain God's grace? We have a duty towards God. We must understand it and perform it with a sense of duty. Because we have not done so, we have been committing errors in our worship of God for a long time.

There is discord between husband and wife. As they continue to quarrel into their old age, their children will also follow suit. This is what I have observed to this day. Only in a few homes is this lack of culture absent. You have never entrusted your children with the knowledge of what is not being done for you here at the ashram. You have not entrusted them with it until today. I do not know what will be done tomorrow.

God does not need your vows and offerings. Are we supposed to offer vows and offerings just to find a righteous path? If you wish to offer something, you may do so. Why? When such a custom has emerged in society, you can do so to learn some kind of lesson from it. That can be done in a temple or an ashram. However, that is not the matter I am discussing with you regarding the worship of God. There is a state of ignorance that our ancestors have perpetuated to this day. By uttering certain words in the very nature of that ignorance and trying to triumph through those words, you are holding on to certain karmic flaws.

Wherever you go in the hilly regions, people speak in grandiose terms and act as if they possess great culture. However, not even a trace of culture can be found in them. By constantly exhibiting their culture, they have become like Westerners showing off their culture. What is that culture? It is only an external culture. It is not internal. They have decided that internal culture is unnecessary. This has infiltrated every home and its inner core.

Since the practice of making vows and offerings has been going on for a long time, it has evolved within the temple system and grown to a large scale. In order to resolve the complications caused by this, God has imparted a certain knowledge to us over various periods. It was given through numerous great souls. Yet, we still have not understood that knowledge today.

Christians are the community that habitually preaches the greatest sacrifice. But is there sacrifice among Christians now? The meaning of sacrifice is to practice living truthfully. Are Christians living truthfully now? Christians stand like compasses pointing towards the West. Other than the culture of the home remaining among some poor people, it does not exist in a single household that has enough to eat, drink, and wear. Why? It is the Hindus who have shifted towards that today. They have also adopted the practice of vows and offerings similar to that of the Hindus. They are even prepared to commit any kind of violence in the name of God.

Muslims claim that they govern according to laws determined by God. Is the divine law that one can commit any kind of plunder? If this is the situation within the Islamic religion, which emerged only a short time ago, Hindus possess a history that has undergone immense changes over time. Hindus embraced oracular deities and became devoid of culture. When their authority waned, they attempted to appear great by displaying foolishness. Similarly, there is caste, and castes within castes. Those who belonged to a higher caste began to live by flaunting its greatness. Those who were not considered great began to live like Westerners. Because of this, humanity has drifted away from its true nature. As human nature drifted away, a realization that both men and women need freedom has spread.

The sense of freedom is good. But what is freedom? It is assumed that freedom is men and women properly arguing and justifying their stances. That is not freedom. What shortcomings have we experienced in the past? The women in the house must know this. What was the situation amidst those shortcomings? How did it happen? Teach them this first. Due to those shortcomings, we have received a misguided life. When the uncultured Western culture began to spread, it became even worse.

Aside from presenting models of sacrifice, there is no actual sacrifice among Christians. Who has become Christians? Those who lived as the most downtrodden among the Hindus. When they acquire money and capability, they will not stay grounded. They will only behave without any manners. Today, Christians and Muslims in Kerala have become wealthy. However, their culture is completely different. They speak eloquently with sweet words, but they will not translate it into action. This is a path towards danger.

God has given you the most suitable opportunity. But you will not take it. I will only speak and behave truthfully with you. What do you do? You squander it. What can I do? What kind of freedom have you envisioned? It is an inferiority complex born from having lived in servitude. This is one kind of freedom. Another is the freedom of an arrogant life. Yet another is the freedom derived from fighting over caste and religion. Is this the freedom of humanity?

Have you felt this idea to be true? If so, you are the ones who must put it into practice. It is for you to implement that I have done this. People assume that this is how freedom should be sought. This freedom is not freedom. It is a freedom that drags our children into error.

The greatest ignorance lies in the hands of the educated. In uneducated children, flaws are seen much less. Wherever wealth, capability, and education have risen, arrogance has also risen. The culture of Mayyanad, the culture of Kottayam, and looking more broadly, Ernakulam, Kochi, and then a different culture in Kozhikode. Thus, how many types of cultures exist in Kerala itself! If you are imparting such a cultureless knowledge, what have you decided to give to your children? I am asking those who come and reside here. The reason you Hindus, Christians, Muslims, and people from Brahmins to Chandalas come and stay here is because I have love and obligation towards you, and you towards me. I have taught you after having done something myself. But that is not what you have perceived. You live here as if carrying a resentment that is the greatest accumulation of an undignified life. You must not bring your old resentment in here and express it. If you express it, your children will be lost. Then I will not be able to do anything. Why do you commit such perversity here? I am telling you this after addressing the flaw that has come down through your lineage, and altering even the freedom of worship to a different path so that the culture of your home may change. But you are unable to think, understand, or obey it.

I have eradicated the tradition that you have been worshipping. I have not done this by looking at whether it is Hindu, Christian, Muslim, or Buddhist. The core of that old culture has been uprooted from your tradition. Have I ever considered whether you are a Brahmin or a Chandala? What I am asking is whether you have ever thought that at least one child who has lived here to date should grow up in this new culture. The experience I have received from everyone who worked near me, and from their entire families, is pain. If that is not the case, you must say so.

Why have I done this for you? If you did not need it, then why did you make me do it? Is anyone among you prepared to live according to that standard and show it to me? Are you living here to corrupt this concept given by God and ruin yourselves?

After taking hold of all your old baseness and doing the work to liberate you from it, the first thing you are told is that you must abandon the principles of caste and class (Jati-Varna Dharmas). You must tell me if you have abandoned them. If you had abandoned them, this is not how you would be behaving here. Is it not a culture forcibly imposed from somewhere that you are holding onto as your asset? Is this why you are being nurtured with such great effort? Have I done things for you while preserving my own self-interest? Please tell me; I want to know this from you yourselves.

You should not assume that I am speaking only about the matter of caste. I categorically state that not a single one of you has been careful in any matter. What is the purpose of sugarcoating these pleasant words to me? For what reason did you come here, believe in this, and reside here? That is what you must tell me. If anyone has acted with genuine affection towards this concept, towards me, and towards the institution, tell me that. Other than living engrossed in the act of feigning prosperity and friendship wherever you look to create a non-existent wealth, what have you done for this? If you do not wish to instill your culture in your children, you must move away from here. Otherwise, you will only leave after destroying this and turning it into a culture of division.

You are performing actions with your focus on some distant goal. Whom are you trying to appease; are you showing this baseness to appease God? If you exhibit this anymore, I will not stand with you. Those who remain within and those associated with this should act only after understanding that. I am saying this to you with absolute certainty. You only need to believe in this, live here, and associate with this if you have the resolve to live truthfully. You do not need to say anything for me to hear. You just need to live and show me. I do not need to hear you say anything. I will not believe it.

You have become the Shudra class. Any mistake that arises from you is not intentional. When you act, it will only happen that way. How many among you came having perceived this before seeing me physically! You can increase your spiritual merit only if you handle this with the understanding that it is a manifestation of divine will. Otherwise, neither doctrines nor miraculous feats are being preached here. What will you gain if I perform miracles?

Someone performed a miracle. Someone portrayed themselves as a great person. Because of that, what inner peace do we attain? You are witnessing this directly. You are directly experiencing spiritual merit. There are so many people who have known me for a very long time. Because they lacked familial fortune, they went astray. What is meant by familial fortune? Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra. It has been understood that this is the era where the class standing in the fourth quarter possesses authority, hasn't it? What authority? The Shudra class holds the authority for the knowledge of Brahman. When speaking of the Shudra class, there is a Brahmin and a Shudra in each of our homes. This is the rationale. But this is not what has been conveyed to us. Instead, Varnasrama Dharma was celebrated, and we were hidden under that class and reduced to a caste. This has grown to such an extent that no one can do anything about it. Today, if we take India as a whole, there are one hundred and eighty-four castes. Let each person reflect upon where we have reached.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarppana Pathippu 2002
Experience, Not Vedanta, Is the Truth

For us to breathe, the lungs must function. For the lungs to function, there must be a sky around us. We observe, or rather state, that there are numerous spheres around this atmospheric nature of the earth. What do we see within this solar system?

We shattered the skies of interstellar space and reached the moon. Even having broken through thus, other than revolving around the sun, what would happen if we crossed beyond it? We become bewildered upon hearing the stories of these journeys. In the rotation involving the sun, the moon, and the earth, other spheres do not catch our eyes. Yet, they certainly exist. We have not yet seen what exists in these spheres.

Navajyothi! The word Navajyothi means nine types of light. We are the people who, even after seeing these nine types of light, claim they do not exist. If this is not visible, then where has it been hidden? When a celestial vibration occurs amidst the layers of clouds standing on parallel borders, our eyes cannot reach its subtlety. It exists. But we do not understand it. Therefore, we do not know how to apply it. If we deny the existence of what truly is, we cannot move beyond it. Every discovery has a limitation. That is all we need to say. Do not say it does not exist. That is what is good for us.

We feel utterly afraid to recognize what is good. Here, we fail. Growing from small to great, or growing in the arrogance of education, wealth, and mastery, how far will we go? We have a human experience that cannot recognize this. It has come through our customs. We currently stand in this predicament.

It is said that Brahmins are the ones who destroyed everything in the nature of customs. How does that Brahmin's house look? Did they prosper after destroying it? If there are twenty-five houses in a village, at least two girls in them will be found unmarried. What is the reason for that? If they did not prosper, then who are you saying did prosper? We do not know what the deep roots of this are.

It is said that God is formless. And that is true. How far can each of us reach on this path that remains formless? That is why the matter of the solar system was mentioned earlier. No matter how many times these nine colors are multiplied, or in what all ways they are handled, they will still remain. Who said this color does not exist? This color is not something that can be eliminated merely by saying so. This is what was referred to as the limitation encountered in experience. If someone denies the existence of what truly is, why should you believe them? If an item is requested and it is not in that particular place, does it mean the item does not exist at all? Whether one is a rationalist or a salvation-seeker, what exists simply exists. It cannot be eliminated.

We state certain justifications regarding Yuga Dharma (the law of the age). However, it has merely not been understood that what is stated is Yuga Dharma. As long as it is not understood, we cannot complete a transition phase. For example, the time is now such-and-such—after a while, this light will assume a different nature. Progressing in this way, there will be a junction for it. Similarly, a junction occurs after every three hours. We are experiencing this junction. But we are unable to resolve it. In this situation, how will we resolve the Yugasandhi (the junction of the ages)? This is what was referred to as our limitation.

We do not know how the juncture of the ages (*Yugasandhi*) operates. It is to make this known that the great souls (*Mahatmas*) were made to act. They strove in various ways for such a long time. It is in this context that we celebrate Sree Krishna, Sree Rama, Sree Shankara, Jesus, the Prophet, Buddha, and Mahavira. We cannot move forward by saying that none of them existed or made any effort. But we need to know the extent to which they have operated. For which era did they work? We know the different times in which they operated. However, there is a distinct period between the times they worked. What we do not know is how to determine the nature of that distinct period.

We must determine this. Only after that should we move forward. Otherwise, errors will occur. That will not be an error like the ones that have happened so far. It will be a much greater blunder. We need an instrument to determine this. And you also need the knowledge to accept that instrument. Will a deaf and ignorant person be able to hear if their head is drilled? In the present situation, each of us is a fool. Let this foolishness remain. But we must surely overcome it.

How can we slip and fall at the juncture of the times when the people called great souls have operated? We cannot proceed by abandoning these great men. If we say that Jesus does not belong to our religion, does it mean that Jesus is not the truth? Would it be right to say that Sree Shankara and Sree Rama are not ours? What will we do with that reality which does not disappear even if we reject it? By not accepting this, we become complete strangers in the path of God. To avoid becoming strangers like this, at least believe that all these truly exist. The one who says they do not exist is not going to reach anywhere. They certainly exist. How should we view this reality?

The state in which we all exist and act is the waking state (*Jagrat*). Similarly, we experience the dream state (*Swapna*) and deep sleep (*Sushupti*). Beyond this knowledge, there is visionary knowledge. It is our soul (*Jiva*) that acquires that knowledge. What is the state of knowledge that the soul perceives beyond the waking, dream, and deep sleep states? That is *Turiya* (the fourth state). It is in that knowledge that we can comprehend the courses and dynamics of our various lifetimes. We must perceive this. If we cannot perceive it, we must believe what those who have perceived it tell us. There is no other logic to this. We must have the karmic awareness to understand and painstakingly acquire what the seers impart. Everyone needs this awareness. In the journey of the soul, we can realize that even a blade of grass, if it exists, needs this awareness. This is the knowledge we attain in the state of *Turiya*.

To what stage of this knowledge did these great souls reach and speak of before they departed! No one should say that these states of knowledge of the soul do not exist just because they are explained with such grand words. This is real. How will we perceive this reality? It may not be that all of us perceive it subtly. Acknowledge its existence to the extent of our experience. Believe the words of those who say there is more beyond it. If you cannot agree with it, you may choose not to believe it as well.

Regardless, it is a truth that there is a formless space. Which heaven (or ether) this formless space is, comes later. It is from there that one perceives what exists. Saying "Alas, I am defeated" also happens from that very state. One aspect of this is saying, "O Lord, what have you shown me, who firmly believed that there is nothing other than You." Reaching the state of what was said, they stood there. That is the position where that religion stands. We should not say it is not so. Whatever those who saw and spoke said is true to the extent they have seen. Just because we have not seen the boundary of truth, we should not say that nothing exists beyond it. Saying so does not make it non-existent. What we need to know is how far this reality operates. This is where these great souls have reached and halted. If they faced a limit, it is no wonder that we also hit a wall.

The great souls have taught us from the point they had reached. There is no need to say that it was too little or too much. You may not even be able to experience and move past what has been stated here. To experience it in such a manner, there must be another dimension to it. That is the truth of *Guru-Laghutva* (the relationship of the heavy/great and the light/small).

Otherwise, our ancestors existed. Our parents existed. Each of us is the lightness (*Laghutva*) of their discoveries. That lightness is what has come as the Guru. We perceive whatever conceptual power has arrived in the word 'Guru'. It is through that we attempt to see the boundless. That requires an innate predisposition (*Vasanajanyata*). Human beings who perceived everything in the position of saying "not this, not this" (*Neti, Neti*) lived here. There are such great souls who have passed away. We must understand that there are also those who are yet to come. We need an instrument to compare those who have passed, those who exist now, and those who are to come. That is what is called *Guru-Laghutva*.

Some speak of Vedanta. Why speak of Vedanta? Isn't it enough to state what exists? Let us first understand what is. Then we can understand what is not. That which exists remains formless. It is beyond thought, akin to the sky. If it has such an ethereal nature, in what all states does it exist? This can only be possible if the Guru reveals it. There are many who have seen this. The Guru is not merely the one who sees, but the one who reveals it.

Now, how will we comprehend *Laghutva* (lightness)? It was said that to see what exists, one must hold onto the rightful heir. The Guru is the one who tells where the seat of greatness lies and what that greatness looks like. From the Guru, one can know what Karma is. The Guru is the master of an intellect that creates greatness through instruction and practice. That is what one must hold onto. By utilizing that, we will reach a position entirely devoid of the defects of Karma. That position is the seat of Truth. It is from there that everything else must be perceived. That is *Guru-Laghutva*.

Only that which exists can be shown. That which is said to not exist cannot be shown. It is merely a stream of words. This refers to the Karma resting in the evolutionary nature of the soul, which operates anywhere as the atom of an atom. Never say that it does not exist. It is real. The goal is to know how to understand that reality. Both men and women have equal rights to it.

We must only proceed there after discerning the boundaries of the great souls. Suppose we cannot reach there. Does that mean it ceases to exist? We can attain it. But even if we reach it, there are difficulties; if we do not stand on the side of love, then it will cause harm.

How can this reality be perceived across these three states of waking, dream, and deep sleep? Seeing what the Dharma resting in the subconscious mind is after that, is a special state. What is that state? Isn't it said in Tamil, *'Thoongamal thoongi'* (sleeping without sleeping). It is not sleeping, though others believe one is asleep. It is something attained in a state of absorption (*Laya*) with closed eyes. This can be seen with eyes closed or open. Only a great power that has reached the *Turiya* state can reveal a *Karmayoga* that permeates the waking, dream, and deep sleep states. How many heavens must be crossed for that is a secondary matter.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Birthday Dedication Edition 2002
The truthful aspects of life and the ethical aspects to be followed

Some people may have faith in God. Some may not. Some people may not immediately understand if they see a novel model in the realm of faith. We cannot say if it is due to their fault or the fault of their land. Because that is the familiarity of the worship we have been maintaining. The majority are people who ask if it isn't enough to keep faith in the mind without showing it outwardly.
Guru: Is faith enough in the mind, or should it be shown outwardly in action?
Answer: In the mind is enough.

Guru: In that case, isn't it enough to eat with the mind? Isn't it enough to get married with the mind? After all, it is the mind that is given to God. God also resides within the mind itself. This is an arrogant attitude, speaking like those who are left over after everything is finished. This is not your own opinion. It is saying something you heard someone blabbering about.

The cultural richness necessary for our homes is absent in any of the religious doctrines we have seen, heard, or known. What is the religious doctrine of the Hindus? One places a local deity (*Madan*) and addresses it as the Lord. Another attempts to reach *Brahman* directly. Yet another does neither, but approaches through a Guru. The one who tries to reach God directly can never be guided properly.

It is not my duty to draw you closer by feigning affection. For when that affection is absent, will you not simply leave? Is it sufficient to keep you close merely by speaking of love? I shall speak of love; that is a different matter entirely. However, you will only grasp this if you absorb these earnestly spoken words with the gravity they deserve. Otherwise, it will slip away.

There are several Devi temples in these regions, which many people celebrate with great pomp. Yet, these individuals never truly unite with one another. It is rare to find someone who does not display a sense of ego after expressing irritation towards another. An elder brother will maintain a stance of superiority. A younger brother will harbor the attitude that the other need not act superior. Even in the absence of outward conflict, they will stand in mental defiance. This is a distinct characteristic of South Travancore.

What if one goes south to the Neyyattinkara taluk? Is there anyone there who does not boast about the greatness of their *Potti* (Brahmin) ancestors? All of this is a kind of mischief. Why engage in such boasting? What is there to gain for anyone? This is merely akin to claiming, 'My grandfather had an elephant'. It is difficult to change such a corrupt nature that one has heard, known, and witnessed since childhood. This is not the case of a single household or a single village. From Chirayinkeezhu southwards, this characteristic is widespread. Then there is the usage of certain terms like *Akkachi* and *Thankachi*. This represents a sort of culture from Tamil Nadu. The moment they cease to show happiness, they will start using abusive language. This culture is far worse than Western culture. Elder brothers, younger brothers, sisters, and siblings may exhibit a great deal of love and respect for each other during childhood. However, as they grow up, they display a rather repulsive attitude. What is the core intent behind my words? Where do you end up when the thoughts from your youth go astray as you move forward? What is the linguistic style here? 'Swami should say, should take, should give'—an inherently commanding tone. It is not spoken with malicious intent; it is simply their customary manner. But if you go north, this is considered a grave error. Every place has its distinct attire and language. Similarly, each caste has its own deity. The temple of an Ezhava will not suit a Nair. The temple of a Nair will not suit an Ezhava. Can a God thus divided ever be the true God? This is the fundamental blunder committed not just by India, but by the entire world.

Only one or two members from your household will come here; the rest will not. If those who do not come fail to understand the ways here, they will end up quarreling with you. What will you do then? You will try to compromise with everyone. Can you abandon your home? Can you abandon this place either? What will your situation be then? Sorrow will never cease. You will be completely unable to form a deep bond with what you truly cherish.

You perform *Guru Pooja* here. What is *Guru Pooja*? A Guru can be worshipped by offering a single drop of water, by lighting a lamp, or with elaborate decorations. In places like Kanchipuram, Rishikesh, Vrindavan, and Ayodhya, ascetics (*Sadhus*) are worshipped. What does the term *Sadhu* mean? There are people around you who live by doing manual labor and begging. Their souls possess no merit; they are bound by the power of sin. Hence, they are merely poor or destitute. *Sadhus* are not like that. Having experienced abundance in food, drink, and clothing to the point of satiation, they renounced everything. Such a person is entirely complete. A true householder (*Grihasthashrami*) should also be like this. Therefore, can you ever become a true householder if you constantly boast about someone else's greatness? What you must attain is the virtue of your own actions. That must first be received from God. You must realize that invoking God is not for God's sake, but entirely for your own.

Before God, all are equal. Age is not a criterion for this. Some young children may possess greater wisdom than their elders. That is an attribute of their birth and the quality of their soul. Some are born with all the fortunes but end up unable to achieve any goodness. Born in the house of Kubera (the god of wealth), they turn into vagabonds. Conversely, one born as a vagabond may transform into a Kubera. Why did one become a vagabond? Was it by throwing away everything they had? One must understand that it is due to the inherent quality of their soul. The path to inquire, understand, or take the effort to discover how that soul came to be, and in what form, is not prevalent among us. We simply live reacting to what we see day by day. All the great beings have given indications of this.

Who is the greatest? The gentle ones, or the virtuous (Sathukkal). These virtuous ones praise what they see day by day. Great sages praise what they see day by day - it means they spoke according to the era. Not according to the situation as you assume. What is the era you live in, thinking and making others think about how you should live in that era -- interacting with home, land, and country -- is Karma. Through this long association with the country, a misguided course of Karma has reached our hands. It has happened not just to one or two people, but to everyone. This familiarity has turned into the form of caste, religion, and class, and even God has been divided - thus the God of the Brahmin, the God of the Nair, the God of the Ezhava, the God of the Chandala. Those from Nair downwards are not allowed to chant the Vedas. Then what will become of him? He is a servant of the upper class. He cannot perform rituals directly; he cannot perform pooja. To perform pooja, one must study the Vedas. These are the mistakes that have come in the human condition. How do we change this degraded state?

Some among you living as father, mother, wife, husband, and children may have good fortune. You must learn to safeguard that fortune. You should not handle that fortune in a manner thinking, "Father has made some, I too must make some, I can carry it if I want, or throw it away." Instead of this fortune, what if the father and mother have nothing, they need to be given food, medicine, and clothing, the sisters have all come of age, and there is nothing at all; what would you do if such a situation arises? You have everything, you do not need to go searching and suffering for anything. What should you do in this situation?

How did fortune come about? How did misfortune come about? Most people assume that circumstances brought all this about. Those with knowledge will not understand any of these arguments. If someone who roams around playing and showing off in the streets is caught, bathed, and given good food and clothes, will he stay? So none of this is based on circumstances. All this lies in the part of the mind's knowledge. We do everything based on the knowledge of the mind. The foundation of the mind's knowledge is the course of Karma that has grown old with our home, land, and country. Nothing good will appeal to him who has grown old in this state. The only thing he can enjoy is the ways of the marketplace. Even if a life that has grown old like this is born into a family, he will only show the behavior of the marketplace.

Before we were born, there were crores of years in which our ancestors lived and came into being along with our home and land. It is after that we have come to live for ten or a hundred years. Even in this, several years of childhood lived without knowing anything are gone. Then for some time, we lived taking care of household matters and other things, as a wife, husband, father, and mother. Your fortune was utilized for all these lives. That fortune existed in life as something acquired in the past. This fortune is of a lakh kinds for a lakh people and of a crore natures for a crore people. These differences are innate qualities of birth. This quality is the result of changes that occurred over eras. Through these eras, errors have also occurred.

How can this error be changed? For that, one must perform Karma and acquire merit. But can we do any kind of Karma other than the Karma that is with us? That is, whatever habits and practices exist in the home and the land will be transferred to us as well. There is no good solely for us. Can a court or a police station be set up exclusively for each individual? If you cannot understand the good and bad of all this, the roles of the home and the country will all be transferred together. Thus, the character transferred over eras is what resides in each of you.

So what should we do? We must change from the circumstances in which we were born and raised. We stand on the path of a culture that has continued for generations and has occurred in the home, the land, and the country. We have to struggle a lot if we want to change this path. For that, you must know a human being closely. Incorporating into the character known closely thus, we must establish Dharma through our lives. For that, we need a doctrine. A doctrine suitable for undertaking Karma and acquiring merit. It must be done in whatever way possible by creating conveniences in some way. It must be done not in justice to anyone's word, but in duty to your life.

When you gather with relatives and friends, not everyone may be able to behave according to your wishes. Whether the relatives who come to us are good or bad, we must try to behave with tolerance and bring them along with goodness. If that is not possible, we should let them go. This is the mindset you must have.

Our ancestors lived, worshipped, gave, and received in both good and bad ways many generations before us. A part of all this can be seen in us. How do we discard this aspect? We have inherited numerous karmic paths. Each of us is the residue of the combination of all their truths, illusions, realities, and falsehoods. What we need to understand is how to change this.

The Gurupooja performed here is the pathway to change this. It was mentioned earlier that Gurupooja is performed in numerous places in manifold ways. However, the Gurupooja conducted here is different. In the Trimurti tradition, the foundational stone of the karma that manifested as Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra rests within the deities of worship. Since it is reliant on this foundational stone, performing Gurupooja arbitrarily is insufficient. What is referred to as Gurupooja is neither good nor bad in the manner you presume. This knowledge is unprecedented, not merely in India, but in the entire world.

Islam is a religion that strictly adheres to monotheism. Yet, they too speak of an Imam. That Imam, upon whom karma is established, oversees the karma of the land, the nation, and the world. No one can deny this karmic course represented by the Imam. This karmic path is not something that can be calculated and learned through a single word or a lifetime. Whichever of your ancestors have worshipped this karmic path, retain only the good within that worship and destroy the evil. This foundational action is what is accomplished through the Gurupooja here. The guidance provided here demonstrates what life is, utilizing this goodness and the familiarity you acquire from here. When you strive for this life, the far-reaching afflictions of that karmic path are taken over here. If you are making me take on this karmic affliction, you must carry forward the efforts rooted in goodness for your life until the very end. Otherwise, my suffering will become fruitless. Such an assumption of burdens has never been undertaken by anyone before; nor is it possible for anyone.

There are numerous flaws and afflictions within us. Do not assume that they can be polished away in a single stroke. They can only be transformed gradually, through immense effort. That requires your entire lifetime. This is because elements of the Trimurti tradition and the system categorized as Yogi, Karmi, Bhakta, and Jnani are intermingled in your life. Once the Gurupooja is performed, what you partake in is a karma that encompasses all these elements. Observing how the detrimental aspects of the aforementioned karmas are attached to your life, I am performing the karma that facilitates resolution through yourselves. Unless you embrace that karma with all its love and reverence, I can do nothing.

Have you not understood that salvation lies buried within the realm up to the Trimurti system? In any case, you cannot perform this habitually practiced karma staying ahead of the Brahmin. Learned Brahmins still exist among us today. They are the ones who perform the highest duties in matters of worship. They have done nothing wrong in that regard. Had you not committed deceit, all the properties in the land would still be in their hands today. If they had lied or prepared for confrontation, none of these properties would have come into your hands. There is a reason why this ruin befell them. The karma of that ruin is being taken upon through the Gurupooja here. This is the practical methodology of Santhigiri.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Dedication Edition 2002
The Foundations of Knowledge

The solar system is composed of nine planets akin to the Earth. Each planet has its own dimensions. It is by crossing the Earth, and subsequently traversing four or five other spheres, that one reaches the generative nature of the Moon. Only after reaching there does the journey to the Sun commence. The journey of an ordinary soul is such that it can never attain the solar sphere.

There are many among us who have worshipped the Sun. It is the Sun that sustains the world. Hence, we hold the notion that worshipping the Sun will bestow great powers. However, there is a systematic progression to reach the Sun. There is no justification to reach there other than through the systematic path. One can go there only after reaching the divine presence of Ishwara.

The presences are as follows: Ishwara Sannidhanam (Presence of Ishwara), Daiva Sannidhanam (Presence of God), Brahma Sannidhanam (Presence of Brahma), and Parabrahma Sannidhanam (Presence of the Supreme Brahman). It is not easy for a soul to pass through these presences. It will merely sway beneath them. None of our ancestors have been able to transcend these presences, and their forward journey stands obstructed. It was upon witnessing this obstructed state that the Prophet exclaimed, "O Father, what have you shown me, who believed that there is nothing other than You! What is this power?"

Many souls who traversed the path of Yoga stand in this atmosphere, having fallen from their yogic state. They are Atma-vadins (advocates of the Self). Standing there, they perish while preventing other souls from passing through. Realizing this, we must foster a desire to facilitate liberation for these souls who remain stranded without a way forward. We are capable of granting them liberation. You must comprehend this and convince your children of it as well. Otherwise, they will regress into a merely ordinary life. If these souls are granted liberation, the lineage of our ancestors who worshipped gods and goddesses will attain birth. Or else, these souls will remain stagnated there, devoid of birth and death. Living as a family—father, mother, and children—you must become blessed through your life. Only then will the goodness of your ancestral lineage flow into you. You are unaware of the hardship involved in living and upholding the dignity of a family. The lifestyle of each one of you seems as though it is being eroded by something.

If you continue in that same state, you will not set anything right. What can parents do if the children in the house do not live and reach an absolute level of dignity? If he or she forms a family, what goodness will they bring to that family? They will only be able to experience pain.

I know of souls who have toiled and suffered for generations and across lifetimes in pursuit of goodness. A karma resides within us wherein they are born among us only to end up losing everything. If we are to attain that goodness, we must, as a dharma, provide provisions conducive to the spiritual merit of our ancestors. We can transcend this realm only if we liberate them. Thus, we must strive in a manner that enables us to cross at least the Ishwara Sannidhanam. If this cannot be achieved, there is nothing to be gained by following the path of devotion and embracing asceticism. If the land, the home, and the nation are to reap the goodness borne by children, we must acquire this kind of knowledge. You, as father, mother, and children, must live in a single faith, in the exact same faith, until the end. A life is not solely for earning money. Acquiring money, capability, and wealth alone is of no use. When you, lacking knowledge, acquire money and capability, arrogance, defiance, and a lack of humility will set in, leading you to plunge into actions exhibiting absolute madness.

What I have been saying is this: liberation must be granted not only to our ancestors, but also to whichever deity, sage, or ascetic we have worshipped in the past. Children must understand this extent of the matter, and they must be made to practice it. If, lacking the means to live in our own land, one goes to a foreign land, struggles to earn a few pennies, and goes around flaunting one's stature, one will eventually meet the fate of becoming an empty shell. One must show the children, 'I am the father.' The mother must show the children that this is not merely the father's capability. Then the children wage numerous battles of their own accord. Our lifestyle is such that it creates axes of this kind. This method must be abolished. For that, either a strict governmental regulation must be implemented. Children should be taught only in a specific manner. Anyone who teaches in a manner contrary to that must be punished.

Another thing is that most people educate and raise their children just for the sake of getting a job. Nobody thinks about how many people can actually be given jobs fifteen years from now. No matter how big the government is, will it be able to provide employment to everyone who gets educated in the country? If we look at the current situation unfolding in the country, the education being provided today will leave the children dried up like ginger turning into dry ginger. Eventually, there will be nothing left here even to eat or drink. Only when such a situation arises will everyone learn to look back. Then they will think, why should they be educated at such a huge cost. This realization will come before long. In about thirty years, this situation will become a reality. When today's children reach forty years of age, the rulers will not be able to control the public. In the meantime, if a war, destruction, or looting occurs, there will be massive losses. Or else, a situation will arise where no one can do anything. Why am I saying all this? All people should have some foresight, right?

Here we perform Gurupooja. It brings about a small amount of goodness. But if that goodness is not nurtured properly, you too will join those who are destined to perish. When we get an opportunity to share our love, respect, and abilities, if we are unable to do anything, all the goodness we have earned will be lost. This Gurupooja is about earning the right to share this goodness with children. Therefore, there should be no flaws in the karma you have undertaken. Those who accept and preserve this goodness with love and reverence will have a vision of the Guru at the time of their death. There have been many instances here where people remain alive until the Guru reaches them and they wash the Guru's feet and drink that water.

Not all gurus will come like that. In such cases, it will be a devil that comes in the place of the guru. If it is a yogi or a karmi, they too will be standing in the place of this devil. These yogis and karmis are not entitled to liberation. However, they will stand and watch the washing of the feet being performed for this dying person. With that, these energies that have been wandering for ages will gain the right to be born and will take birth in this lineage of Gurus. Whether they are born or whether they die, it is certain that by the end of this yuga, they will become the masters of the Satya Yuga.

All this that is being said will be quickly understood by those who have performed Guru Pooja. Because they have the experience of seeing many yogis, karmis, jnanis, and bhaktas. Those who have seen this also possess the knowledge that there is only this much in these mentioned powers. It is after seeing like this that they believe this Guru is true. They have the experience and knowledge of this from a small grain of sand of knowledge. They can reach the knowledge of the chitta, a state of transition that stands in the intellect without birth in varna-nature. This is the complete form of darshana (vision). Seven thousand four hundred and forty-four such visions constitute one state. When reaching this one state, the Guru will try to cultivate us into the nature of a visionary. After that, taking each of these visions one by one and determining their weight (value) is an extremely arduous task. This determination of weight begins on the basis of how the karma in the subjects we have known, seen, and heard, and the ideas of our mind stand. In this way, "A person who transcends the limits of the three worlds and swells up need not do any other work." But this lamp, which clears up after the destruction of the triputi (triad), called darshana, will not be attained by a fake ascetic. This is the part we must be very careful about.

The complete nature of the primal karma of our mind has already come into us. What is to come hereafter must be shown to us. We can grow only in accordance with the qualification of the person who shows it. This is why it has been commanded not to proceed without a Guru.

To see the aspect of truth that stands beyond the four states, one must reach the status of the Trimurti. Seeing that aspect, one must reach the realm called Vettaveli (the vast void). When reaching that realm, a Guru is needed to provide guidance from there. If there is no Guru, one will prepare to divide times from the position attained. There are four epochs (yugas), aren't there? Then, if there is no Guru to tell us what the true duration of the Chaturyuga is, we will become nothing in the realm of authority.

This action of weighing a Chaturyuga is beyond thought. This state of consciousness, which swells up crossing the boundaries of the three worlds, must be seen while standing in the Trimurti state. Passing through there and looking upwards again, there lie other vast realms. Along with that, we also see the path we have traversed. We will see the path of any time we have traversed. To determine that time, the person who has seen this must also transcend the Trimurti state. The Trimurtis are the gurus of the time entitled to them. They stand in the subtle. The Guru is the one who breaks open this subtle. The subtle ranges from a grain of sand to the infinite (Akhanda). We must also think whether the infinite itself is only for the world, or whether it exists beyond that too. There are many infinities. What is the path to enter into these infinities? The Guru is that path. Otherwise, one can only go to an infinity and stand bewildered. Here lies the importance of the Guru. This Guru must be someone who has passed through all these infinities. Having experienced it thus, it is not enough to merely understand the endless expanse; the Guru must also be the master of an action accomplished through understanding.
Question - Isn't a life that has attained perfection brought in as a Guru?
Guru - Yes.
Question - Then why repeat "One" while remaining in a human body?

Guru - A soul may be born even as a blade of grass. Evolving progressively, it manifests as all the trees in a vast forest, assuming the nature of trees such as the banyan, mango, eaglewood, and sandalwood, and from there it enters another womb. As each blade of grass and tree completes its respective lifespan, that soul remains in the atmosphere and emerges as something else. Just as a mango sapling sprouts, grows, and spreads its canopy, human beings also sprout, grow, and flourish. We thus witness the karma that acts as the gross, subtle, and causal basis for this expansive evolution.
Question - Is it not after passing through the stages of birds and animals that one is born as a human being? Did everything originate simultaneously?
Guru - First the bird, then the animal. After all that, the human.
Question - Did all these creations come into existence at the same time?
Guru - The history of the same era is being revealed across various time periods. Everything is not revealed simultaneously. If shown in such a manner, errors will occur.
Question - Is Darwin's theory of evolution correct?
Guru - It is correct. It is difficult for those who deny rebirth to accept this.
Question - Darwin does not say that life departed into something else. He says that living beings evolved from one to another.

Guru - That itself is correct. It is our duty to interpret it. With the passage of time, the characteristics of snow, rain, the sun, and darkness will all undergo changes. Only by observing these changing characteristics can one elucidate what lies beyond. Otherwise, it is impossible. It is to explain and impart this understanding that colors are determined. One must interpret it while remaining confined within those colors.
Question - Isn't color external?

Guru - Just as it exists externally, it exists internally as well. Do we not speak of the subtle body? That body exists in the subtle realm. We must observe which color it has attained. Thus, seven colors must be perceived. Then, we must discern the karma that unifies these seven colors. There is a special procedure to retrieve these seven colors from white. By the grace of God, the trajectory of that soul is being imparted. Where, in what all forms, and across what times has such a soul operated—this is another trajectory—the stream of light that penetrates through this is what is termed as the lamp that shines forth upon the dissolution of the triad (*thripudi*).
Question - Will a soul that incarnates with perfection in this very birth perceive all of this?
Guru - It will. It must inevitably perceive it, even if it had witnessed it in all previous births. Because this soul has acquired a new vessel (body), hasn't it?
Question - Does it mean that residing in that vessel, it will repeat everything from the past? If that vessel incurs a flaw, could what was previously correct also go wrong?
Guru - It can go wrong. That is why it is said that even if one reaches the *Brahmaloka*, they will fall downward.
Question - Then, even when the Guru incarnates perfectly and resides in this vessel, is the suffering endured identical to the suffering of ordinary people?
Guru - One must suffer even more than that.
Question - Is there a moment in the Guru's life without suffering?
Guru - How many years has it been since you came to me! In all this time, have you witnessed any comfort in my life?

What is being said is this. If you are told to do this or not to do that, will you understand? Your soul has not traversed to that realm. Therefore, you falter from there. Then, rationality intervenes there. That is how upheaval occurs, leading to ruin. Consequently, a great karma will suffer an untimely demise. This is a very difficult subject. A zero-watt bulb will not provide light during the day, will it? That is, it will burn, but its effect will not be visible in practice. Is there any point in saying that everything is our own handiwork? One's knowledge reaches only as far as the realm in which one operates.

It is here that it was said a mistake has occurred. Do we need to overcome this or not? As far as you are concerned, you have God and Goddess. Why have you not reached the perfection of knowledge and fortune? Is there any household or individual who has reached such a state? Do you possess any karma that aids in reaching at least the presence of God? You cannot proceed beyond the point where your medium of worship culminates. At most, you can reach up to that point.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Dedication Edition 2002
Diverging from conventional ashram concepts...

The majority of those who have come to Santhigiri are communists and Naxalites. However, upon the foundation of faith, all 'isms' and ideologies will fade away. Such is the nature of the experience here. No one should think that this place is merely about renunciation (*sannyasa*). There is a comprehensive way of life here. Or rather, everything except waywardness exists here. Whatever exists here must be imparted to the people of the world, no matter the hardships involved. If you possess the resolve for that, you too become participants in that universal karma.

There are no other karmas here apart from prayer. Through your actions, you can acquire all the goodness and fortune you need. If a renunciate operates, they can deviate from rituals. However, if karma is not carefully guarded, everything will be lost. The vision here is that the ten-time prayer prescribed here must be instilled in every child and thereby reach the people of the world. This is our primordial karma. If fortune is to prevail, one must first pray to God. Subsequently, it is the action for our survival. Following that is the intellect for the survival of the soul. One must cultivate that intellect and reach a state of resolve to develop a personality capable of repeatedly fulfilling the karma of a hundred thousand people. Through this emerges a discipline and order beneficial to the world.

There must be a steadfast sustenance in faith. Our necessity is not to listen to what anyone says. Our necessity is to come to the Guru and know. Along with that, there must be the consciousness to surrender everything unto God. The realm in which we operate today is one that endures across countless *Chaturyugas* and *Manvantaras*. The Guru is bestowed by God as a medium for this. A special attribute must always be ascribed to it. Forgetting distinctions of male, female, big, small, caste, and religion, you must exchange mutual love like the children of one father. If a situation arises in a brother's house where they are unable to marry off a girl, or if a family faces ruin due to a boy's misdeeds, you must be prepared to resolve all such issues.

Never find fault with a renunciate. Even if nothing else, he is someone who has endured a considerable amount of sacrifice. If the renunciate has sacrificed, there will be a perfection in any of his karmas. If an understanding of this is formed, fortune and prosperity will come to your offspring. Stated differently, if the sacrifice of a renunciate is respected, the benefit belongs to the householders.

I heard a lot of abuses, endured them, and suffered pain. Eventually, God brought me to a shore. Although the disciplines and regulations of an ashram are established here, there is a difference in this from the general concepts of an ashram.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Dedication Edition 2002
A New Phenomenon for the World

We are completely unaware of the cause and context behind the advent of the *Trimurti* (Trinity) system in the world. We can never comprehend it through our own cleverness either. The *Trimurti* system is a karmic qualification that all people firmly believe to be divine grace. In such a way that there is no authority for the knowledge of Brahman (*Brahmajnana*), the eminence of the four-faced one (Brahma) ceased to exist on that path. Having spoken of four faces, how it was concealed within three faces has not been understood by anyone so far, nor have there been people qualified to understand it thus far. Sree Narayana Guru opined thus:
The lamp that shines forth upon the dissolution of the triad (*thripudi*)
Cannot be attained by a pseudo-renunciate.

Numerous people came in accordance with the divine decree. That was not possible. This is because we do not know how to conclusively explain what we have heard of as the *Manusmriti*, how it is, or what it is like, nor do we know how to explain in what manner it was eliminated and what was created in its stead.

Many great souls have come at various times. But none of those were appropriate times with conducive circumstances. Liberation cannot be attained except during the advent of a Kaliyuga. This is what is referred to in the *Jnanappana* as 'Kali Shudrankal'. However, we lack this realization. Because, according to the karmic justice that these followers of the Trimurti tradition arrived at by acting upon what they heard, it was completed and stopped with the three faces (Trimukha). A proof for this is Devendra receiving a curse. The story of Gautama states that Devendra, distressed by the curse, suffered the misfortune of being unable to travel where human beings exist. It is also said that Anasuya, the righteous wife of Sage Atri, removed the curse upon Devendra due to the Guru-disciple relationship. Anasuya turned the Trimurtis into infants. When it became impossible to identify these infants, it is added and completed in another way in the story that all three were recognized by praying to Parashakti.

The Trimurti faction has gifted clever storytellers who, whenever a tradition of truth emerges, subordinate it under something else and turn the truth into falsehood using the veil of Maya, calling it Bhagavanmaya or Mahamaya. Due to this affliction, not a single Guru who has come in this era since Sree Krishna has been spared. This is evident from history. What is reconnected to this is the Devendra Pooja held at Suchindram at twelve midnight. Thus, none of our predecessors are inferior in the matter of tying down Maya and fulfilling Dharma.
They have completed writing history in various ways. If one starts talking about it, there will be no end.

Santhigiri has found a way to clarify this. Reaching the shore of that path, standing in a karma that blocked any upward progress, this has been fully known through experience. The only proof for this is a personality who experienced persecution across various times, starting from Varkala Santhigiri. After that personality attained completion by the divine will of Brahman, a karma called Guru Pooja was prescribed from Brahman. However, it is difficult to explain about a householder who has the capacity to recognize this Dharma. The situation is such that not even one person is capable of undertaking that karma. It is the testimony of experience, gained from thousands of families who performed Guru Pooja, speaking, turning, shifting, and acting, that led to such a family description. This is merely one truth of it. Know the rest from Santhigiri. Or else, observe and learn from the believers here. Such is the nature of the realm of Dharma.

The truth of Darshan was of no use to the karmic capability of the Trimurti, which was completed over ten Chaturyugas after the lineage of Manu. It absolutely did not travel beyond the three faces (Trimukha). The history of Sree Krishna and Kamsa is a great tradition brought forth to show us what Kaliyuga Dharma is. We are convinced of the truth that even after bringing this, the downfall of this Dharma could not be altered. To change this situation, I worked here. Then, indicating the fulfillment nature of that remedial karma, a fire broke out in Guruvayur. On the night of the fire, at twelve midnight, it was shown here in a vision. The next day, the fire incident appeared as major news in the papers. A proof of this remedial karma is the intellect and brilliance of children born within a span of twelve years over the past twenty-five years. Parents are indeed experiencing this. Subsequently, this proof is also present among the families performing Guru Pooja here. It is seen without any discrimination of caste, religion, or class. A few isolated householders are able to see in visions how and to what extent the Trimurti tradition exists. This is a secret that is not highly publicized. The children in the ashram who have visions are receiving this more clearly and truthfully. People need to be convinced of this.

It is impossible to verbally convince you of what ideological purity is, based on the notifications received to date. However, believing people are doing it in a manner of dedication to the best of their abilities. In the sense that faith is one, when looking comprehensively at the lineages of prophets and Gurus that have come so far, and the believers who came within those lineages, the order of this notification is not a matter that can be convincingly explained to anyone.

The aspect of Darshan exists in all religious philosophies. In some, it is more, in some less, and in others, it is nominal. However, I have tried for many periods to say that the nature of Darshan is nothing like that. I could not do so back then. Today, since people have developed an interest in this, I am conveying some words to you to make known this ideology and its magnitude. Caste and religion should not be an obstacle to knowing this.

Every religious theoretician uses a different language for the truth of Darshan. You should see this by making a distinction from that. We have been taught by placing knowledge within the path of Siddhi (Siddhimarga). There is evidence spanning a long time for having been taught like this. And it originated from India itself. This ignorance exists in all the deterministic philosophies of India. What is being said here is a part of the path that the people of India have been practicing in their own language to this day. Just because Indians said so does not mean that the truth of Darshan is non-existent or incomplete. It very much exists. It is what is seen and known at Santhigiri; and it is what operates here with the permission of Brahman.

We know that all lineages of gods and goddesses and all lineages of prophets operate in various ways, as if they themselves become prominent. This is also a similar act. However, there is a difference.

How did the deterministic philosophies go wrong? How was the cause for their failure formed? Can the knowledge concerning such cause and effect be obtained by acquiring bookish knowledge? This is said to make you understand at least a little. This is a temporal condition where Indians must take up and actualize all the paths of devotion that have appeared in the world to date. It might seem that we operate as if we do not need these paths of devotion today. But it does not mean they are unwanted. Their time has passed. How should the path of devotion proceed hereafter?

This is what God has bestowed so that the path of devotion becomes clearer to you. How did the Manusmriti operate when it came into the path of creation, where does it stand today, and how did this karma transform into three faces? Any dedication within our knowledge—which confines the four-faced philosophy into three faces and says it is Bhagavan's Maya and that reaching the feet of Bhagavan is sufficient—is inadequate for this. I have understood this through experience.

Do not assume that I am asserting that nothing of the past exists. The expansiveness of Karma and Dharma proves how the Shudra class—who has the responsibility to take up the full rights of the Kaliyuga and operate by paving the way for the deliverance, salvation, and liberation of everything we have worshipped and respected—should reach the Satyayuga.

The karma of Guru Pooja in Santhigiri is the completion, through that path of divine decree, of wherever each of us—not just each of us, but every atom—has operated and stopped. All those who perform Guru Pooja should not only know about this but also sustain it for their children until the final period. Until the final period does not mean until the end of our lifetime. Nor is it until the period in the foresight of the Devas. It is the wealth of experience of fourteen Manvantaras. Regarding the generations to come, Guru Pooja is the karmic purity that sets forth into the Satyayuga after the Kaliyuga. That karmic purity exists. How should it come to us? Once it comes, how can we practice it and pass it on to our children and future generations?

The medium of *Darshana* serves as a means of realization for all prophetic lineages and for all seekers on the path of the Guru. How many *Chaturyugas* and how many solar systems exist within a single *Manvantara*? We must not only firmly establish this in our minds but also be prepared to act upon it. I am imparting this knowledge to the people so that this medium, bestowed by God to help us understand the preparation of the lineage and act accordingly, is not squandered by anyone.

The fourth face succeeds the first three. Under the misconception that Kali signifies destruction, we squandered this fourth phase. This *Brahmashakti* (divine power) is now reclaiming what was lost and revealing it through human beings. *Darshana* is the medium bestowed upon us so that we may honor it and experience not only what has befallen our nation but the entire world—by examining the good and bad deeds of the past. It is an explanatory compilation of the good and the bad. To avoid going astray, one must make corrections through the medium of *Darshana*. I am aware that this generation may not be able to comprehend this entirely. However, for the sake of humanity, I am imparting this knowledge, bearing the responsibility to announce a novel phenomenon among all that has transpired since the inception of the world up to the present day.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Dedication Edition 2002
One Must Know the Yugadharma

For a prolonged period, we have been discussing rebirths and the accumulation of merit across various lifetimes. Concurrently, there are those who question the very existence of rebirths. There is no need to question whether rebirths exist or not. The reason lies in the very existence of the visionary (*Dirghadarshi*). The visionary is capable of foreseeing across vast expanses of time. Consequently, is there any necessity for the question of whether rebirths exist?

The *Karma* (actions/rituals) of the Hindus is anchored in the *Trimurti* system. There is no practice within this path to discover if anything exists beyond it or to act upon such realization. This has been the prevailing situation for a long time. However, prior to the emergence of the Hindu doctrine, the doctrine of the Manu lineage was in existence. Yet, there is a distinct absence of information among Hindus that could aid in understanding what Manu is, what the Manu lineage entails, or what each of us belonging to the Manu lineage truly represents. Apart from scholars and similar individuals discussing the *Manusmriti* and engaging in related storytelling, no one has elucidated what we require from this, having perceived it in the light of time. Nor have they explained what has transpired and passed away in this realm.

The reference to 'epochs' pertains to the *Chaturyugas*—the *Krita*, *Treta*, *Dvapara*, and *Kali* yugas. *Kali* is the final epoch. We have been taught that *Kali* is malevolent and that it paves the way for destruction.

*Kali* should not be regarded trivially. It possesses special attributes and offers a rightful claim to salvation. Our perception that such a *Kali* is detrimental is incorrect.
