How can we alter this misconception regarding *Kali*? How can it be elevated to the level of a doctrine? We have not received any of this knowledge from our ancestors or from Vedic scholars. After all, they can only impart what was useful to them or what they had attained.

We have traversed millions of years. Yet, we only possess a history that extends back to a maximum of 5,000, 6,000, 7,000, or 8,000 years. Can we glean anything from a chronological calculation that relies on the foresight of such a minuscule period? However, according to Hindu calculations, a single *Chaturyuga* encompasses 12,000 divine years. One divine year equates to 365 human years. What did we accomplish, and what did we fail to accomplish during such an extensive *Chaturyuga*? Whom should we ask this? Has any great sage ever elucidated this? Their inability to explain stems from the fact that they attempted to comprehend it while remaining confined within the *Trimurti* system.

Sree Krishna arrived 5,200 years ago. There has never been an incarnation greater than that of Sree Krishna on this earth. By concocting sensational and obscene tales, such a profound figure as Krishna has been obscured behind the *Trimurti* system, rendering it impossible to truly understand him. We remain ignorant of the matters commensurate with his greatness.

The story of Kamsa serves as another prime example of our ignorance. We have been conditioned to believe that Kamsa was wicked. However, Kamsa was not wicked. He merely became stagnant in a situation illuminated by the light of epochs. The author of the Gita asserts that *Dharma* is perceptible. There was a king in the Yadu dynasty who perfectly exemplified how a king should conduct himself. This Yadava belonged to the *Shudra* varna, the fourth among the *Chaturvarnas*. Yet, we have been indoctrinated with a Vedanta that alienates the *Shudra*. This does not refer to the *Shudra* by caste. There are *Shudras* in the households of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas. Similarly, Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas reside in every household. Because we are ignorant about this *Shudra* class and the *Shudra Dharma*, we have consequently become oblivious to the *Kali Dharma*.

Countless great souls have striven to rectify this misfortune. However, because both our ancestors and we lack the knowledge of where we faltered or where mistakes occurred, we have become so lost in the specific actions we perform—segregated as men and women, superior and inferior—that we no longer comprehend the essence of *Dharma*. This loss has escalated beyond anyone's capacity to repair. The reason is that we possess no means to transcend the *Trimurti* system, nor were we prepared to do so. Yet, without transcending the *Trimurti* system, or at the very least attaining the state of being the Lord of the Ganas (*Ganapati*), one cannot lay claim to liberation. We possess absolutely no knowledge regarding the Manu system that enunciates this truth.

This is the era of Vaivasvata Manu. Vaivasvata Manu is the seventh Manu. The current epoch is the *Kali Yuga* of the 28th *Chaturyuga* within the seventh *Manvantara* (Vaivasvata Manvantara). Which path should we adopt—the *Trimurti* system or the Manu system? This is a subject that must be understood by transcending the divides between different classes. Whom shall we inquire of for this purpose? What actions must we undertake?

Except for the fact that our ancestors made various statements and discarded them, no one has anything definitive to offer. Neither the scholar nor the Vedic priest has illuminated anything for us. Consequently, the repercussions of an action that has deteriorated due to these reasons persist in nature. It must be understood that we are incapable of extracting any good from this total catastrophe. You yourselves must reflect upon what you and your children should become through the actions you perform. Are you cognizant of the fact that each of you is paving the way for destruction for your children? Are you not competing to your own detriment by excessively advancing science and technology? This very world is hurtling towards a state where it will be incinerated and destroyed by an atomic deluge. Let us abandon this headlong rush toward annihilation and prepare ourselves to work for a better tomorrow.
We inevitably require a path to comprehend all of this through action. And God Himself must reveal it to us.

The *Dharma* of Kali is beneficial for all classes—Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra. The term 'Brahmin' should not be interpreted to mean one who performs Vedic rituals. It must be understood in the sense of *Brahmajnaneti Brahmana* (one who possesses the knowledge of Brahman is a Brahmin). Discarding the myth that the knowledge of Brahman will not flourish in Kali, we must perceive Kali as a distinct epoch that provides the most opportune time and conducive circumstances to cultivate and achieve it. A righteous path leading to realization within worldly actions must be divinely ordained by Brahman itself.

From the moment the *Dharma* of Kali was rejected, we lost everything that was inherently ours. What remains is solely the Western paradigm. Circumstances unfolded here in such a manner that their system of action prevailed. Although numerous doctrines emerged here through various great souls, we failed to adhere to or sustain any of them.

The truth remains unknown to us. Sree Krishna came to highlight the truth. But not even a single household of ours understood it. Ours became a lineage that failed to understand even after receiving a celestial voice (ashareeri) from the presence of Brahma. Consequently, not only was a lineage destroyed where the idea of liberation should have evolved, but we also lost the true essence of statecraft. The Portuguese, the Dutch, and the Mughals were able to invade us because we failed to grasp true statecraft.

Our ancestors and gurus committed mistakes. We need to know how those mistakes occurred. We must receive a correction for those mistakes from God. Through the favor of time, we have to take up and perform the karma of our ancestors. Can we do that? The magnitude of the ignorance that has devised a situation where the followers of the God of one caste cannot approach the God of another caste is what has destroyed us.

Born and brought up through the *Trimurti* system that has traversed several *Chaturyugas* (four-epoch cycles), we possess an ignorance that renders us incapable of creating anything of our own or sustaining what was once ours. In foreign lands, however, numerous intellectuals and thinkers were born, developed science and technology, and conquered the fields of industry and commerce. But all these previously belonged to Bharath. Why did they not remain Bharath's own? It is because we only know how to sit idly, boasting about the greatness of our ancestors and cultural centers like Nalanda and Takshashila.

Thus, we have sunk in every way. To escape from this situation, what we need is a lifestyle in accordance with the *Yugadharma* (the duty of the epoch). Everyone who came to prescribe a lifestyle according to the *Yugadharma* made mistakes. This is what we must clearly understand. We are drowning in the deception of stories. No matter who does good, they will destroy it. There is an example of this in this very *Chaturyuga*. Mahabali, who ruled the kingdom exceptionally well, was pushed down to the netherworld (*Patala*) by the Lord stepping on his head.
Guruvani

How Far Should One Go to Eliminate the Sense of Duality

It is the *Gurudharma* that has illuminated religious doctrines. People of all religious doctrines stand within the *Gurudharma*. The dharma called Guru, which is capable of enlightening all doctrines, is what is referred to as 'Guru is the soul of all dharmas' (*Guru sakaladharmatma*). That is, if one observes this Guru closely, it can be seen that all gods, goddesses, acharyas, and prophets who have appeared so far merge into this Guru. There is no other justification for this. If this is the spiritual merit of that Guru, it is meant to be attained by the disciple. However, all disciples may not receive it. Only the destined disciple will receive it. Destiny is written at the very time of birth.

In the world, origination occurs according to the course of karma. The doctrine of destiny is the doctrine of the time of origination. Householders (*Grihasthashramis*) must act with the knowledge of this doctrine. Then they will have the origination of good progeny. Those children will be valiant in action and virtuous souls qualified to rule the country. That is how any karma gains power. But we have not been trained in any of this. We, on the other hand, are stubborn that we will not practice any of this.

As a characteristic of the *Yugadharma*, a karma has been introduced that allows even a *Chandala* (outcast) to rule. Just because a *Chandala* rules the country, no one can step aside, can they? This is how God inflicts punishment. Since they cannot be kept away by citing caste, bring about absolute freedom and make this very *Chandala* rule. When the divine resolve is such, is there a need to lose oneself by preaching, familiarizing, and getting accustomed to doctrines that lack even a shadow of truth?

The dharma of Kali (*Kaliyuga*) is the same for the Brahmin, the Kshatriya, the Vaishya, and the Shudra. But here, the Shudra has come in eighty-four castes with eighty-four types of karma. If the Shudra is alienated by creating castes in this manner, the dharma of Kali will be endangered.

Everything has gone wrong here because *Gurudharma* was denied in the name of *Vaidikadharma*. The mistake of behaving in an unconscious state, with dharma obscured without knowing the glory of *Pravachakadharma* (prophetic dharma), exists here. The masterminds behind this ignorance are trying to escape by performing mantras and tantras.

This is my experience. I had the experience even when I was a very small child. I understood how to realize the experience through an experienced Guru. Initially, I traveled through the path of Advaita. However, that path did not help me reach the state of realization.

What is realization? Vision (*Darshana*)! Vision in the states of wakefulness (*Jagrat*), dream (*Swapna*), and deep sleep (*Sushupti*). Later, it becomes transcendent (*Lokatheetham*). What is meant by transcendent? As meditation and chanting continue, one can see the light of life without even realizing it. Then it will see in whatever ways it lived in this world, and whatever forms of skies exist. After seeing that, one will see one's Guru and oneself. This will be seen without any gender difference. After that, the followed *Acharyamarga* (path of the teacher) or *Devamarga* (divine path) will be revealed. This is the truth of the vision. After seeing all this, one will automatically reach a speaking state. Once the speaking state is reached, doubts can be cleared. This is the manifestly evident dharma (*Prathyakshavaham dharma*). The essence of truth that stands manifest and imparts knowledge through words is God. One who reaches up to the form of sound is a Vedantin. The convergence of such a Vedantin and a prophet is the door to God. Knowing this, one should surrender and work under a Guru. This is the only way to eliminate the sense of duality.

Mistakes can happen even if one acts with a complete understanding of the essence of truth that is tangibly expressed. Because when one believes in a prophet or a Guru, by taking refuge in them, one is reaching God. As the disciple advances a little further, they feel that they and the Guru are not different. This feeling will pave the way to the soul of truth. Then, even the variations in the journey of life can be seen. The journey of the soul, seen in wakefulness, dream, and deep sleep, and setting out into the *Turiya* state by experiencing wakeful-deep sleep (*Jagrat-sushupti*), is the same for everyone. Thus, the Guru, who is the essence of truth residing within the bliss of the soul, encompasses countless formless skies. Whether one is a sectarian, a follower of the prophetic path, or a follower of the Guru's path, doubts may arise for those who believe that God is one.

Once one believes in the truth called Guru, mistakes can occur even if one lacks the realization of what must be observed and known. This is the mistake that happens when a blemish (doubt) appears in faith. Such people are ignorant of what the path of the Guru is. If faith remains unblemished, one will not care about any circumstances. Wife, husband, children, wealth, education, or lordship—none of these will matter. The doctrinal ignorance that has existed in one's family to date must be dispelled. What one needs is an action to reclaim doctrinal knowledge through love, respect, and humility. This is the only requirement for a disciple. This is the ideal model of *Grihasthashrama* (householder's life). Such a householder does not need caste or religion. Nor do they need knowledge belonging to any sense of justice within the human system. They will not become alien by gaining strength in the ignorance that divides people. This is the magnitude of the statement that the Guru and the disciple are not different, but one. In the end, when there is no one to accompany you, only that truth comes along. I have come to speak this truth. I have not come to preach any particular guise of any doctrine. If anyone says so, I will not accept it either. Seeing your rights and wrongs, I have come to help you rectify your mistakes in any way possible, if you are capable of doing so.

You must know the Guru in this manner. Otherwise, as indicated earlier, mistakes will occur. There might be difficulty even in spending anything in the name of the Guru. That difficulty will cease only when the aspect of what the Guru is, is known.
An example:

This is the history of a great aristocratic family. This lord was someone who lived according to the Guru's principles. History has fabricated that he cleverly left his house for that reason. He didn't leave cleverly like that. He was a follower of the Guru's path. His own Guru told him, "You have everything, but a situation will arise where your children will be of no use." What should be done when the children have no destiny? Perform karma. All karmas can be performed. He often asked his wife, "What will you do after I am gone?" "I will become a beggar. Therefore, I will also die with you." (It is a matrilineal system, after all.) "Alright, let it be so." He decided to test this. Approaching Bhartrihari,

Ashram: The Place That Gives the Knowledge of Experience

We hold an understanding of the ashram as it existed in the Treta Yuga or beyond. However, that is not how one should perceive the ashram. The nature of the ashram must evolve according to the Yugadharma (the duty of the age). Until today, we have had no knowledge regarding this matter. No one has clearly informed us about it, nor have we known it.

The purpose of the ashram is to create an opportunity to perform the karma destined for each yuga in a manner that benefits the land, the nation, and the world. The ashram is not merely meant for sanyasa (renunciation). This does not mean sanyasa is absent. It is there; there can be sanyasis and brahmacharis. There can also be vanaprastha sanyasa. It can also serve the purpose of fulfilling the faith of those who do not fall into any of these categories.

What should we understand by terms like brahmacharya, vanaprastha, and sanyasa? We have ancestral Gurus who were born in different yugas and otherwise. If we consider a single yuga itself, they functioned in five different ways. A Yugadharma is accomplished based on the information provided by Gurus possessing five distinct natures. Among these five Gurus, there is a Guru who appears at the beginning of the yuga and another who appears at the end. The great soul who emerges at the intersection of the end of one yuga and the onset of another will be the one arriving as the Yugadhikari (Authority of the Yuga) during that period. The notion that an ashram is simply a place to sit around, chant, and breathe one's last without knowing any of this is incorrect. Those who harbor such erroneous knowledge are not the ones who should come to the ashram.

The vasanas (latent tendencies) that have been worshipped and perpetuated across multiple lifetimes must be severed. Only the great soul who arrives at this yugasandhi (junction of ages) can prescribe the karma necessary to sever these vasanas. All the events that transpired in the first three yugas of a chaturyuga (cycle of four ages) must also manifest in Kali, the dharma of the fourth yuga.

What is it that we need to comprehend in detail about the Kali Yuga? We have heard that Kali is evil. Such statements were made because matters were explained by highlighting individual flaws. Among the yugadharmas, Kalidharma is the most superior. The dharma of Kali is to evaluate the good and bad deeds performed thus far, to discern if there is any divine will beyond that, and to determine our course of action in accordance with that divine will—evaluating the virtues and vices of all these aspects.

Many great souls may emerge in Kali. Numerous great souls may have appeared in the preceding yugas as well. Beyond all this, the dharma of Kali entails recognizing the mistakes committed through one's own life and the lives of ancestral great souls, and understanding how to establish the system of worship and other requisite karmas in alignment with the Yugadharma. The ashram is not a place to behave basely, as misconceived by some who lack this knowledge, nor is it a place to retreat to and squander one's life when rejected by family and society. Such individuals will not adhere to the ashram, its discipline, or its teachings. They will lack the capability to function in that manner. Such people will only propagate evil among others and will never perform good deeds. Whether male or female, for every single virtue they possess, they will harbor ten vices; for a thousand virtues, they will sow ten thousand seeds of destruction.

For a long time, God has desired to reveal that this is not the dharma of Kali, or to seek the absolution of this world's sins. Who are we within the dharma dictated by that desire? Kali is the era equipped with the facility to process the numerous experiences embedded in the karmas associated with our many lifetimes, allowing us to realize the essence of our soul. The ashram is the arena designed to put such a dharma of Kali into practice. The ashram is not a venue meant for adhering to the dharmas of the Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga.

It is during our period of education that the most optimal method is desired. Because an individual has numerous tasks to accomplish, certain events have transpired in their life, specific occurrences have taken place in the lives of their ancestors, and from all of these, a destined karma has emerged. The period of education is the phase granted to rectify those mistakes and to render service by understanding what can be optimally prepared not only for the family but also for the land and the nation. However, what develops within us is the karmic capacity envisioned by the ancestors, devas, and rishis, which has assimilated the good and bad deeds of our forefathers. This is the most significant issue afflicting us. It is not the karmic trajectory or vasana of today or yesterday that burdens us. Regarding service, all of this can be executed consciously, knowingly, or unknowingly. What is implied here is—there is no role here for the scholar's literal interpretations, the layman's foolish interpretations, or the individuals who seek such things.

What all has been enacted in the Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga; how many Satya Yugas, Treta Yugas, and Dvapara Yugas have thus elapsed; and how much karma has been resolved through these yugas. The karma into which we are currently born and raised is the absolute accumulation of the preceding yugadharmas. What is the utility of pursuing education without the requisite knowledge to comprehend all this? Today, college education and the education beyond it are mere facets of a culture forcefully imposed from elsewhere.

It is indeed beneficial to adopt an ashram-like nature and its corresponding mindset. However, the karmic accumulation of the Kali Yuga cannot necessarily be comprehended through that alone. The Kali Yuga is a truth to which the scholar and the layman, the knowledgeable and the ignorant, and individuals of any caste, religion, or class hold an equal claim without any prejudice. But instead of preparing to operationalize it, our family members and local community dismiss it with contempt, relying on obsolete knowledge they have merely heard. They do not even pause to consider what enhancement this contempt will bring to our lives.

I am conveying certain matters to you based on what has been revealed to us here (at Santhigiri) through divine visions. This has been iterated many times in the past. Yet, I have not been able to convince myself thus far that anyone has truly paid heed to it. Having established this space as an ashram, undertaking only what is strictly essential for life, and dedicating the entirety of the remaining time towards fulfilling the dharma of Kali, we are currently in the process of learning from the most fundamental aspects onwards. Among those engaged in such learning, there are also individuals who find themselves incapable of fulfilling it.

We do not see here an inheritance that our predecessors have diligently cultivated and handed down to us with complete love and respect regarding any aspect of karma. It is not merely the duty of a Brahmana or a Kshatriya; they are also unaware that Kali is the era where the Vaisya and the Sudra must advance in karma by joining hands together. Therefore, they will not change their mercantile nature either. Today, humans have a tendency to manipulate any situation to justify immoral actions. However, that is not what we should desire. By examining the paths through which the humans, deities, and sages of the present and the past eras acquired knowledge, our focus today should be on what needs to be done to acquire knowledge now, how long our health will permit it, how we should live until old age, how we have been advised to act practically, and how much of that advice we have been able to assimilate. Instead, what can we achieve by fabricating, modifying, and arbitrarily renaming old customs? We are born in an era where nothing can be achieved through such fabrications. However, this is an era where everything is attainable.

Today, what is predominantly seen are ashramas functioning according to the dharma of bygone eras. They continue the rituals based on those traditions. We must have the knowledge of the virtues in them. Otherwise, we will face the misfortune of standing bewildered even before our own children. The widespread rituals of today heavily incorporate the aspects of mantra, tantra, and yantra strictly according to the Vedic religion. However, they hold no place in the dharma of the Kali era.

One must reside in an ashrama to attain the fruitful realization of undertaking and performing the duties of a grihasthashrami (householder), an aspiring seeker of knowledge, and an aspirant of wealth. However, without a purpose, it will not lead to purity of intention. Nor will it bear any result. If one resides in an ashrama without knowing any of this, with a mind wandering and becoming corrupt, they gain nothing but the unloading and distribution of the accumulated impurities of countless past lives. Many venture here to gain familiarity with this old habit. The logic they use for this is the phrase, 'The great sages praise what they see day by day.'

The great sages praised what they saw day by day. However, this is not what the great sages truly saw. This is merely a literal interpretation. One should not look at this karmic progression that has been exaggerated through mere wordplay. Then what? Concerning ourselves, one must ask: Why was I born? Why did I grow? Why should I continue to live? Many things have intruded into my life, which has been caught in the cycle of birth, death, rebirth, and death. I have accepted this karma (the body) to eliminate this from myself. How many of us possess the ability to reflect upon this?

There are also those who act by only seeing right and wrong. It is referred to as four generations. That is not merely a calculation of human generations. It implies four generations corresponding to a yuga. That will subsequently align with the calculation of the Chatur Yugas (four eras). This is an experience. Just because an experience occurred, it does not mean it is understood. The experience must have primarily occurred at the beginning. This is not something that resides in the scientific consciousness of either the scholar or the ignorant. If one habituates oneself to actions driven by foolishness, it will result in karmic flaws. What is being described is the path of knowledge that serves as experiential evidence.

There might be experiences of the Treta Yuga and the Dwapara Yuga. One might have passed through the Satya Yuga as well. In the Satya Yuga, one only speaks and acts truthfully. Therefore, the action is truthful. The action in the Kali Yuga is also the same. But the karma of the Kali Yuga is not like that of the Satya Yuga. One must cultivate a determination to inquire how dharma is sustained when karmas are exhausted without rejecting the dharmas that came and went in other yugas, what is required for it, and what is not. Past gurus have worked tirelessly for this. However, we have strayed from all those paths. No one knows what our present requirement is. The brahmachari, the householder, and the sanyasi do not know. This is because we have not received that knowledge from the temples and the ashramas.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarppanappathippu 2002
The Mistake That Imprisoned Humanity

Most people among us will ask, 'Is he a Siddha?' Unknowingly, the actual question is whether he is a Jnani (a realized soul). A Siddha cannot be a Jnani. However, this is how we have understood it. We must recognize that we have been fundamentally wrong here.

Ours is a tradition that has functioned for a long time through deities, goddesses, sages, ascetics, the wise, and devotees. They must have done various things in accordance with their times. It is not that those times did not exist; we must respect those periods that existed. But how did a situation of disrespect arise? We should at least possess an interest in knowing this.

Islam will claim that it operates in the best manner. The Hindu, the Jain, the Buddhist, and the Sikh will also say the exact same thing. Which of these is correct? Christianity has already divided into numerous denominations. Therefore, what we require is a foundation that unifies all of this.
Seeker: Aren't our land and our culture the most important?
Guru: What has our culture become entangled in, and where does it
stand? We must understand this.
Seeker: We can only know this if knowledgeable people tell
us.
Guru: I am not a highly educated person. I am someone who grew up
as a simple man.
Seeker: All our ancestors were exactly like that.
Guru: There is a concept called the Chatur Yuga. Within the Chatur Yuga, it is said that this is Kali.
Most people assume that Kali is bad. A few people have stated that Kali is not bad. But we do not accept that.
Seeker: Generally, it is indeed said that Kali is bad. Saturn is also
said to be bad. But it is also said that the period of Saturn is good.
Guru: Yes. It becomes good only in accordance with that aspect. For someone whose Jupiter is favorable,

Saturn will not be favorable. Similarly, there is goodness in zodiac signs and mandalas. Everything has its own inherent goodness. No matter how modern our actions are or what we do, we can only operate within the twenty-seven stars, twelve zodiac signs, and nine planets. Even then, we must surely know what the mistake is and where it lies.
Seeker: Whatever the mistake is, it must be known; and the truth must be understood as well.
Guru: Mahatmas are mostly brought forth by being classified

as avatars. Even Buddha has been classified as an avatar. But is that the truth? We have no certainty about what this actually is. That is why it has come to this. Had there been any certainty, we would have held onto it.

Our ancestors might have done the right things in many ways, and they might have done wrong as well. Explaining it will not bring it to an end. We must move to the position where it needs to be put into practice. We cannot say that nothing was done. If we are to say nothing exists, we must explain what existed beyond it. One should not speak otherwise. Anyone can provide the information that something does or does not exist. If we have the belief, love, and respect that it does exist, how should we handle it? That requires a foundation. Our goal and achievement, which have been established as a foundation, reach up to the position of the Trimurti or Parashakti. We have believed and revered a system of worship that fosters such a nature. Has anyone ever heard someone say that there is a mistake in this?
Seeker: Right and wrong are based on their respective perspectives.
What is wrong to some might appear right to others.
Guru: Do you believe that there is a concept called Yuga Dharma?
Seeker: The concept of Yuga Dharma exists.
Guru: Then how will the concepts of the Treta and Dwapara yugas
be fulfilled in Kali?
Seeker: As the yugas change, the concepts also change. According to the respective
times' requirements, those concepts must be
fulfilled.
Guru: Yes. But just because we say it should change, it will not

change on its own. Sree Krishna is the one who has risen to the position of a perfect *Jnani* (wise one) among all those who have come thus far. A *Jnani* by birth. However, we did not respect that. Knowledge regarding His arrival was provided even prior to Sree Krishna's birth. But with that knowledge, Kamsa merely killed the seven children born before Sree Krishna. Sree Krishna has been relegated to this state. How are we to interpret this? Can it be resolved by merely reiterating the actions of the Treta Yuga? Do you believe the statement that 'Kali resides in the Shudra' is true?
Seeker: I do believe it. Swami Vivekananda also stated that this is the epoch of the Shudra
(*Shudra Yuga*).
Guru: Yes. He stated what he perceived. When it was termed as the epoch of the Shudra,

what did we comprehend? If it belongs to the Shudra, shouldn't the Shudra assume it? A Shudra essentially means one devoid of *Brahmajnana* (knowledge of the Brahman). Anyone lacking *Brahmajnana* is indeed a Shudra. Everyone is currently situated in a *dharma* where they remain inactive, whether they are entangled in that Shudra *karma* or not. There is no distinction here regarding a specific sect, Hindus alone, or followers of other religions.
Seeker: Sree Narayana Guru Swami did say that humanity should improve itself, didn't he?
Guru: We have been saying that since the very beginning. 'One caste, one lineage,

one God' has been proclaimed even prior to that! However, how can it be realized? Sree Narayana Guru Swami has also stated thus: 'The lamp that shines forth upon the dissolution of the *Tripudi* (the triad of knower, knowledge, and known) shall never fall into the hands of a hypocritical ascetic.'

All of this is true. Our lifespan is, at most, a hundred years. We are engaged in actions throughout this entire period. There is a value to that as well. How do we elevate that value towards self-realization? However, the knowledge we possess is merely in accordance with our individual inherent tendencies (*vasanas*) and origins. When limited to that knowledge, we become utterly insignificant with respect to true realization.
Seeker: What is the remedy for this? Just as medicine is the treatment
for a disease, what is the antidote to our current state of degradation?
Guru: The degradation is not confined to India alone; it afflicts the entire world. When considering the world

as a whole, we must assume that India has not suffered such a severe degree of degradation. All other nations have gone egregiously astray. It would be more accurate to say that the error is absolute. It is impossible to rectify matters while remaining stagnant in this condition. This is because the fundamental error lies elsewhere.
Seeker: Where did that fundamental error originate?
Guru: What currently exists is the twenty-eighth
*Chaturyuga* within the *Vaivasvata Manvantara*. Every *Chaturyuga* possesses a Kali Yuga, doesn't it? Therefore,
the fact that the *dharma* which emerged in each yuga was not imparted to us is
the root cause of this error.
Seeker: Who was supposed to impart this? Does it mean we should approach the *Jnanis* (wise men) and *Vijnanis*
(scholars)?
Guru: That is insufficient. What is the use if one, two, or even a hundred of us go and acquire this

knowledge? It must originate from the very source it is meant to come from. Let me cite an example. Suppose one group wages a war against us, drives us away, and confines us to a specific location. Then, another group drives us away from there and abandons us elsewhere. Thus, we are chased hither and thither and discarded. What we require now is the knowledge of what we ought to do in this situation.
Seeker: It is precisely for that knowledge that we are wandering in search.
Guru: Do not assume that I arrived with the knowledge of all these matters. I do not even

possess the knowledge gained through reading. However, I shall recount my personal experience. I must share it. I harboured a deep desire for a spiritual life. For that purpose, I first went to Kalady. At that time, only a conventional schooling system existed there. There was no tradition of taking in disciples and imparting spiritual education. Therefore, I walked from there and reached the Advaita Ashrama in Aluva. Although the Secretary initially refused, the then head of the Sivagiri Mutt, Swami Sankarananda, intervened and allowed me to stay. My ashram life commenced there. Two years passed there. Subsequently, I was summoned to Sivagiri. I worked across various branches of Sivagiri and did everything I knew. I realized that it was impossible to survive there without aligning with one faction or another. I could not take sides in such factionalism. I treated everyone equally. But that was not enough for them. During that period, a receiver was appointed for a legal case concerning Sivagiri, involving a person named Nijanandan who was the Secretary at that time. The receiver's authority was granted to Swami Sankarananda. Exercising that power through a power of attorney, I was transferred to another location for two years. I went there, spent two years, and returned. In total, I spent about eighteen years in Sivagiri and its branches. Yet, the factionalism among them remained unchanged. That division began to affect me. Some individuals convened a committee and instructed me to go on a pilgrimage and return. Their opinion was that I lacked an understanding of renunciation (*tyaga*). I replied: 'I can undertake a journey, but will renunciation dawn upon me simply by following someone else's orders? Furthermore, you possess the authority to ask me to leave.' Then they said I could do as I pleased. I responded: 'Alright, you must provide me with food for three more days. After that, I shall depart.'

After three days, I built a hut in the compound belonging to Varkala Gangadharan Muthalali. I stayed there for seven years and four months. During that time, a sense of degradation overcame me. I did not know the reason for it. I experienced this on several occasions. Later, an inner intimation directed me not to reside in places where two people are seen together. That is how I came to Pothencode. There was absolutely nothing here in those days. When this same Gangadharan Muthalali purchased this land in Pothencode, he had set aside half an acre of land for some purpose. It was his son, Advocate Pushpangadan, who had set this land aside, perhaps in the name of his mother or father. They bestowed that land upon me. I erected a small shed-like structure here. Various people would come and light lamps there. Upon arriving here from Varkala, I received an inner calling to maintain absolute silence for five years. I adhered to it. After five years, I received the intimation that I was free to do as I pleased.

I am merely narrating matters from my own experience. I possess no scholarly or Vedantic knowledge. Just as they speak of visions manifesting, I began to perceive things within the operational states of *Jagrat* (waking), *Swapna* (dreaming), *Sushupti* (deep sleep), *Turiya* (the fourth state), and *Turiyatita* (beyond the fourth). This is elucidated in terms of the Trinity (*Trimurti*) forms and their lineages. Even when speaking of Lord Subrahmanya, apart from standing slightly apart from the Trinity form, it inherently belongs to the Trinity aspect. Subrahmanya represents the sixth state. He is, after all, referred to as *Arumukhan* (the six-faced one). That is, an individual turned towards six directions. We have the traditional knowledge that when *Arumukhan* asked for the meaning of the *Omkara* (the syllable Om) and Brahma was unable to answer, Brahma's fourth head was plucked off. We do refer to him as *Nanmukhan* (the four-faced one)—representing the face of wisdom.

The doctrine of *Nanmukhan* essentially denotes the authority of Kali Yuga. The other yugas are Satya Yuga, Treta Yuga, and Dvapara Yuga. To say that there is no four-faced one implies that there is no Kali Yuga. Such a narrative has been fabricated to deceive us. Among Brahma, Vishnu, and Maheshwara, it is said concerning Brahma that the fourth face is absent. That is, the face of true wisdom is missing. It was plucked off. Because he did not know the meaning of the *Omkara*, the fourth face was severed.

This is the very subject I wish to convey to you. Some among you are doing commendable work. I am pleased about that. However, I am also aware that this effort is inadequate. That knowledge refers to a trajectory of action (*karmagati*) which even the Trinity cannot achieve—and it exists here. That supreme knowledge is Sree Krishna. Even prior to Sree Krishna's advent, knowledge of that arrival was disseminated. We were unable to retain Sree Krishna here. Although there are accounts of various wars, we drove Sree Krishna away to the extent that He had no opportunity to remain in India. He was driven away by the monarchs of that era themselves. There is a history to that. It is said that having been forced to flee, He reached another shore and constructed Dwaraka there. That city was subsequently submerged in the ocean. Evidence of this can still be observed today.
Seeker: It is understood that the Kali Yuga commenced following the era of Sree Krishna.
Guru: That is merely how it is stated. The presiding authority over the *dharma* of Kali is Sree Kri...

shnan. We have been made to believe that position is bad. Nobody has been able to know Srikrishnan from the knowledge of any science. Because he doesn't yield like that, they have just said maya, mahamaya, bhagavan's maya and so on. Will the dharma of kali change if it is said so? We must understand what happened to our moral karma in this condition. Dharma has to be understood through the paths of devotion, yoga, karma, and jnanam. Then the knowledge that came as a devotee, yogi, jnani, and karmi cannot be carried without a body. Therefore there is a body. We must have a moral sense to know what the movements of jivan are within that body. Whether it is through devotion, karma, yoga, or jnanam, it is the dharma of kali itself. This is the reason why it cannot be accepted if kali is said to be bad. Can we think of a karmic method like the one existing today some time ago?

This karmic method is meant to come somehow. Nobody has plucked it off. Nor will it go like that. This is my experience. That is, the knowledge acquired through the system of shakteyam, shaivam, vaishnavam or brahma, vishnu, shiva and the knowledge that has come through the puranas and itihasas included in it and the knowledge mentioned in the vedas. It is not necessary to think about such a subject. That dharma which is the authority of the veda is beyond thought and like the sky. It is to be known how that dharma exists in the present time in the karma called sthulam, sukshmam, karanam, karyam. There is no point in talking about what has passed. That matter cannot be found and brought from anywhere. Because some basic mistake has happened in the dharma that has come till today. If that mistake is not removed and the people are not led, the people will always be in prison. This is my idea. I will only talk about this.

As stated earlier, the current time is the kali yuga of the twenty-eighth chatur yuga of the vaivasvata manvantara. When we say manusmriti, we should not see it as a small book that exists today. The whole human race has come as a lineage of manu. Even the word manushyan has come from manu. This manushyan has a karmic path of kali to become clear as a deva, rishi, sanyasi, bhaktan, and jnani. But the face of knowledge of kali dharma has disappeared. That is why kali is said to be destruction.

Manu dharma happened only in three chatur yugas out of twenty-eight chatur yugas. Three chatur yugas in the remaining twenty-five chatur yugas went in vain. Because it was assumed that there is nothing that man cannot achieve. That is the reason for the mistake. As long as this is not understood, we will not be able to understand anything. Kali destruction is said from the clarity only up to the trimurti state. When coming to the dharma of kali in the four periods, everything is cleared and changed to jnanam and going to satya yuga. To reach the subject of satya yuga, the dharma of kali must have happened. That is the reason for saying kali shudrangal. Regarding the shudra, the human being must get the knowledge to handle a karma that helps for mukti or jnanam by completing the dharma in the fourth quarter. This knowledge is beyond religious theory. God has brought us to this much part of knowledge.
Guru Vani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarpana Pathippu 2002
The Secret of Life and the Reality of Karmic Form

Those who believe in Santhigiri will understand the secret of human life, reality, karmic secret, and the reality of karmic form. If the word is kept without fail, the karmic path will be pure. This society doesn't have the nature of seeking to know and respect anything. Generations will be needed to change this nature. If even a fraction of the purpose and objective here is acted upon, it will get the fruit of a great sacrifice.

To be able to respect the will of God, one must have glory. The desire of a complete guru is to make everyone good. One must be able to obey what the guru says with a sense of duty. The dialogue between krishnan and arjunan is an example of that.

You must have a guarantee that you will change the perversions in the world. Nobody has complete knowledge about hindu culture. Some have an impression that they have general knowledge. But that knowledge cannot be applied anywhere. That is why they cannot accept and respect anything. Those who came from the land covered with ice blocks and where the brightness had dimmed ruled us. Due to the ignorant people who were here, the past few generations went wrong. There were a few devotees and sanyasis here who thought about the future and generations of this land. Along with that, there were also a few people here who shouted and laughed seeing all this. Whom is our inclination to accept among them? This is also the reason why nobody understands the things happening in this ashram. When there was an intimation from God to do the prayer happening here, I didn't understand then that there was such a big purpose behind it. Only after understanding the vision of fifty people by asking, I started understanding the weight of this. The vision of each one is in a different way--according to the broadness of their own mind. When all these were evaluated together, I understood that God is standing and watching with pleasure by making a group of ignorant people who are like machines to implement the world justice completely. If you take such a big thing without giving respect, there will be danger. There is no other thing as dangerous as this. Every child who gets an opportunity to stay here is obliged to protect this even by sacrificing their life. If they don't show that love and sincerity, its destruction will happen by them itself.

The perversion existing in the world must completely destroy. You must have the ability to dig a channel for this perversion to be trampled and flowed away. Each sankalpam made here goes to the respective rasis and changes the meannesses firmly rooted there. The meannesses in the subtle are also changed by the power of sankalpam itself. This process takes place in the nine planets, twelve rasis, and twenty-seven nakshatras. All that is changed in this way is falling on the earth, like the dust particles of the moon falling on the earth. If it continues like what is happening in this atmosphere, you cannot even think of the danger that is going to happen to the earth in the future. Only the one with eyes can see.

You don't have any knowledge about the guru parampara. Some of their contemporaries did some acts fearing the siddhas. But it is not like that here. You have an opportunity here to do it with a full mind and love. Whatever changes are made in the atmosphere, for that change to be useful for the people, you must act. The karma you do should be held in the atmosphere and return as the nature of prakriti.

Until recently, there were daridra narayanans who worked for the lord, got the result, and submissively said that this is your rice. Such people still exist in some places. But there is also another side to it today. We must understand that even the incidents of slaughtering these lords are happening from prakriti. For every karma, there is a reaction. Every karma is worn in prakriti. The lotus grows in mud. Nothing else will be formed from the pure. It will only dissolve away. It cannot be taken and applied. This is the special creation since the beginning of the world.

The epochs are in a state of continuous transition. The masses lack the profound wisdom required to adapt in tandem with this epochal shift. Consequently, some form of natural cataclysm is bound to occur. It is only in the aftermath of such events that this concept is brought to the forefront. One faction asserts that liberation from the shackles of caste will resolve everything; another contends that the Trimurti system is ideal; yet another group proclaims that the ultimate truth resides exclusively within the confines of their own religion.

As far as we are concerned, we possess the certainty of direct experience. As our chanting of the holy name reverberates, the ensuing spiritual resolve will incinerate all the baseness that lingers within the subtle forces of the universe. It is the divine will that this task be executed by a group of simple-minded people who are incapable of comprehending its profound value. To sever the tuft of the Trimurti system, which acts as the feudal lord in the spiritual realm, a revolutionary force akin to the Naxalbari movement must inevitably awaken in alignment with the ideology of the Guru lineage. You must never corrupt this by applying your own intellect and cunning at any point in time. This is an arena where even the Buddha and Sri Shankara laboured and ultimately faltered. Your sole contemplation should be on how to act while remaining absorbed in that ultimate dissolution of whatever is perceived. These great souls were those who performed austerities, bathing in the snow-fed, flowing Ganges at four in the morning, chanting with intense spiritual agony. From the exalted position where that sacrifice devolved into mantras and tantras and was solidified through penance, one must descend by operating solely with the karmic capacity of an ordinary human being. Only through such a descent will true order be established.

The word of the discoverer is logic. There must be someone to actualize that word with utmost sincerity. This is because it has been corrupted through action (*karma*). Therefore, it must be purified through action itself. The scoundrel has erred through the scoundrel, the yogi through the yogi, and the ascetic through the ascetic. Rectifying this is no easy endeavor. If the action is not executed with absolute tranquility, it will inevitably go astray. This is a subject that eludes the grasp of any scientist.

As stated earlier, our primary asset is our experience. The inception will be arduous. The difficulty will fluctuate in proportion to the degree of sincerity. Even during prayer, the initial experience is often one of distress. There may even be times when one feels an aversion to praying. Then, interest resurfaces, followed by another phase of dullness. That is its nature. Just as one does not desire to consume the exact same food every day, a yearning for variation in prayer will also arise. The perversions carried over from one's own past lives are the root cause of this. No religious adherents speak of this, because their depth extends only up to the status of the deities. The Quran discusses liberation to a certain extent, but it is not exhaustive. This is because no religion possesses a prehistory and antiquity that spans the duration of the epochs. The Bible recounts merely six thousand years of history. These are insufficient to penetrate the profound secrets of human existence and the ultimate reality of karmic forms. The realm of absolute knowledge is located far, far beyond all of these. In that realm, there are no artificial fabrications. There is no tuft, no purdah, and no other external masquerades.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Dedication Edition 2002
Life Devoid of Self-Discipline

Every household of ours possesses a certain shrewdness. The land itself possesses that shrewdness. However, each of these forms of shrewdness has its own inherent flaws. In southern Travancore, there are certain ruffians. The lineage in the households of these ruffians invariably stands on the side of a particular kind of ignorance. A specific type of ignorance, characterized by boastful arrogance, has developed among everyone. They may have acquired wealth, employment, and capabilities, but adverse consequences will inevitably manifest during their children's generation. If these youths attempt to turn towards a righteous path, their own guardians will obstruct them. If necessary, they will even go so far as to pray that their children do not tread the right path. This is orchestrated by demonic forces acting to diminish the prosperity of that family.

In Tamil Nadu, there is generally a cruel kind of affection and cruel amusement. They exhibit this even among siblings. They will not say anything directly to one's face. However, once they step aside, they will say, "He happens to be my younger brother, he happens to be my elder brother ٹ. Otherwise, I ٹ." If they possess a bit of education, before finishing a betel chew, they will roll out ten big words. Women have a different disposition. An affectionate sister-in-law, an unaffectionate sister-in-law, and then this woman herself. All three of them will get along perfectly. Do you know why they unite? It is to gossip about others. After ten days of such continuous association, a massive conflict will sprout from there. This too is orchestrated by demonic forces.

This is precisely why it is advocated that the atmosphere must be purified through prayer. A demonic entity standing ten thousand miles away merely needs to make a gesture from there, and it will manifest its effects here on earth. We can cite numerous examples to illustrate this. Certain households might be lying utterly ruined. If slightly provoked, a person's entire demeanor will alter. He will step aside and vociferate whatever comes to his mouth. By the time he acts this way with ten people, he becomes an unbearable burden. In this manner, a vast multitude of individuals have fallen into corruption.

What is worshipped here in the south and elsewhere are essentially demonic entities. These entities will actively corrupt the subsequent generation. It is only due to the inherent goodness of the present time that some fleeting benefits may arise. However, when the time of the forthcoming generations arrives, such extreme affliction will not be witnessed. This is because we have undertaken a specific intervention to address it. Nevertheless, if we fail to establish it in its proper state, the resulting devastation will far exceed all of this. For instance, if a wholesome substance and a toxic material are placed together in one location, the poison will contaminate the wholesome substance the most. Consequently, the good element will be entirely spoiled. If a virtuous offspring is born into a household, that demonic entity will siphon away the fortune accumulated from its past lives. For if it were to lead a righteous life, it would no longer acknowledge this demon, would it? Therefore, the entity ensures it is born in circumstances where it cannot live a virtuous life.

You must study these matters and pray that, by reforming these circumstances through our lives, a truthful path may become accessible to you. There are many here who perform deeds to the best of their abilities, believing them to be good. However, this demonic force will surround you on all sides in a manner that induces sorrow within you. This is its very function. Under such circumstances, it is impossible to reform children by any means. If it is a locality where a sorcerer (mantravadi) resides, corrupting them becomes exceedingly easy. This is because the practice of sorcery yields immediate results, which firmly establishes belief. Consequently, even for a common cold, an individual will resort to sorcery. This is specifically the nature of Tamil Nadu. In Kerala, regions beyond Kollam exhibit a different disposition. The people of the Ernakulam region are largely innocent. But having assimilated Western culture there, they have adopted a worthless way of life. The situation in Kozhikode, Kannur, and Thalassery is identical. This did not occur as a consequence of modernization. We possess an ancestral heritage. When caste infiltrated and corrupted that heritage, these Westerners arrived. With their arrival, a circumstance arose where one could freely pursue some education. As a result, they abandoned both their traditional heritage and the Western ways. The model currently observed in Varkala is also of this paradigm. Regarding the people of Chirayinkeezhu, they possess a distinct character. They will travel anywhere, work laboriously, earn some money, and manage affairs through transactions. However, they might also exhibit a certain degree of barbarism alongside it. They do not associate with individuals akin to themselves. In that state, they will even disrupt their own households. Family members themselves cease to communicate with one another. Historically, they were good human beings. It was the influx of wealth that corrupted them. The people of Kilimanoor share a similar trajectory. In the past, they too were virtuous individuals. Today, there is arguably no one as corrupted as they are. They have now devolved into the most aggressive of people. They find themselves unable to share affection. Thus, by engaging in cruel actions and perverse amusements in various forms, the very beauty of life has been systematically eradicated.

There is no alternative but to thoroughly comprehend this predicament and nurture a new generation as a definitive solution. That is the very path we are undertaking here. Regardless of circumstances, human beings can optimally maintain vitality only up to the age of forty. Thereafter, does health not progressively deteriorate and deplete? While we attempt to accomplish what we can within this timeframe, adversarial forces of equal magnitude stand ready to destroy those efforts. Simultaneously, in the physical realm, one's own kin and relatives remain observant spectators. Should a voice be raised here, they will proactively interpret the meaning of that sound. Within three days, they will invariably end up in conflict amongst themselves.

The root cause of this is the practice of black magic (abhichara). Black magic primarily encompasses these rituals and oracle-like dances conducted in the forests. They execute these rituals venerating entities that resemble beasts. What is their exact modus operandi? If they encounter a virtuous soul, they will instantaneously bestow wealth upon him. Consequently, he develops immense arrogance. Concurrently, this force lies in wait to have him crushed by his very own kin. These are the catastrophic disasters orchestrated by this demonic entity. Yet, we remain completely oblivious to the fact that this is a demonic force at work. We merely assume that these relatives are determined to destroy him out of sheer jealousy regarding his prosperity. But this is not the reality. It is the demonic force that instigates these actions. When an individual lives in such a state and eventually dies, this demonic entity assimilates that soul as well.

When we conduct Guru Puja and related rituals here, and observe individuals showing slight improvement, this demonic force orchestrates their corruption through an alternate route. It systematically alienates them from this path. We remain entirely unaware of this process. However, children born after 1973 cannot be alienated so easily. This is because the epoch of their birth possesses an inherent excellence. Moving forward, with every passing twelve-year cycle, this excellence will progressively amplify. They possess the capability to align with ideologies that resonate with this progression. Refraining from attending here, or conducting marriages and other ceremonies without understanding the auspicious time and context—when such missteps occur, demonic influences infiltrate these actions, inevitably corrupting the individuals involved. We have witnessed numerous such instances here.

The majority of you remain incognizant of the specific areas where our interventions have yielded improvement. When beneficent deeds are done for certain individuals, it often results in a spectacle resembling buffoonery scattered in all directions. It will require one or two generations for this systemic pattern to transform. As successive generations pass, the environmental triggers that breed jealousy and mutual conflict will organically diminish. They will simply lack the time to indulge in them. Consequently, with the passage of generations, the potency of this demonic influence will progressively wane.

When certain individuals develop an affinity for God, they attempt to confine the Divine within rigid, self-drawn boundaries. They do not commit this act out of conscious desire. While navigating and interacting within this worldly existence, we must manage such matters with utmost circumspection. Merely listening to Vedantic aphorisms serves no practical purpose. There lies another insidious danger within that practice. It is a methodology constructed by reiterating a single sentence in ten different permutations, expounding on its meanings, and artificially projecting reverence and adoration. When associated with such superficialities, the essence of the actual good deed is entirely lost.

Two Jupiter cycles (twenty-four years) have elapsed since this paradigm began its transformation. After another two Jupiter cycles, it will undergo a complete metamorphosis. By that juncture, the current generation of children will have reached maturity. It is through them that this systemic transformation can be actualized. What you, the elder generation, critically require is the competence to nurture them toward that standard. Contemporary environments do not furnish the requisite conditions for children to flourish in that manner. The foremost obstacle is the modern educational framework. The secondary issue is the glaring absence of qualified mentors within the household. Presently, in most households, both the father and the mother are employed. After concluding professional duties, managing domestic affairs, and overseeing the children's academic and tuition schedules, they are left with absolutely no time for anything else. What is being instilled in these children are inclinations that are far more detrimental than mere Western tendencies. This phenomenon currently stands as the most formidable destructive force against our cultural fabric.

It is with a profound understanding of this reality that we must undertake the upbringing of children. However, the majority of households fail to comprehend this. Parents have time for nothing. The children, likewise, have no time. Rousing them precisely at four o'clock, these parents sit together, verbally reprimand them, and compel the children to study. Should the neighbor's child secure a mere ten marks more, these parents, unable to endure the ensuing psychological agony, will beat their chests, wail hysterically, and collapse face down. This is the tragic reality of our parents!

I am frequently compelled to reflect on this. While we have labored painstakingly to orchestrate these efforts for the welfare of these families, Western absurdities have deeply infiltrated their midst. Exorbitant fees are levied starting from the nursery level itself. As they advance, educational expenditures escalate proportionally with the progression in grades. The parents endure immense hardship. Yet, despite undertaking all these sacrifices, they are plagued by a persistent fear—if they fail to yield to the children's whims, will the children abandon them to pursue their own desires? Upon completing their education, these formally educated youths behave precisely in accordance with those ingrained expectations. If their demands are unmet, they direct their resentment toward the parents—questioning why they cannot purchase an automobile? Cannot they observe others acquiring vehicles? Alternatively, if it is a household financially capable of purchasing a vehicle, they will argue: why not purchase a separate vehicle for each individual? Why must everyone travel collectively in a single car?

How exactly do our people undertake religious pilgrimages? Officials from various departments congregate and embark on journeys meticulously tailored to reflect their social prestige. Upon returning, the entire narrative revolves around the detailed accounting of the expenditures incurred during the journey. Similarly, in households possessing substantial financial influx, if the husband exhibits frugality, the women of the household will conveniently manifest severe physical ailments hither and thither. Consequently, they must be admitted to the most prestigious medical institution available. Subsequently, correspondence is dispatched to distant relatives detailing the ordeal. Diagnostic procedures will encompass the examination of feces, urine, blood, and even investigations into anomalous bone growths. Exorbitant laboratory fees, astronomical physician consultation charges—thus culminating in a colossal financial hemorrhage. This wealth is painstakingly accumulated by individuals who, unable to secure a livelihood in their native land, have migrated to foreign territories to toil arduously. Do the individuals residing comfortably in these households possess even a modicum of awareness regarding this harsh reality?

You are nowhere near true knowledge. This is what I have been stating. Most individuals have not comprehended how we ought to conduct ourselves in accordance with our ideals. What are we engaged in today? How much bribe must one pay to educate someone from nursery upwards to make them a doctor? How exorbitant is the amount paid merely as an admission fee! Why do you exhibit such a keen interest in submitting to such extortion? Is it not because you anticipate some other form of extortion in return? Alternatively, someone might claim to be honest. Apart from that single individual, you will not find another of his ilk. We have been conditioned in a system of giving and taking extortion. How will you emancipate yourselves from this? Where do all these aforementioned aspects stand in the context of your righteous deeds?
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Dedication Issue 2002
The Karma Bestowed by God for the Salvation of the World

We possess a traditional knowledge that has been practiced and adhered to for many *yugas* (epochs). Whether this knowledge is correct or flawed, we have continually perpetuated it. We are unable to clarify and consolidate this knowledge. The underlying reason for this is the competitive spirit among *Shaivam*, *Shakteyam*, and *Vaishnavam*. They have engaged in this rivalry without comprehending the true nature of God, *Shakteyam*, or *Vaishnavam*, nor understanding their inherent characteristics. Such competition exists across all religious denominations. However, the intense rivalry witnessed within Hinduism is unparalleled elsewhere. It is not that we have refrained from contemplating the reasons behind this. We have reflected upon it numerous times. Yet, despite such contemplation, the true reasons remain elusive. I comprehended this through my own personal experience.

What have we been conditioned to hear? That attaining a single vision of the Lord is sufficient and constitutes everything. Regardless of who asserts, believes, or propagates this, the unequivocal truth is this—a *Deva* (god) or *Devi* (goddess) is utterly incapable of granting us anything substantive. In the contemporary era, for you as human beings, ascending to the status of a *Deva* or *Devi* is not a remarkably difficult feat. Any among you can attain that state.

What we must understand is that as we advance along the path of experience, within the realm that determines the ultimate trajectory of the soul, a *Deva* or *Devi* has absolutely no role to play. A *Rishi* (sage) subordinate to a *Deva* is similarly powerless. *Rishis* exist both subordinate and superior to the *Devas*. Among them, the *Rishis* who transcend the *Devas* have never submitted to a *Deva* or the epoch of a *Deva*. However, we remain entirely ignorant of these matters. There is a specific reason for such non-compliance, which shall be elucidated later.

*Shaivam*, *Shakteyam*, and *Vaishnavam* have competitively proclaimed the supremacy of their respective deities. Adherents of each of these traditions have further fragmented into major and minor castes, subsequently assigning distinct deities to each specific caste. We must introspect and question ourselves as to how this phenomenon originated. We have harbored the misconception that these matters do not concern us, and that they ought to be solely addressed by ascetics (*Sannyasis*) and similar eminent figures. We have also assumed, or rather have been conditioned to believe, that we require none of this and only necessitate the material aspects of life. It is entirely due to our profound ignorance that such circumstances have transpired.

What we must contemplate here is this—does not a virtuous *Brahmachari* (celibate student), *Vanaprastha* (forest dweller), or *Sannyasi* (renunciate) emerge from a family life itself? It is precisely because you fail to comprehend this that you blindly accept whatever arbitrary claims others have propagated. That is not how we should perceive it. From family life, noble offspring must be born who are beneficial to their home, society, and the nation. Furthermore, if there are any shortcomings in the monumental contributions made for us by the visionaries of the past, there must exist competent individuals within the lineage of such visionaries to elucidate and rectify them. This is the absolute doctrinal truth.

The folly resulting from the inability to recognize visionaries in their true essence is colossal. Visionaries do not manifest in every era. Even among them, those who arrive to exemplify the merit and *Dharma* (righteous duty) of specific *Yugas* are exceedingly rare. Even visionaries who appear at the commencement of one *Yuga* cannot adequately articulate the *Dharma* of other *Yugas*. Where it was decreed that a *Shudra* possessed no right to sovereign rule or Vedic authority, we must ponder why, at the dawn of this *Yuga* (*Kali*), royal authority was bestowed upon Sri Krishna’s lineage. It was Kamsa who was initially granted this authority. However, Kamsa was incapable of accepting it with an attitude of complete surrender. Whether it originated from a *Deva*, a *Devi*, a *Guru*, or God Himself, Kamsa ought to have approached the divine voice (*Ashariri*) he received with absolute devotion. Kamsa failed to do so. Yet, if one asks whether Kamsa committed a sin, he did not do that either.

Have we not been conditioned to perceive Kamsa as entirely wicked? Yet, Kamsa was not inherently wicked. How could a malevolent person receive a divine voice (*Ashariri*)? A wicked person might perhaps receive a disembodied voice from a demon or a *Deva*, but certainly not the divine voice of God. The fundamental error Kamsa committed was this: a deeply ingrained devotion towards the physical manifestation of a *Deva* was entrenched within him. The majority of people, much like Kamsa, firmly believe that the visually manifested *Devas* and *Devis*, and their ensuing blessings, are of paramount importance. Those who experience such visual manifestations tend to believe in their own consequential greatness. If every religion, caste, and class claims supremacy, and if every individual subscribing to them considers themselves superior, is God an entity to be apportioned in such a manner? Will such individuals ever act in our best interest? Those who think and speak in this manner rationalize the purported truths in their minds, ultimately descending into actions devoid of broader wisdom. For them, only two arguments exist: rationalism (*Yuktivadam*) and the doctrine of liberation (*Muktivadam*). Consequently, any debater arguing incessantly will merely end up paralyzed by their own rhetoric. Absolutely nothing can be achieved through such argumentation.

Devoid of any profound comprehension regarding the divine will, we merely fragment God and construct disparate paths; as far as we are concerned, there is absolutely no righteous action emanating from this that imparts benevolence. The primary reason for this is our indoctrination that the *Dharma* of *Kali Yuga* is inherently evil. If a boy or a girl in the household commits a mistake, it is immediately attributed to the influence of *Kali*. However, what is the actual fault of *Kali*? We remain ignorant of that as well.

If there exists a *Dharma* delineated across four distinct *Yugas*, how ought we to perceive it? In the *Satya Yuga*, all human beings are equal; in the *Treta Yuga*, the modes of worship undergo a transformation. That transformation intensifies and solidifies further in the *Dvapara Yuga*. If any fundamental errors were committed during these preceding three *Yugas*, the intrinsic *Dharma* of *Kali* is to thoroughly churn and resolve all of them together.

Once your mortal time has passed, will you have the capacity to contemplate anything? Before that eventuality, were you able to impart anything of value to your children? If there is a devout child in your home, how will the parents guide them? Will they introduce God by recounting tales of miraculous creations? Does God perform magic tricks? You are entirely incapable of contemplating any of these questions due to the sheer ignorance that has somehow permeated your intellect.

When speaking of humanity, one must not artificially segregate it based on caste, religion, and class. Conversely, the assertion that all are simply uniform human beings is also inaccurate. This is because there exist inherent fluctuations in fortune and misfortune. Both the fortunate and the unfortunate have continually striven and continue to strive. That relentless striving is indeed valid and correct.

*Chaturvarnya* (the four-fold social order) operates in accordance with the *Yuga Dharma*. The prevailing assumption that the caste system originated from *Chaturvarnya* is fundamentally incorrect. It is absolutely not a historical truth. The true nature of *Chaturvarnya* is to elucidate the specific *Dharma* of each respective *Yuga*. It is a profound misconception stemming from the arbitrary actions of those bereft of true knowledge regarding *Dharma*. Concerted efforts have been underway here for countless millions of years to rectify and reclaim this monumental error.

What you believe and teach is a history of two thousand, four thousand, or at most ten thousand years. Has it been only this long since the origin of this world? No. The calculation is that one Kali Yuga itself consists of four lakh thirty-two thousand years across many crores of years. Of that, only the five thousand years of the Kali era after Sri Krishna have passed. What have we turned even such a great man as Sri Krishna into? To some, he is the author of the Gita; to others, he is the one who stole the clothes of the Gopis. To some, he is truly a philanderer. We must not forget the truth that we do not know what all this "philanderer" has done. None of this is the karma of Sri Krishna. If Sri Krishna, who was born in a prison, gave a vision to sixteen thousand and eight women, you should observe what that greatness is. When the creation of these sixteen thousand and eight women came through the poet's imagination, it turned into sixteen thousand and eight wives. How negative is this act! How have you absorbed this? Shouldn't it be said at least in a logical manner? So, going after the poet's imagination, deviating from dharma, we are seeing God on the basis of an ecstatic, trance-like knowledge. This is the ignorance of the Shudra class. In our homes, in each one of us, there resides a Shudra nature. There is a story told about this. Once, Sri Narayana Guru told a rich man in Thalassery, "A Chandal dwells within you; you must get rid of it." This man immediately went and drove out the Chandal (a person of lower caste) who was a tenant in his compound by beating him. So, our ancestors are ignorant people like this. What knowledge will they impart to us?

In fact, what should be the knowledge of a householder (grihasthashrami)? In order to serve this land, home, and country, the children, father, mother, wife, and husband should set out with all their wealth, lordship, and educated knowledge. Their knowledge should be such that it protects their fortune without spoiling or corrupting it. Instead of this blessedness, what are the householders doing? In the name of education, they are sowing plunder and reaping plunder. When educational institutions came into existence by the grace of God, you became Western-looking machines. You gather everything that happens in Western countries and place it here. Your only job is to stare solely at that and gather it here. What has happened as a result of that? The more beautiful North Indians turned the South Indians into monkeys. In the matter of worship, Vaishnavism is everything to North India. As for Shiva, Dakshinamurthy, that is, one Guru for all the four states in South India together - Shiva. Its spiritual aspect is the Dakshinamurthy Stotram. They wrote the Dakshinamurthy Stotram backward like this and convinced us. We fell for it. Shaivism, and then combined with it, Shaktism. When it was written and added in this manner, we could not digest any of it. The truth is that, knowingly or unknowingly, we got trapped in this knowledge. And if someone comes among us to tell us all this, we will not understand it.

There are people who even believe that devotion to God is for ascetics and householders do not need it. But if an accident or any other harm befalls you or your most loved ones, you will call upon God. Which God are you calling like that? A knowledge that came as Shaktism and Shaivism exists in this nature. It is by looking at the nature that has taken form that they are calling: My Goddessٹ .. let nothing happen. They are praying that nothing should happen to the child who has completed ten months and is about to be born. That is, neither good nor bad should happen. Such is the level of ignorance that has grown in our mothers.

What is the reason our mothers have become like this? There are quite a few names to call a father who goes somewhere, works, and struggles to support his children, wife, and others. In South Travancore, it is called by adding meanings to words like *moopparu* (the elder) and *achhan sakhavu* (father comrade). There are others with such special meanings. They are the ones who swallow up logic and liberation. Other than the fact that there are children who are getting spoiled in these ways, what special thing do we have? We are unable to take up the dharma of our home and land. How should we view the downfall of the rulers who even asked for a price for their own country? They are the ones with the heritage of the greatest tradition in India. Moreover, they are the authorities of all kinds of high deeds of knowledge, lordship, and wealth. Because they only handled Western education, they could not figure out what things are conducive to the goodness of this land. However, they did not try to spoil the land either. But the truth is that they fell into a pit by not knowing the reality.

When they went after Western culture, even the way Hindus greet God became like Christians making the sign of the cross. When imitation came about in this manner, we could not find a way to align with the truth. Thus, everyone became scavengers of foreign countries. If it is said that this culture is what the ruler here was able to serve us, it shows how much we have degraded. Because we degraded in this manner, it was as if the imperialistic nature caught and swallowed us.

All the imperial models in the world originated first in India. When that happened, people of each country developed their own models here. Even the model of governance where one ruled the country after imprisoning his own father was staged right here. Which model of governance that originated here do we need? It is here that all violent natures occurred. Thus, we fell behind in all aspects. And this did not just happen today or yesterday. This is a mischief that has been going on since ages ago.

We are unaware of the karmic course established by Manu and his lineage. The one karmic course we are familiar with belongs to the Trimurti system. Hindu spiritual masters, followers of prophetic traditions, solitary theoreticians, and guides who practiced diverse yogic disciplines have prescribed remedial measures for this through four paths: Karma, Jnana, Yoga, and Bhakti. If instructed in this manner, what are ordinary human beings to do? An individual must be taught what his specific duty (*karma*) entails.
