However, we lack the tradition of instructing one on their duty. Consequently, the children growing up in our households have become undesirable to their mothers, fathers, homes, and the nation. The children they raise find themselves ensnared in the very same bondage that entraps their parents. All our families have degenerated in this fashion. Ultimately, it has culminated in a situation where your children construct old-age homes for you. What virtue can be gleaned by us, who have been conditioned to degrade in such a manner?

This predicament is not confined to a single religion or caste. Every religion and every caste confronts this situation. What must we do to transform this? If we are to muster the courage to change this, we must first recognize the fundamental rights and wrongs of our respective religions. Subsequently, these elements must be carefully sorted and rectified. The fundamental error in Hinduism occurred when it deviated from the lineage of Manu, driven by the fabricated history asserting that the Manvantaras emerged under Brahma. Similarly, every religion originated from the absurdities conceived in the minds of historians. In every epoch, God consistently presents the genuine truth before us, yet we refuse to embrace it. Irrespective of which guru or prophet arrives, myriad methods emerge everywhere. Thus, the traditional knowledge we possess is derived from thousands of factions, resembling scattered cloud formations. In which of these factions does God reside? Is God an entity to be compartmentalized into every division created by human beings? God is not of such a nature. No one's God is of such a nature.

The customs currently prevalent in the Hindu tradition are entirely incorrect. As for adherents of other religions, it would be commendable if they could sustain themselves at least according to the temporal duties (*kala-dharma*) they have prescribed for themselves. However, no one within those factions possesses a true understanding of *kala-dharma*. They too remain perplexed in this regard. What is the nature of this perplexity? According to the revelations concerning the Antichrist and the Final Prophet, it is the calculation of Manu that has faltered.

What ought to transpire in this world? Which calculus should we adopt to ascertain this? That of Manu's lineage, the Trimurti lineage, or the prophetic lineage? Or perhaps that of the visionary's lineage? Ignorant of this, we are warring against one another, hesitating at nothing. We have plunged into such profound degradation because true religious consciousness has not been imparted to us. It is an ignorance that has been bequeathed through tradition.

What constitutes religious consciousness? Religious consciousness is a karmic trajectory in which the profound truth of our life is firmly anchored to our birth. Once you have established such a life truth, you possess the prerogative to contemplate what lies beyond it. However, as householders, you have discarded the religious consciousness conducive to this; instead, you have embraced a burdensome traditional knowledge, acquired haphazardly, which extends no further than a mere ten thousand years into the past. How can the wisdom necessary to guide the truth of your life be reconciled with such a flawed paradigm!

You are under the illusion that the epoch of Kali will conclude imminently. Of the 4,32,000 years, merely 5,200 years have elapsed. If one asserts that all those born in Kali are inherently worthless, then who shall fulfill the *dharma* of Kali? The assertion that Kali is inherently malevolent is fallacious. Securing an opportunity to be born during the Kali Yuga is itself a tremendous privilege. This is because we have been entrusted with a karmic duty that fulfills a paramount *dharma*. Regardless of religion, caste, or class, it must unequivocally be accomplished. This is what we must realize. Kali possesses the mandate of a karmic action that identifies the errors of the past and present, distills them, and establishes the ultimate truth. Instead of imparting this wisdom to the youth, religious dogmas are fed to them, thereby instilling a violent propensity for mutual conflict. No virtue whatsoever can be derived from such an aggressive and distorted mode of divine worship.

Today, for us, gods, goddesses, and even malevolent spirits are deified as God. This phenomenon occurred because successive generations were nurtured without being imparted knowledge concerning the wheel of time (*kalachakra*). What necessitated the advent of prophetic religions here in the first place? It is the consequence of invoking God through malpractices, having irretrievably discarded the authentic *dharma* of the Hindu tradition somewhere along the way. Consequently, conflicts erupted. Those of lower castes were forbidden from approaching the paramount deities. They were compelled to seek solace solely in the deities designated for lower castes. Consequently, they migrated to spaces that offered freedom. Such an exodus was inevitable. Had they not departed, they would have never attained freedom, education, or socio-economic dignity.

Only such a convoluted karmic trajectory prevails in India. Indeed, this very same karmic trajectory is evident throughout the world. Whatever prerequisites a human being requires to lead a life nurturing a religious consciousness aligned with the *dharma* of this Kali epoch, those are essential not merely in India, but anywhere across the globe. We can exist only in consonance with nature. It is impossible for anyone to impart *dharma* to householders who exist devoid of the discerning intellect to act in alignment with nature, and who are incapable of reclaiming the inherent goodness of the natural order.

Should two more generations pass in the current manner, children will fail to even comprehend the true essence of freedom. What will ensue thereafter is an arbitrary notion of freedom constructed according to their whims. If we acknowledge the profound truth that rationalism and doctrines of salvation are inadequate to redeem us, then what, ultimately, is the resolution? That lies with the visionary. Visionaries themselves are of diverse kinds. Visionaries who emerge with a profound influence spanning two thousand, three thousand, or five thousand years will impart their teachings for their respective epochs and depart. Subsequently, in order to rectify the aberrations that have afflicted *dharma*, the extant generation must possess the requisite wisdom. Otherwise, they will resemble a tree with a decaying foundation. A tree with such a compromised base will inevitably topple when subjected to a forceful gale. Similarly, we are mindlessly participating in a race driven by the karmic momentum of unchecked scientific advancement. That race is profoundly misguided.

What I convey to you stems from my personal experience. I have not appropriated the logic, scriptures (*shruti*), or rationalizations of any external authority. By virtue of being born a Hindu, I operated under the assumption that the Hindu paradigm was superior. There was indeed an extended period during which I harbored this belief. In our formative years, our mothers instill in us the notion, "Children, God is a wrathful entity that punishes with death." Consequently, even if God is not a punisher, can one evade the ingrained fear of Him? As we mature further, God is perceived as an entity that orchestrates trials and surveillance. Advancing still further, God is reduced to the residue of frenzied oracles—trembling, dancing, chanting, and exhibiting possessed behavior. Subsequently, after cultivating faith, devotion, and reverence over a prolonged period, a realization dawns that this entity is not worthy of being revered as God. At that juncture, embracing rationalism and alternative ideologies, an individual showcases intellectual prowess within the confines of those arguments. Ultimately, the individual finds himself entirely lost within them. In this manner, men and women perpetuate diverse spectacles across various strata. There exist myriad such inexplicable karmic trajectories. These are the very phenomena you categorize using diverse nomenclatures—*Karmi*, *Yogi*, *Jnani*, *Bhakta*, Fakir, Saint, and Apostle. Irrespective of our caste, religion, or class, we are fundamentally incapable of transcending this overarching paradigm.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Dedication Edition 2002
The Aspect of the Householder Undertaking the Karma Kanda of Worldly Life

When we hear the term *ashram*, our general assumption is that it is a place intended for ascetic renunciation. Is not Shantiniketan an *ashram*? Are children enrolled there to embrace asceticism? Even Lord Krishna resided in the *ashram* of Sage Sandipani. Was Krishna sent there to become an ascetic? There are even individuals who believe that one should never visit an *ashram*. Women are strictly prohibited from entering an *ashram*—such is the nature of your understanding.

How did such profound ignorance take root within you? You have failed to comprehend that this is merely a residual manifestation of a traditional practice that denied women access to education, wealth, and authority, even prohibiting them from dressing appropriately. The historians who imparted this knowledge merely perpetuated the same distorted narrative.

You perceive an ascetic as someone who sequesters himself in a forest or wilderness, forsaking sustenance, or surviving solely on water and leaves. This is the extent of the knowledge you have amassed. Is there a modicum of historical truth to this assertion? You have regrettably lacked the intellectual curiosity to investigate this matter. In this domain, it is the Brahmin who is presumed to possess some knowledge. Yet, even he has not investigated the true purpose of visiting an *ashram*. Regarding this specific knowledge, the Brahmin and the Chandala stand on equal footing.

The mandate of *dharma* dictates that a state must secure the blessings of a sage to maintain its righteousness. Individuals resided in *ashrams* and sought counsel to refine governance and to attain a deeper understanding of life. Given this historical context, how have you descended into the ignorant and unjust presumption that children are merely abandoned there to be forced into asceticism?

I have engaged in extensive discourse with you and undertaken necessary actions to eradicate this ignorance! These were not mere empty words. I performed these duties as a lifelong obligation that must be preserved until the very end. However, you remain incapable of comprehending and respecting this on a universal scale.
What is the underlying cause for this?

We have been indoctrinated with a restricted knowledge centered exclusively around gods and goddesses, asserting that all living souls are subordinate to the divine. No one has preserved the profound knowledge regarding the concept of *Manvantara*. There is a pervasive ignorance concerning the number of *Chaturyugas* that constitute a single *Manvantara*. We have collectively assimilated numerous such fallacies. Consequently, regardless of the extent of explanation provided, it fails to permeate your understanding. There is absolutely no recourse left to rectify this.

There is a residual karmic force behind us, stemming from the practices worshipped and propagated by our ancestors. This force continually assails us. It manifests as a corrupted karmic residue through afflictions such as disease, poverty, malevolent offspring, and a multitude of violent traits that are fundamentally incompatible with domestic harmony. Such detrimental characteristics arise due to a profound absence of merit or virtue. What can be expected of children born into households devoid of such merit? These children are inherently incapable of demonstrating obedience when instructed. The catastrophic consequences stemming from this disobedience are not insignificant. These children remain oblivious to the fact that this is a mechanism designed to foresee the blunders resulting from your unwarranted actions, and that we must cultivate a specialized discipline to uphold *karma* and *dharma* through this very mechanism.

You belong to a cohort that offers vows and offerings to the divine solely for the fulfillment of personal desires. How deeply degraded must you be to attempt to manipulate the divine through such offerings? What is the distinguishing merit of an intellect that presumes to achieve its goals by bribing God with vows and offerings? What is required for you to transcend this pervasive ignorance? You require the fundamental honesty to comprehensively assimilate any acquired knowledge across your household, your community, and your nation. To actualize this, you must possess a harmonious and adaptable disposition. Yet, you are incapable of cultivating such a disposition. This is because you are the very embodiment of ignorance, operating within a distorted intellect that has been infiltrated by myriad extraneous matters. You do not genuinely desire a truthful mode of existence. Even if such a desire were present, you would be utterly incapable of manifesting it.

This deplorable predicament is not confined to a single household, community, or nation. Nor is it an affliction exclusive to any one religion. It is a universal malady plaguing all of humanity. In the realm of genuine knowledge, you are making absolutely no progress. No substantial assistance is forthcoming from the state apparatus. The state has devolved into an entity that actively devastates the world. Ignorance merely spawns further ignorance when statecraft is manipulated to serve the transient interests of caste, religion, and immediate political expediency. Everyone considers themselves exceptionally astute. Yet, if questioned about the purpose of this purported astuteness, they possess no answer. The most preeminent writers and the greatest thinkers have all emerged from this very paradigm. The root cause lies in an educational doctrine that has entirely forsaken the virtues of humility and the expression of respect through genuine affection. Each of you is vehemently eager to embrace the culmination of a profoundly degraded existence, a consequence of your entrenched unfamiliarity with humility and love. Alternatively, you operate under the stubborn conviction that you will persist in your current ways, regardless of whether it results in disease or calamity. Because such a destructive karmic force is being sustained, annihilation is descending like a tempest, not only upon humanity but upon all living beings.

What do the elderly mothers in our society often proclaim? They state that they have fulfilled their duties and that the subsequent generation may act as they please, threatening to simply abandon the household if circumstances become intolerable. What is the underlying implication of such statements? It is an implicit threat to adopt a life of asceticism. We have an abundance of individuals harboring such a distorted inclination towards asceticism. We possess ancestors who similarly abandoned their responsibilities under the guise of renunciation. This is the primary reason. Is asceticism merely a convenient weapon to be wielded when one's physical vitality wanes, despite having possessed wealth and capability? The prevalent notion is that divine devotion is strictly reserved for old age when physical strength deteriorates, and until then, one is entitled to lead a recklessly indulgent life. How did such a degraded aspiration permeate our society? This fundamental misunderstanding is precisely why conflicts arise upon hearing that someone has visited an *ashram*. Each of you is the very embodiment of ignorance, utterly incapable of distinguishing the true essence of an *ashram*, the duties of a householder (*Grihastha*), the nature of a celibate student (*Brahmachari*), or the distinction between a practitioner of action (*Karmi*) and a seeker of knowledge (*Jnani*).

It is a mother belonging to this specific category who threatens to leave when confronted with disappointment. What profound knowledge can one possibly acquire from such a mother? Her obstinacy stems from a vindictive desire to make society believe that her children are so neglectful that they would deny her even a drop of water, or to ensure people say that she departed just as someone else's parent had previously abandoned their home.

Similarly, another manifestation of this absolute ignorance is the guise of political leadership. An individual who merely hides behind political banners or agricultural symbols, fleeing at the slightest approach of law enforcement, suddenly transforms into a self-proclaimed leader upon returning later in refined attire. He subsequently drags even the third generation into his ideological wake. Among these youths, some will mature into unquestioning followers of the North, while others blindly align with the West. Is it genuinely possible to rehabilitate children raised in such an environment? Instead, they are excessively coddled and indulged. Ultimately, both you and these children will be left entirely hollow. They will have attained neither material prosperity nor spiritual elevation.

If you are to truly fulfill your roles as parents to your children, you must possess the capability to educate them about the genuine legacy of your ancestors. Instead, you must refrain from imposing distorted intellects upon them merely to conceal your own moral failings. You—parents and children alike—are existing merely as symbols of the bestial nature instilled by a corrupted educational system. Who can possibly reform you, and through what means? Consider yourselves fortunate if you can contribute even a single, capable child who is of genuine use to the community or the nation. That remains your sole avenue for ultimate salvation.

Why do I say this? I have struggled my whole life so that you could attain such a karma. But not even a handful of families have understood and embraced it. It is not because you lack love, respect, or experience. You lack the inherent aptitude (vasana) and the genesis born of such aptitude. This aptitude cannot be bought. You can handle this properly only if you have the sense of dharma to imbibe it through your life. Otherwise, you will achieve nothing. I am saying this out of my pain.

After understanding this ideology and this karma, you are merely picking up what lies on the wayside and behaving erratically. You, who grow up seeing, hearing, and experiencing this, must remember that you have a duty to share this with your life. My desire is that at least the children who grow up observing this should take up this dharma, without becoming clever like their parents, eager to pull everyone down and climb on top of them, thereby becoming possessors of impure intentions, injustice, and baseness.

If you desire any good, it cannot be achieved except through love. You will not receive God's love through your prestige and arrogance. You must not create a situation where everything is consumed by fire and destroyed. You should not lead a life in a way that makes it impossible to ever undertake God's dharma. Ask yourselves whether you are living in a manner worthy of embracing God's justice.

This is not like the ideology, asceticism (sannyasa), or ashram as you have understood them so far. You are pretending to be scholars, seeking the magnitude of scholarship of those whose karmic path is corrupted and whose merit (punya) is destroyed. What is the buffoonery shown by the scholar? What can you earn from this action of creating a sphere of influence of letters by defining and interpreting the meaning of every vowel and consonant? It is foolishness devoid of action and experience. That does not mean you shouldn't learn. Learn, but you must understand its limitations. After understanding, you must also recognize that it introduces us to concealing within ourselves actions that are completely untrue, lead to deviant thinking, and are highly harmful.

Those who engage in this scholarly work have never earned any spiritual merit. This is the work of harmonizing the nature of an incarnation (avatar) with the nature of God. The act of making an avatar out of any personality that rises to prominence is an imposition of Hinduism. What other good is there in this than building a fortress of destruction by speaking of avatars, saints, and holy women?

What I am talking about is not asceticism. Asceticism does not necessarily require an ashram. Yet, it does. When one renounces and feels completely fulfilled with life, an ashram is needed. For that, an ashram and its associated arrangements are required.

It was mentioned earlier that a place without virtuous people (sadhus) is doomed. Who are the sadhus? The aforementioned ascetics. They are noble beings. They did not live considering anything material. Whatever you do for them is not too much. But asceticism is not the act of feeding and destroying people using money, education, and intellect. An ascetic is truly blessed. Knowledge, wealth, and mastery will all reach the place where he sits. If they are ascetics, with what will you preserve that asceticism? How will you protect the ascetic who came to preserve your knowledge, wealth, and mastery without decay? You lack the humility to know this. You should not be ready to take on the karmic flaw of action without humility. Even those who do not know me should always preserve these words.

You are meant to undertake the path of action (karmakanda) in connection with worldly life. Otherwise, there is no use in wandering here and there. Your ancestors lived without knowing this and failed. We cannot reject their failure. We are taking on that sense of failure. That is, we are taking up the karma and dharma in which they failed. Then we must contribute children who are inheritors of merit. This is possible only through your life. It cannot come through an ascetic. The one who accepts that karma is the karmi. You, who are supposed to accept that karma, should not live creating chaos with an obstinate mindset that you will neither obey dharma nor seek punya. Ignorant writers, with depleted intellects, are binding you to the path of destructive actions where intellect and knowledge clash.

A householder (grihastha) is not meant to degrade like this. Through life, one must acquire wealth, knowledge, and prosperity, and if needed, undertake the duty to govern the nations of the world itself. If you stand on the logic that what is under your arm should not be lost, and what is above must also be taken, you are never going to achieve anything. This is the opportunity ordained for you by God. Let the flaws committed by your ancestors be resolved through your actions. Instead of doing bad and reaping bad, let everyone do good and reap good.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarpana Pathippu 2002
Knowledge in the States of Waking, Dreaming, and Deep Sleep

There is a familiarity that we have been worshiping, seeing, knowing, and speaking of for many ages (yugas). We have passed through the actions of many eras. The calculation regarding one yuga, or rather a chaturyuga (four ages), is immense. Seventy-one such chaturyugas make a manvantara. After six such manvantaras, the seventh manvantara is currently in existence. The residual energy of karma, worshiped, seen, heard, known, and practiced over so many manvantaras, is retained in this atmosphere. Every word we speak and every wave of thought we release remains imprinted in this nature, much like taking a photograph.

There is a life essence to what we speak. It is inscribed in this nature. Sound has been inscribed. That is, it is our actions that have been inscribed. Similarly, the karmas we have performed by taking bodies over countless births are also recorded in this nature. That being the case, it is not enough to merely talk about the concept of past lives (janmanthara) in words. We must be able to see that janmanthara. There is a soul within the body. We must be able to see in this nature the actions performed by the bodies previously taken by that soul. Looking at it that way, we should be able to see everything from the origin of the world and the universe up to the present. We cannot see this by blindly believing and sitting at the feet of whatever is labeled as God. That is not enough; we must be able to see it. There are crores of people in this world. At least one person among them must have seen and understood this, and be there to tell us.

If we are to believe that God exists, we must be able to see God, right? But do the believer and the non-believer believe after seeing and knowing? The non-believer does not know what God is. The believer also does not know what God is. However, it is God who has created the laws of nature. The laws of nature have operated and reached areas where science cannot reach. Science itself moves while remaining within the laws of nature. Should we think that something immense has been discovered just because gravitational force was discovered? It is not just about gravitational force; the existence of all living beings, their evolutionary processes, and the determination of which realms they should reach must occur in the physical world. What is the plan of action to take the subjects that occur beyond all this to a realm where they are handled even further? What all should we prepare for this?

Where does the past era stand, which realm should be reached in the coming era, and what is needed for that—this is the habit of thought we require. This is the time we are living in, after all. Do we not need to know these things to live knowing the reality and karma of this life?

Three eras have passed. Now the Satya Yuga is about to arrive. Witnessing these, if we, who are born and living in the Kali Yuga, must live by perceiving the dharmic aspect of the eras, we must live by perceiving the reality of life itself. Do we not need a preceptor (Acharya) to teach us this? Has any guru, ascetic, prophet, or sage told us about this karma? No one has told us. But what we desperately need is this action plan (karma paddhati). An action plan for the times to come. That must come through our successive generations. We must wipe out or resolve through action the calamities of the past and the present, and bring our generations into a life ordained by God. Thus, as generations pass, we ourselves will reach the aforementioned stage. This is the cycle of rebirth and death. We need an Acharya to perceive and explain to us these births and deaths.

We have done many things in the name of worshipping God. That has been practiced for many generations. Our ancestors worshipped demonic entities, imbibed their base qualities, and their souls ended up in the ancestral realm (Pithru Rashi); we are born in those very realms, and our lifestyles, experiences, and everything else are imbued with base qualities. The very inclination to reach real life is lost for a soul that bears miserable life experiences and suffers, due to the calamities that occurred by virtue of birth.

When a child is born, a horoscope is written. The horoscope is cast based on the time of birth. How is that time derived? It is from the astrological sign (Rashi) where the ancestor (Pithru), who is the cause of the birth, is situated. So, this destiny has come from there onwards. The cause for the tendencies of good and bad, fortune and misfortune, all lie there. How will we know this? The astrologer merely mentions a word called ancestral curse (Pithru Dosham). Or else the wrath of the goddess. Or family curse. He will also prescribe remedial rituals according to Vedic tenets. But will it be resolved? One must firmly believe that it will not be. Let me give an example for this. What is the state today of the Brahmin who authoritatively performed all these Vedic rituals? Given that state, how will we, who adopt these ritualistic rules, be saved? Then one can only wonder where the truth behind these practices lies. Christians and Muslims are those who do not perform any of these rituals. They have come to a somewhat more peaceful life than the Hindus. If nothing else, they have at least managed to earn enough to eat and clothe themselves.

It is the Hindu, who has traditionally conducted worship and carried forward a lifestyle, that has suffered the greatest calamities. India had sciences, Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, Mantras, Tantras, and many such doctrines in a way no other nation had. Even people from foreign lands came here to study and conduct research in universities like Nalanda and Takshashila. What a great economic status existed here! We were the highest not only in wealth but also in culture, mathematics, aeronautics, and chemistry. But everything was ruined. Those who came from foreign lands looted and took away all the wealth that existed here. Then they developed it in another way and greatly elevated their living standards. What is the reason for us ending up in such a degraded state?

Life has a foundational ideology, doesn't it? So, we lived, grew, and perished on some foundation. We have ancestors who worshipped and caused to be worshipped in the name of various entities. The methods they believed in and the karmas they performed are here. Only their physical bodies have perished. Their souls and the karma-potential born of their intrinsic tendencies (vasanas) have not perished. Just because we say it doesn't exist, it won't cease to exist. Nor will it ever leave us.

There are tendencies (vasanas) forged through mind, word, and deed before our ancestors were born and before we were born. That vasana has reached and stands in a part of our souls, just as it does in our ancestors. No one should doubt this. How can this vasana be eliminated? There is another karma standing there, which has passed by, knowingly or unknowingly, calling and causing to be called, without realizing any of this. Whether one is a rationalist or a salvation-seeker, can they escape from this? We ourselves are acting here. When this body is left behind, the result of the karma we performed will remain with us. I say this after seeing the truth of nature that has imbued itself into every atom of the karma that came and went before and after us. That is experience. This is the cause of the good, the bad, the disease, and the happiness of each one of us. That is, the remnant of the karma that our ancestors and we have worshipped and acted upon, good and bad, and imprinted on nature, is the cause of the happiness and sorrow of our souls.

Narayana Guru, Sri Shankara, and Chattampi Swami were born in Kerala itself. Knowingly or unknowingly, a number of us believe in them. There is this belief, and there is the karma that was made to be believed. Should we know this karma or not? Just like this, the entire world exists. Seeing this in this state, we need a medium (upadhi) to bring it closer to us. What is this medium? We have a spiritual familiarity that was traditionally ruined by conducting worship in the name of whatever entities. This is not what I am talking about. Only an individual who wishes, on the foundation of love, to analytically understand philosophy, see the damages in it, and impart its good aspects before us can become that medium.

We haven't even thought about what rights the woman in our house has. She is someone's mother, someone's wife, someone's daughter, and yet another's sister. Have we ever pondered what fundamental mistakes have happened to this woman who has come this way? If one says, "I am a rationalist, nothing like that will come into my house," will it not come? If there is a person who can point out and explain this mistake, as well as the mistakes pertaining not just to the human realm, but to the realms of Devas, Rishis, and the Solar system, that person is that medium. You may call it a Guru or whatever you wish. Without understanding this, if you go somewhere, add ignorance to your efforts, and become owners of regretful karma, what will happen? You will become owners of a miserable karma that imparts blindness unto itself. If you pass this on to your children as well, what will they become?

I will only tell you what I have seen. Have no doubt about that. You must have unquestionable certainty in that. There is a truth of nature standing in this atmosphere that goes to the realm called the city of phantoms starting from the demons, teaches what the nature of the city of phantoms is, leaves that realm to ascend to the realm of Devas, from there ascends to the mandala of Rishis, from there ascends to the formless realm, and shows what the nature of the formless mandala is. Does it make any difference if I, you, or someone else says this exists or doesn't exist? This is in my experience. If you want, I can make you experience it too.

First, see all this. Then see what its original form is, what the cause of destruction is, through what all the destruction happened, and when and where that course of karma existed. But if we are to see, we must believe that there is a nature that shows all this. If we do not understand it in this way, we too will impart this same old mistake to the children growing behind us and die. With that, we are creating an opportunity for these same deranged souls to enter these children as well.

You will leave this atmosphere after being born, growing up, and working here for a while. The truth of having come and gone through countless births exists in this nature. To be certain that it exists, one must see it. Vision occurs in different states—waking (jagrat), dream (swapna), and deep sleep (sushupti). Just as you see in the waking state, you must see in the dream and deep sleep states. Where did you get the knowledge that you slept well during a sound sleep? It is the comfort your body received and the peace your soul attained. That knowledge convinced us even when we were asleep. If you ask a person who slept well how they saw it, what answer will they give? What kind of argument is this? Is it atheism or the argument that God exists? If it is the argument that God exists, first see that argument. Then we can see the argument that He does not exist. Thus, standing in the karma that everything exists, one must dissect and understand each one. Through whom can this be known? I am not saying this with the assumption that everyone can experience and know it. Even if one cannot see it, everyone can hear about it. Some can know this in their soul. This is a truth. There is a truth beyond this as well. We can know that truth only if we believe that this is true.

The knowledge and ignorance of countless souls, who followed and did not follow ancestral practices, are within us. We can distinguish between what is present and what is not only by keeping the life force within the body. Why can't we just chop off the bodies of those Vedantins who say that the body is non-existent, that it is perishable, and therefore an illusion (Maya)? The body is non-existent, after all. Then why should one rub, bathe, and cover it to carry it around! Where will the scholar who splits words, interprets them, and makes us believe by saying 'Swaha', and the ignorant person ultimately reach!

A person you believe in. Only if we attain an experiential doctrine equivalent to the one this person has actively established with their life and body—brought about knowingly or unknowingly, through learning or not learning, by the virtue of their soul—can we too become acquainted with that doctrine.

I will not say that everyone can see and know this. Because, in what all ways have our ancestors passed on their innate tendencies (vasanas)! The unfortunate plight cultivated by desiring various things, born and raised as a remainder of those vasanas, remains in the soul. Such a soul may not necessarily have the inclination to know this.

The inclination to get acquainted with that doctrine will come only through believing the person who created this doctrine. Believing in a deity (Deva) will not make it happen. Because the souls that worshipped the deity died, became ghosts, and will stand around this manifesting deity. What we need is a soul-body (subtle energy) residing inside that deity which can remove this ghost for us. Then we will be able to see that subtle body, the subtle body of the ghost surrounding it, and the soul-body residing inside all of them by bestowing good merit (sukrutham) upon them all. It is seen in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states, or in the present, past, and future times. This is a karma that remains connected to our soul just as it is in nature.

You should not assume that this acquaintance is meant for asceticism (sanyasa). This must grow in you, who are family people, and evolve into the greatest performer of action, the greatest follower of dharma, and an action-potential brimming with the greatest greatness. You must understand this while you are still alive. Then, you and God, or having been convinced of that word as truth, you should accept that truth as your Guru. But this equation is not true for all gurus. Whichever individual becomes true in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states, that individual should be accepted as the Guru. That person who accepts all the flawless and flawed karmas inscribed in your soul and inscribes that which is truth back into your soul, is your Guru. There is no other justification for this.

Sri Krishna is a person born before the beginning of the Kali Yuga. What all has happened through the life of Sri Krishna! Why did Sri Krishna run such a great race? He ran all over India. History says he ran, stood on another shore, and managed to build Dwarka. As soon as Dwarka was built, he was hit by an arrow. It is said to be a mistake made by a hunter. Anyway, he fell down. Even Arjuna, who won great victories, became helpless. Sri Krishna tells that Arjuna, "Arjuna, at least transport these children and women across the continent and save them." Have any scholars been ready to tell us this truth and set things right? Instead, we have been taught an inexperienced illusion (Maya Vilasam). We must see what the purpose of this trick by the scholars is. To speak the truth about a soul, shouldn't this scholar have experience? If one repeatedly says "not this, not this" without faith, it will only become like a kind of nihilism (Shoonyavada). If your mind's distress goes into that emptiness, won't you also become empty? What is the use of such nihilism and the karma that imparts emptiness? This is not what I am telling you.

A karmic trajectory that has crossed crores of years—born, died, worshipped, and made to worship, knowingly or unknowingly by our ancestors—permeates this atmosphere. It is a special energy dissolved in the air, fire, water, sand, and dust. God for us is the Guru who shapes and manifests this special energy. How is this formed? How this energy was in the earth, in the sky, in the water, and likewise in the five elements; knowing it through the five senses, touching and seeing it with the mind, and where the five sheaths (Pancha Koshas) operated within the magnitude of the five senses—it is not easy for us to figure this out. Because our soul's innate tendency (vasana) is not that high. Thus, if the mistakes and right actions seen yesterday are to be shown to us, there must be a foundation stone for it. It must be a soul-stone (Atma Shila). Atmanatma-niveditham—there must be a karma-purified one who offers the soul with the soul. Without going through him, we cannot formulate this.

The doctrine of Shantigiri is the Guru who makes this formation happen through experience. You yourselves must see what this Guru, who is this doctrine, can do. The meaning of what has been said is that you yourselves must see that karma which blends the past, the present, and the future things yet to come, across the waking, dream, and deep sleep states, and pours them into our souls. He who sees this as truth makes this formation happen. Moreover, one must see all the struggles, wickedness, glory, humility, respect, and greatness of the soul. There, one must see what one's Guru stands as. If we are to be able to get close to this Guru, we need an acquaintance to see what that karma was, where the snow that caused Sri Krishna's Dwarka to sink became rain, and then turned into water.

Where was this snow in ancient times! It was here even without anyone creating it. This is the magnificence of nature. The real story regarding Sri Krishna is that this snow, which was so hard that it could only be broken by shooting it, melted into water drops, mixed with whatever there was to mix, raised the water level, and submerged everything. A Guru is needed to know in detail about such a great soul. If one ever says anything denying the Guru, everything will be lost. How foolish is it to say that one will only think and act logically. How can a person, who is in the unfortunate state of not even knowing who his own father is, logically decipher these matters that are beyond thought and vast as the sky? There is a very ancient ignorance within us regarding this logical reasoning. The Guru is the one who points out this ignorance and eliminates it.

You have no experience of being taught such matters at the time of your birth. Instead, what have we been taught? That a mere vision of God is sufficient for everything. We stand upon this foundation of ignorance. Even if God were to manifest not once, but a thousand times, there is nothing to be gained. For any true realization to occur, one must reach a state where the soul is offered as an oblation to the soul itself. The one who enables such a transformation is the Atmaguru!

If one wishes to tell another, "I slept well yesterday," it must be an experience they have personally had. What can be done if one claims not to possess that experience? It is "I" who states that I slept. Therefore, the concept of "I" is present there. That perceived "I" is the Dharma—not separate from oneself—existing in a state of cessation, possessing an imperishable nature, and residing in the action of the form of sound. You must reclaim this discernment. Just as the sound we produce and hear eventually dissolves into the atmosphere, nature captures an imprint of the actions we perform both individually and collectively. Similarly, the truths—both good and bad—worshipped and propagated by our ancestors remain intertwined within this nature. The life force clinging to my body is merely the residue of countless lifetimes that have manifested, vanished, and acted consciously and unconsciously over an immense expanse of time. We can attain this knowledge solely through a Guru. Whether one encounters a deity or a demon, my Guru will be present there. Toddy, rice gruel water, and milk may share the same color; the differences lie only marginally in their form and essence. One must learn to distinguish these subtleties. This comprehension is impossible without a Guru. Thus, a Guru must be someone who has traversed through all that is good and all that is evil. No matter what absurdity is witnessed, one must be able to perceive their Guru amidst it. In this manner, we are shown the paths that the Guru has traversed. Ultimately, one must observe what they transform into when themselves, the Guru, and the perceived objects all dissolve and merge into one.

By revealing a formless essence within nature—where all demonic forces are subsumed—one must perceive the entity that endures as the ultimate truth in this formless state as the Guru. This is precisely why it is stated that a Guru is essential. Does the Guru reside exclusively within the good? No. The Guru is present in both the good and the evil. Otherwise, who would absorb your impurities? One must perceive within themselves a formless power manifesting as a form, remaining unblemished and without losing mental equanimity, realizing and imparting the knowledge that it is in no way evil. That is to say, the Guru is fundamentally formless, yet simultaneously possesses a form.

Jagrat (the waking state) and Swapna (the dream state). Whatever is perceived in the waking state is subsequently experienced in the dream state and in Sushupti (deep sleep). It is Turiya (the fourth state of consciousness) and Turiyatita (the state beyond the fourth) that reveal the intricacies of the variations in forms and names. The Guru represents the absolute totality of action that elucidates and differentiates these five distinct states of consciousness.

What was the nature of the deity during the era of the deities, and what was the role of the sage (Rishi) then? Who are these sages diverging into the four paths of the ritualist (Karmi), the mystic (Yogi), the seeker of knowledge (Jnani), and the devotee (Bhakta)? What is the relationship between such a sage and one's Guru? How are the attributes of bygone sages and deities reflected in my Guru? The Guru is the embodied knowledge that discerns and elucidates the authentic essence of all deities spanning the Shaiva, Shakta, and Vaishnava traditions, the true forms of Ghatotkacha hurling serpents with a thousand hands, and Goddess Durga—and transcending all these, reveals the manifold virtues of a soul devoid of gender distinctions. All of these profound realities must culminate in our direct experience.

Here, this profound experience does not belong to the offspring brought from my household; rather, it belongs to your children, husbands, and wives. It is subsequently transmitted to their descendants, eventually attaining a state of permanence. Thus, it is the love rooted in faith in the Guru that is being instilled within you. The formless essence that pervades and empowers all manifested forms within nature belongs to the Guru. It is nature itself that reveals this reality. This Guru is the one who characterises and demonstrates to us the nature of that eternal power from bygone eras. Guided by that vision, we continue to progress forward.

What constitutes the evolutionary transformation of our life force? Through what all has it intricately woven its way? This must be perceived through the soul. True knowledge is the wisdom reflected synergistically by the life force and the soul residing within this physical body. The life force and the soul exist within you. How does one recognize this? If the trajectory of action required to reclaim this realization is absent within us, we will be left utterly bewildered. Our faith constitutes the resolute firmness required to actualize this experience. At times, my Guru may appear virtuous; at other times, he may seem like an unparalleled scoundrel. Yet, he remains my Guru. I shall acknowledge all of these facets. This is the ultimate steadfastness of faith. One cannot simply take a Guru somewhere to be cleansed, purified, and rectified. What scientist, what proponent of liberation can ever assert that such love, such a profoundly deep connection, does not exist?

Direct experience is the most profound bond; it is the ultimate love. It is beyond comparison. The experiences encountered in the Jagrat (waking), Swapna (dream), and Sushupti (deep sleep) states constitute the exclusive domain of the Guru. No one else will be able to comprehend them. Therefore, such matters should be disclosed only to the Guru. One will witness the good, the evil, and the absurd. The Guru serves as the sole medium to question why one has been led into the ignorance of such absurdities. The philosophy underpinning our faith is the spiritual oblation (Atmanivedana) that unifies one's life force and vital breath (Prana) as one, after traversing through all these dualities sequentially. It is certainly not Vedanta. The assertion that the Katha Upanishad dictates one thing or another Upanishad dictates something else—none of this constitutes the true philosophy of our existence. The Upanishads are merely the documented personal experiences of various individuals. Can interpreting and expounding upon them ever constitute true spiritual realization?

The witness to the Jagrat (waking), Swapna (dream), and Sushupti (deep sleep) states. The Guru represents the ultimate culmination of action (Karmapoorthi)—encompassing all that we have worshipped or neglected to worship with this witness as our focal point, the good we have acknowledged or remained ignorant of, the circumstances arising through special destiny, and the spiritual heritage nurtured collectively by the Guru, oneself, and one's lineage.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarpana Edition 2002
What the Believers Must Know

I have never performed any magic tricks before you. I have not exhibited any special mystical powers (Siddhis). Whatever is pleasing to God, that must transpire. The exact will of God has been revealed to us. Several among you have also been convinced that this is the absolute truth. However, how do you conduct yourselves with one another? You are individuals who constantly quarrel among yourselves, as if bereft of the capacity to utter a single kind word. When one arrives at the threshold of a virtue that, through the sheer majesty of a benevolent word, could be transmitted to the younger generation, the community, the household, and the nation—what inevitably accompanies you is strife. The conflict escalates to its fullest extent and then dissolves into sheer nothingness.

If those residing in the Ashram fail to comprehend the spiritual ethos of the Ashram, then for what purpose am I toiling? If, having arrived as believers, you do not assimilate the intrinsic nature of the Ashram through seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and tasting, not only will you remain ignorant of this path, but you will also ultimately tear apart and discard the fragments of knowledge you have gathered from various sources, thereby straying entirely from the path of faith. Have you not witnessed countless individuals abandoning this place in such a manner?

What is attainable here can only be acquired through sheer endurance. When one examines the reasons behind your quarrels, it becomes evident that there is absolutely no valid justification for them. You do not even practice the foundational virtue of forgiveness. You will only comprehend the heights to which patience can elevate you if you actively practice it. As far as Sannyasa (renunciation) is concerned, there is scarcely a need to speak of patience. Honor and dishonor are treated as equals (Manapamaname thulyam). That is to say, before the ideals of Sannyasa, both honor and disgrace hold no significance. Relinquishing both, whatever one receives in the contemplation of the Divine, that alone must be accepted. Beyond this, there is no alternative justification to be sought. You engage in various antics under the misguided assumption that life merely consists of the superficial displays inherent to materialistic existence.

There is a sect known as the Lingayats. They are individuals who do not wear clothing. I have read in newspapers that they occasionally enter the parliament and cause disruptions. They number in the thousands. When they arrive, it becomes impossible for others to remain in that vicinity. Thus, how many varied followers of spiritual paths exist in India alone! However, one should not presume that adopting these paths will lead to the ultimate truth. To lead one to the truth, an individual who has intimately experienced the truth must arrive. For this, forests, mountains, women, or men do not constitute an obstacle, as it is a matter of profound fortune. Even if one were to wander the entire globe in pursuit of the truth, it is not guaranteed to be discovered. Conversely, even if it is in your immediate proximity, you may remain oblivious to it. If individuals residing in the ashram fail to comprehend the ashram's environment, what else can possibly be said to such individuals?

There is an adage that to determine the purity of gold, one must bring it to a touchstone; bringing it to a grinding stone will not reveal its true value. This implies that you must engage intimately and act to rectify your own flaws. One must utilize their knowledge to repair the defective aspects of their being. If one lacks the knowledge to preserve seeds without them spoiling, three-quarters of those seeds will invariably perish. Similarly, you are individuals who have squandered your lives without prudent preservation. You fail to comprehend even the accomplishments achieved within your own home in the broader context of your household, society, and the nation.

Many among you had proven to be rightful heirs to this fortune (experience) even before encountering me. It has also been demonstrated to each of you what the necessity of this experience entails. Despite comprehending this, you refrain from embracing it. Even though God has provided an opportunity to profoundly understand the knowledge bestowed upon you, the requisite action to honor it does not manifest within you. Why do I insist that this must be imparted to your children? It is not solely for your benefit, but to ensure that this society receives whatever it is destined to gain from you.

You possess love and faith. I acknowledge that. Your affection and trust towards me have no boundaries. Even if boundaries were set, the Divine would eradicate them. Although you may lack purity of soul, you harbor the thought that nothing contrary to this ideal you believe in should emanate from my side. Those who stood with me continue to leave, one by one. Those who depart stand aside and claim they bear no enmity towards the Swami. When asked why they leave, they attribute it to the actions of others. Do you come to the ashram merely to observe others? These others are individuals with their own rights, wrongs, and flaws, much like yourselves. Consequently, they will act and cause actions in accordance with that nature. You must recognize that it is partly your responsibility to prevent such alienation from occurring. Blaming others is not the appropriate recourse. They might have acted according to their level of understanding. I am not suggesting that you should undertake the task of reforming them. However, if you comprehend the situation, there is no harm in gently and affectionately advising them against such actions. Do not inflict pain by using substandard words. I articulate this because there exists within you a tendency that does not hesitate to hurt others.

Can anyone—whether those who stood close to me or those who later departed citing various reasons—utter a single word claiming that this is not the truth? I am not referring to those who have had a brief association with me. If those with less familiarity display displeasure, they cannot be faulted. If those who possess an association spanning twenty or thirty years are unable to assimilate this in profound accordance with their tenure and affection, and if those who witness it with their own eyes and harbor immense personal devotion cannot sustain it within their own homes, what is the point of blaming others?

Knowledge exists, but there is an absence of true understanding where it is required. This is the essence of a Shudra state of mind. If you are educated, you will tend to evaluate things from the standpoint of your acquired learning. If, instead of demonstrating humility, you exhibit the arrogance of a learned person, you will be unable to internalize this experience. Is the subject matter here something that can be guided by a salvationist, a rationalist, an atheist, a wealthy individual, a scholar, or a Vedantic philosopher?

It is easy to speak of truth, compassion, and empathy. However, do we possess the action required to unify these virtues? The essence of this truth is being demonstrated to you as your rightful inheritance. Yet, you fail to recognize it. Our knowledge is entirely directed towards claiming ownership over children, wife, husband, wealth, and education. I have never instructed you to abandon or refrain from acquiring any of these. I have never asked you to forsake your home, nor abandon men or women. What I am stating is this: you diminish yourselves concerning the profound knowledge residing deep within your minds. I have imparted this very understanding to the experienced children who stand beside me. This is a subject attained through immense struggle. However, I have reiterated to you a hundred times that I have not struggled for it presently. I have done nothing for it in the present time. It is exceedingly ancient. It was Buddha who calculated and stated that he attained numerous lifetimes where that state of philosophical vision was sustained—five hundred incarnations where the state of vision endured. An argumentative nature that denies all this may be considered acceptable; however, the truth remains that such individuals are incapable of achieving anything significant. If each of you were to contemplate in this manner, the nobility inherent in that knowledge would enter your minds, and you would begin to externally manifest what true nobility is. That is the experience you have received.

I possess no mystical powers, nor do I engage in speaking in tongues. Nevertheless, I possess the ability to articulate the actions occurring within each of your homes. These are actions that remain incomprehensible to others, even if they were to see, hear, or learn of them. Having understood it in this manner, and recognizing that this is the highest of Dharmas and that no greater Dharma is yet to emerge, you can embrace it with the utmost courage. The predicament faced by those who departed from here is entirely due to their failure to comprehend this reality.

We must transform the actions residing within our minds. How can you, who have solely learned to berate and criticize others, accept this? Is this not akin to the egoistic grasp of politicians? Scholars, on the other hand, will enumerate the names of numerous books and merely unearth their deepest roots to present to you. Entangled in such individual traps, we remain ignorant of how to properly honor this. Why do I articulate my experience to you in such exhaustive detail, akin to an open book? It is with the intention that if even one or two among the many who happen to encounter these words comprehend it, they might honor it, disseminate it to the public, and internalize that action as their own. That action is not for me. Yet, in another sense, it indeed is for me. Whatever you do will ultimately reach me. For when the authority of a Dharma has been established, I must not declare that it does not belong to me.

It is the Divine that has granted you the opportunity to accomplish this. It was by understanding Buddha in this manner that Emperor Ashoka renounced everything and set forth for this cause. He sacrificed both of his children for the sake of the ideology. Why did he undertake all these actions? Being an emperor and possessing a refined culture of that magnitude, he comprehended it. He demonstrated to us the requisite qualification on how to strive, sacrifice, and propagate it. What destiny awaits us, who are incapable of even contemplating such matters? If you are to uproot the inherited flaws deeply entrenched within you, and should you attain this, you must be prepared to contemplate solely upon it, cultivate it, and handle it in accordance with true knowledge. I convey this to you after having introduced the illumination that the subject of experience has offered thus far. It would be immensely beneficial if you cultivate at least a habit of contemplating how to assimilate this truth. However, one thing remains certain: even if you become acquainted with this knowledge, you will be unable to embrace it if you fail to preserve the truth.

Sacrifice possesses an inherent glory. It is not intended to display greatness. Whoever receives this in their hands must honor it. This is the greatest of fortunes. It is so because it is the path of liberation that rectifies the errors accumulated over numerous *yugas* (epochs).

What am I essentially telling you? By analyzing a vast period beyond *yugas*, I am highlighting the true aspects of the lives of the Gurus who appeared solely in this *Kaliyuga* and presenting them to you. If the children growing up before you make an error in even a single word contrary to this ideal, it must be corrected immediately. Otherwise, it would signify a lack of humility towards the truth. Furthermore, this ideal will depart from your household. If you are blessed with the fortune to receive the fullness of God, you must undertake that *karma* at any cost. This is neither for renunciation nor for acquiring dominance. Emperor Ashoka did not embrace this to attain dominance, did he? His intention was to bring benevolence to his kingdom through his and his children's *karma*. He was a man who had acquired sufficient wealth. Even after Ashoka demonstrated such immense glory of sacrifice, what could the subsequent subjects or vassal kings achieve here?

You must be able to contemplate this at such a profound level. This can be accomplished only if there is love for God. If there is a conviction that the *karma* within us, which causes us to flourish and perish, rests upon that glory of God, then executing this becomes our necessity.
Guru Vani
Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Commemorative Edition 2002
The Truth Realized Through Experience

The path of prophetic vision is profound. The prophetic vision of a *yuga* is fulfilled through five Gurus. The influence of each Guru intermingles with the others. The fifth Guru is one who arrives to reveal the characteristics of the forthcoming *yuga* as well. However, the influence of the fourth individual will also be blended into the influence of this fifth individual. That influence will persist until the person of the next *yuga* assumes it. A mistake that can occur during such an assumption is that if the fifth individual, upon observing the truth of the past, makes an error while evaluating the stance of that truth in their own era, everything thereafter will be entirely flawed. Since the *yuga* is changing, there is a possibility of making mistakes. This is how Sathyathranan erred. That mistake was repeated by numerous Gurus who came subsequently. If inexperienced thinkers write about this, a perspective blending the Western mode of thought and Eastern prophetic vision will result.

Among the four *yugas*, *Kaliyuga* has the shortest duration. The chronology determines that *Kaliyuga* itself lasts for four hundred and thirty-two thousand years. *Dwapara* is twice the duration of *Kali*. When *Kali* is added to *Dwapara*, it becomes *Treta Yuga*. When *Kali* is added to *Treta Yuga*, it forms *Krita Yuga*, also known as *Satya Yuga*.

In a *yuga*, a visionary who perceives all this, along with individuals resembling prophets, sages, or Gurus functioning under them, will emerge and operate. When referring to a visionary who observes all this, Sri Krishna can be cited as an example. Before Sri Krishna's birth, royal status was bestowed upon the Yadava clan. Kamsa's downfall was his inability to fully comprehend its significance. However, Kamsa cannot be entirely blamed either. He failed to understand the manifested form that was declared in accordance with the *Yuga Dharma*.

This manifested form is referred to as *Rupapadam*. One can only proceed by relying on the feet of that form. It is the lesser Gurus arriving in that period's influence who completely attain this *Rupapadam*. The divine voice (*ashareeri*) that Kamsa heard was formed as a command from the divine will (*Brahmasankalpa*) to proclaim Sri Krishna's birth prior to it. One can only function by prophetically envisioning and imbibing the Gurus who manifested in the past and brought forth *karma*. Regardless of how great a poet or philosopher one is, numerous doubts will arise. At such times, one can only rely on the *Rupapadam* of the visionary.

The reverence required to reflect upon the reason for delivering a divine voice prior to the visionary's birth, and the quality generated by that reverence, cannot be determined by certain Gurus. For the Guru appearing at the beginning of a *yuga* and those coming intermittently, starting and operating from those divine feet necessitates examining the doctrines of those who came before them.

Sri Krishna is the Guru born between the end of *Dwapara* and the beginning of *Kali*. Gurus appearing under the influence of two thousand, three thousand, five thousand, or ten thousand years associated with these divine feet have nothing to retain or offer here. In this state, it became impossible to comprehend who a visionary is. How much can even the primal Guru who originated a religious doctrine declare? At most, only up to a realization. Realization implies the manifested *dharma*. The form and nature of this manifested *dharma* is not displayed as the form and nature of the immediately preceding *yuga*, but as the form and nature of the *Yuga Dharma*. It commences as one. Sri Krishna arrived by unifying numerous doctrines together. The Gurus coming under him are supposed to elaborate and demonstrate those events.

The temporal determination of each *manvantara* will vary. However, it is not sufficient to merely observe the change in time. One must also examine whether there is an error in the determination of *karma*. Our understanding is that the seventh Manu, Vaivasvata Manu, has also completely executed the determination of *karma*. Similarly, five Gurus appeared for each *yuga* and repeatedly fulfilled all the *Yuga Dharmas*. Documenting and executing the prophetic vision to be expounded in the respective *yugas* is also the very same *karma*. In the *Yuga Dharma*, this *karma* also stands distinct with an image. It is from this that any error occurring anywhere in a *manvantara* can be identified.
For such an identification, seven Gurus will emerge under each of the aforementioned five Gurus.

Sri Krishna came in the capacity of a visionary for numerous such Gurus. Due to the inability to determine *karma* and error in this context, the poet's mode of exposition diverts into another direction. The incident of Sri Krishna opening his mouth to reveal the universe represents this divergently expounded *karma*. It is said that he opened his mouth and showed it to Devaki and Yashoda. Is that the truth of the event?

The history of seven children being beaten to death caused countless emotions of sorrow to flow together for Devaki and Vasudeva. From the time of Sri Krishna's inception, great souls had provided visions to the mother and father, explaining why the eighth child was being born and what all he would accomplish, thus resolving their doubts. The corresponding conviction and courage continued to instill within them. Otherwise, how could a mother and father wait in such a manner and partake in sorrow?

These matters are not to come from the hands of scholars. Nor do they belong in the hands of the great sages who repeatedly appeared under the deities. The gurus who have come and gone from the time of Sree Krishna to the present day belong to periods ranging from two thousand, three thousand, five thousand, to ten thousand years. We see stories of many gurus who appeared in India itself making immense efforts to acquire spiritual powers (siddhis). Writing down stories based on the imaginative conceptions of gods and goddesses, calling them eternal (Sanatana) and so on, disrupts the Yugadharma (the dharma of the epoch). The trinity of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva belongs to the imagination of forest dwellers fabricated in this manner. Those referred to as Adam and Eve also belong to the category of prophets. All of this is stated based on the culture of each land at that time. How much faltering has occurred within these two thousand years to the Christian laws that speak of the old and the new! Can we recognize the life of Christ and the return of Moses today? What is the return? Even after whipping and driving the people who were completely lost in polytheism and bringing them to this side of the Red Sea, the calf's head still remains under their arms!

Gita Govindam and the concept of Meera are examples of the imaginative excellence of poetic assemblies. Both the intellectuals and the unintelligent here hang onto the imaginative splendor of these poetic concepts. Through alphabetical interpretations ranging from the Shabdataravali to the Amarakosha, which purifies vowels and consonants, even Sree Rama is being showcased. The entire population of the world is hanging onto the part that says 'Amara Nirjara Deva'. This chain of hypocrisy has spread and climbed even among the authors of the Vedas and epics, and the authors of the Upanishads. It must be assumed that even the prophets have not been able to recognize this hypocrisy. There is no point in forgetting the truth that we cannot comprehend the blunders that may befall us by getting caught in the path of action, which is praised by combining terms like avatar, guru, and prophet. The blunder that occurred when Sree Krishna was praised in this manner is proof of this. The exact same situation has occurred in the case of Moses as well. It is by adding a bit more imagination that things are said about Jesus: when it was said, 'Let the rock split and move apart', it moved. How should we view the ignorance of the disciples who could not obey the instruction to pray until three in the morning, and the question at the final stage of that life, 'Father, why have you forsaken me?' In what way and by what kind of person should the determination of faith of the Sikh gurus and the divine law residing in the atomic concept of the Jains be corrected?
Mine is the path of an unlettered scholarship, where the answers to these cannot be found through the mere knowledge of alphabets. This is the error I had to face.

It was the time I was performing poojas at Aluva Advaita Ashram. Then, there were some thoughtful people who would come there, enjoy the beauty of nature, sit in the courtyard on the northern side of the ashram, talk about many things as if passing the day, be lost in thought, and spend time writing poetry according to their intellect. I too have often gotten involved in that path of action. Many of them were studying at Aluva UC College at that time. I also had an acquaintance where I stayed away from the knowledge and thoughtfulness of these young men, while at the same time understanding many of their characteristics and enjoying their company. One among them was Narendran, who later became a High Court Judge. The rest of them I recognized during my ashram life. Among them was Chandrabhanu and some others. At that time, there was an Ayurvedic clinic on the way from Palayam to Chempazhanthy through the church cemetery. They used to gather there. The special nature of their good imagination has filled my mind with love. This sweet feeling is still in my mind. One of them later became a sanyasi. When I built a hut in Varkala, I called this sanyasi as if it were a thought. Then his response was like this: 'Whatever is built for Karunakaran is not enough. He has to build his own' . Later, when a hut was built in Pothencode, this person happened to come there too. Before coming to Pothencode, I had asked him an experiential question. To that, he asked me a counter-question brimming with humor: 'Karunakaran has a lot of questions, right?' But after that, I got the proof for this question of mine from a rogue soldier named Pattalam Ramakrishnan. He is the one who revealed the things about Sree Krishna, the eternal celibate Hanuman, and the Brahmarakshas that came to disrupt Vasishta's yagam during Sree Rama's time. Isn't this enough proof that a scholar dressed as a sanyasi does not even have as much knowledge as an experienced devil? Let that be.

The narrative has been constructed to claim that Sri Rama descended into the Sarayu river and attained *jalasamadhi* (spiritual salvation in water). Does this imply that *samadhi* cannot be attained on land? Why was such a fabricated tale recorded? Similarly, Ramatirtha is also said to have attained *jalasamadhi*! If one asks for what purpose, there is no response. If it is argued that they simply renounced this life, then what becomes of the *karma* they accrued through their existence and the power of their penance? These great figures did not merely renounce life; rather, they were led astray. When they realized and were convinced that their path had gone astray, they were confounded—what have I been doing all this while? I need this no longer. The truth is that they simply abandoned it. This is what the Prophet meant when he asked: "What have you done to me, who trusted only in you?" It is for this exact reason that Jesus lamented, "Father, have you too forsaken me?" Did these great souls utter these words without reason?

The souls existing as *Brahmarakshasas* do not enter *Brahmaloka*. They are the ones who performed severe penance, as if standing on the point of a needle. Why does God give birth to a great soul? It is not merely for his own spiritual attainment. Rather, it is to simultaneously fulfill his inherent *dharma*. In contrast, what does Vedanta proclaim? That everything is *maya* (illusion), the *maya* of the Lord. Consequently, the masses were rendered incapable of understanding anything. This is not *maya*; it is reality itself. What one must understand is how to deal with this reality.

The established system of worship remains subordinate to the deities who manifested during the *Treta Yuga* and *Dvapara Yuga*. During those epochs, human beings were incapable of independent action. In the *Kali Yuga*, man is born with agency. It was in such a context that Sri Krishna appeared. Thus, Krishna, who manifested as the primordial Guru (*Adi Guru*), has been depicted merely as a philanderer. It is for this precise reason that the *Gita Govinda* was composed. We merely translate and interpret its meanings. I have not formally studied any of these commentaries. However, I know for a certainty that this is not the truth.

Due to the failure to truly comprehend Sri Krishna, this nation was plunged into ruin. How many Gurus emerged after Sri Krishna! The Buddha, Mahavira, and Guru Nanak appeared. The *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* (twelve clans born of the Pariah woman) and the eighteen *Siddhas* manifested. Did all these figures appear merely for the sake of singing praises? Yet, we failed to obey even a single one of them. What was the underlying cause of Sri Narayana Guru's sorrow during his final days? His grief stemmed from the fact that there was not a single disciple capable of taking up this mantle. There was no one left to perceive this as the ultimate truth. I am not stating this merely to inform others. I am compelled to articulate the truth that I have witnessed.

Furthermore, having categorically divided traditions into the *Trimurti* system and the *Manu* system, we have been instructed by portraying Manu as the son of Brahma. Is this indeed the truth? Manu is *Swayambhu* (self-manifested). It is the self-manifested Manu who has been inaccurately depicted as Brahma's son. This is mere intellectual gymnastics with words. This is the profound fallacy that has befallen us. No one has been able to transcend this error. Gurus who emerge with the spiritual influence of two thousand, five thousand, or ten thousand years are powerless to rectify this misconception. Divine sanction is absolutely necessary to correct this. What must we do to attain this divine sanction? One must manifest in accordance with the *Yuga Dharma* (the law of the epoch). Having thus manifested, one can only depart after elevating *Dharma* to its rightful state.

I have not acquired formal academic learning. Had I been formally educated, I would not possess the capacity to definitively state what the truth is. However, I can now declare that this is the absolute truth. Once it is affirmed as the truth, one must perceive the profound secret underlying that truth. It is the disciple's duty to perceive this. When Sri Narayana Guru lamented that there was no child left to inherit his legacy, it signified that there was no disciple capable of perceiving the inner secret of the truth. Instead, what do people claim? That he exhibited miraculous powers (*siddhis*), alongside propagating various Vedantic mysteries. Where do we currently stand? If we continue along this trajectory, what shall become of the profound knowledge inherent in our tradition? Rather than rejecting traditional wisdom, one must attain a profound realization of reality and translate it into direct experience. No alternative path will lead to our salvation.

Where do we stand within the framework of *karma* that the *Trimurti* system has conveniently defined as creation, preservation, and destruction? We must cultivate the capacity to comprehend this. To achieve this understanding, we must reach that specific state of realization. Having observed this, one must discern whether it is the *Manu* lineage, the Guru lineage, or the *Rishi* lineage that is truly qualified to perceive it. Subsequently, one must investigate why the *Rishi* lineage failed to attain it, and why the lineage of Prophets was unable to advance further. Unless spiritual liberation is granted to those *Rishis*, Prophets, and Gurus who remain stagnated, incapable of progressing further, no individual can transcend to that ultimate state.

We have established a practice of worshipping everyone. However, apart from merely offering worship, it is impossible to ascertain the specific spiritual plane (*mandala*) in which these deities exist. It is precisely from the plane where they reside that we fail to ascend. Consequently, we fail to derive any spiritual merit from the astrological sign (*rashi*) in which we are born. Unless this condition is liberated, no true benevolence can be attained. This profound act of liberation constitutes the true essence of *Guru Pooja*.

Therefore, one must cultivate a profound understanding of the Guru. Having realized this, one must inquire: what is the true nature of the Guru, and what elements converge within this Guru? Everything referred to as a *Brahmarakshasa*, a *Trimurti*, or a Prophet must ultimately merge within this Guru. That is the true essence of a Guru. It is futile to underestimate anyone. Everyone has contributed to the utmost of their capabilities. Do you genuinely believe that these great souls departed without realizing the exact spiritual state they had attained? They departed with full awareness. Yet, they find themselves unable to progress further. Your intellectual pursuit must be directed toward formulating a *karma* that enables them to advance. That should constitute your paramount sense of duty. If you choose to conceal yourself behind the veil of ignorance propagated by individuals uttering '*Swaha*' or preaching *Advaita*, you will remain incapable of fulfilling your fundamental duty. Let no one harbor the illusion that spiritual attainment is possible without first loving and spiritually liberating our ancestors. That is simply an impossibility.

I am not propounding any complex Vedantic calculations. Rather, I am elucidating the fundamental principles necessary to safeguard the masses within the realm of true knowledge. Instead of protecting the people, are we not merely thrusting them into a bottomless abyss while blindly reciting *suktas* and endlessly reiterating literal, pedantic interpretations?
