Imparting of Knowledge in the Form of Guru and Disciple

The word 'experience' has a very vast magnitude of meaning. We have the knowledge of experience ranging from installing *Madan* (a local deity) and calling him Lord. If *Madan* or any other such deities are assigned the position of a god and called Lord, those who do so will never reach the position of God. Moreover, those who intensely perform *poojas* and worship by swaying and shaking like demons might attain certain direct experiences and some special mystic powers capable of bewildering people and leading them into blindness, but their souls will become more degraded than that of an unbeliever who considers saying they have no faith as a matter of prestige. I have been able to see this as the greatest evidence in my belief. There are people with another kind of devotion. They are the group who make vows and offerings, perform frantic dances, buy elephants and offer them to the temple, conduct *kuthirayeduppu* (horse effigy procession), and organize *Padakam*, *Harikatha*, and *Kathaprasangam* (storytelling performances) for wealth and the accomplishment of other matters. Then there is another group of devotees who, out of extreme devotion, get some minor visions which then increase, and when a *Yogeeswaran*, *Manthramoorthi*, or *Bhadrakali* lying dead and suppressed in the family stands strong, they do something or the other until their death to make people believe. The family members then turn him into a favorite deity or a favorite *Yogeeswaran* and make him the family deity. Due to such practices, that family itself will wander and become bankrupt after one or two generations. Moreover, they will be subjected to a great sin.

There is a reason for writing and revealing this. Among the many thousands of such families who come to me, I am only able to eradicate the sinful power of ninety-nine percent. The reason why the sinful power of some remaining cases could not be eradicated is that they suffer from the greatest of major diseases or have gone mad with an incurable manic nature. It is incurable and hereditary in the family.

If we examine it this way, we might wonder if there is anything real. Yes, there is God who transcends the magnitude of what was mentioned earlier. A God who cannot be confined in a temple or within the limits of *nirmalya* rituals. In some families, there are some ancestors (*Pitrus*) like sacrificing great souls who have maintained honesty throughout their lives and managed to reach at least the position of a *Brahmarakshas*. In later times, some children will be born in that family in the zodiac sign where such ancestors reside. Even if that child does not become spiritually realized, they will be mature enough to perform good deeds without caring about the aforementioned artificial practices and liberate those ancestors. If it is a girl, there will be a lot of goodness. If it is a girl, she only needs to be helped in the act of granting liberation. Ancestors who attain liberation in this way can show some visionary paths to a woman or a man and make them a good devotee or a wise person. Otherwise, they will at least make them a fallen yogi or a wealthy person.

The most superior path than all of this is to find a wise Guru. If a Guru is found, one will be able to attain spiritual merit (*Atmasukrutham*) at least to the extent of the fortune of their soul. All these things mentioned might perhaps seem negative to those who are not spiritually realized. Therefore, I desire that the idea for a good path becomes clear to the people. In a state filled with ignorance born out of the lack of love, not just of our land but of the world itself, and some barbaric idiocies of enjoying making money through savagery, even if you do not read such things, you should try to seek a good path that helps to bring firmness in virtue and the fortune acquired through karma.
Disciple: Guru! If you summarize this subject like this, we who are ignorant do not know how to take it. We also do not know how to grasp it through the words of a wise person.
Guru: The antiquity of the soul itself is necessary to grasp this subject through the words of a wise person.
Disciple: I have felt in many ways and situations that the antiquity of the soul is necessary. Still, we have an intense desire to know. Therefore, we wish to know it in detail.
Guru: Everything said earlier was about the antiquity of the soul itself. If doubt arises even now, what is to be done? Now, let me speak about what is meant by the antiquity of the soul.

Biology itself represents the evolutionary principle, consolidated and manifested completely in the macrocosm and atomically in the microcosm. The Hindu doctrine holds this as the eternal principle. This is the very foundation of the Puranas and epics. However, whether experienced or not, some scholars harbor doubts regarding certain illogical aspects of this doctrine. Therefore, they claim that what the sage Badarayana has written, what the four Vedas, the six Shastras, and the eighteen Puranas have unequivocally praised, and furthermore, the merit of the scholars' own research studies, are authoritative. They also employ a highly logical language for this purpose. Such scholars, who think solely through their own logic, will fail to recognize the truth in biology. At that point, they seek refuge in *Mayavada* (the doctrine of illusion). Yet, when *Mayavada* is subjected to logic, it essentially states that there is only one, not two (non-duality). Subsequently, clinging firmly to the truth that there is only one and not two, they introduce dialectics (*Tarkashastra*). Their peculiar logic is such that they can study and teach such dialectics for any length of time. Using ordinary Puranas and logical words, they illustrate this with the inference of mistaking a rope for a snake. If the one who gives this illustration sees a snake (let us assume it is a King Cobra) right in front of him, even if he dares to chase it away with courage and arrogance without fear, the snake will inevitably turn and bite if driven into a corner. The truth is that one cannot escape that snakebite without medicine, imagination, or knowledge. If he firmly clings to *Mayavada* with the force of his erudition and logic, will he remain unaffected by the venom? If there were a snake instead of a rope, and if one adopts some method to step aside without getting bitten or to destroy it, doesn't *Mayavada* become a hollow concept? The one who has studied dialectics, the scholar, and the ignoramus are all equal in this regard. However, a Sannyasin possesses certain esoteric techniques by which venom does not affect the body, regardless of which venomous snakes bite, let alone a King Cobra.
Question: What is it that you refer to as a technique (Vidya)? Doesn't the Sannyasin possess true wisdom (Jnana)?

Guru: What the Sannyasin possesses is indeed true wisdom (Jnana). That wisdom does not have a method of destroying or otherwise eliminating what is ordained by divine will. The wise one (Jnani) anticipates such matters in advance and adopts a path to escape from that event.
Question: There is history of massive snakes serving as an umbrella for Sannyasins, as well as history of them being companions to certain Sannyasins, is there not?

Guru: There is some truth to that as well. The reason for this is that most Sannyasins adopt disciplines belonging to the path of propitiation (*Upasana*). For instance, they are those who have attained occult powers (*Siddhis*) through actions—in thought, word, and deed—along the *Upasana* paths of Shaivism, Shaktism, and Vaishnavism, thereby acquiring the eightfold sovereign powers (*Ashtaishwarya Siddhi*) as a manifestly attainable state. Others do not do this; they adopt the path of *Kalpaseva*. This is a discipline that involves the consumption of substances, starting from various leaves up to the seeds of the Strychnine tree (*Kanjiram*). Furthermore, there is another discipline that involves the consumption of the nine poisons (*Navapashana*) prepared in various ways. During the period of such consumption, they reside inside a specially constructed cave with nine entrances. While consuming the medicine, this individual will be unable to stand or walk. Even the excretion of feces and urine will cease. There is a specific calculation that one must face a particular entrance during a particular watch (*Yama*). The accompanying disciples shift their position to face the respective entrances. The disciples would have been taught beforehand about the care to be administered during that time. By the time they attain the eight *Siddhis*, their body will return to its former state. Once this regulated regimen is applied to the body, it will no longer be afflicted by old age and graying hair. There is also a principle that even death will occur only when they desire it. Serpents can recognize those who have attained two or four of the eight *Siddhis*. Serpents possessing such recognition will immediately turn back upon seeing them without staying. Or, even if bitten by snakes belonging to an ignorant, wicked path, the venom will rebound upon the snake, merely resulting in the snake's death. All of this is not achieved in a single lifetime, but rather through paths adopted across multiple lifetimes in accordance with inherent tendencies (*Vasanas*). Upon attaining *Siddhis* in this manner, they exhibit various miraculous feats. Such *Siddhas* are often mistakenly perceived as truly wise (*Jnanis*).

Haven't you heard people asking whether a certain person is a *Siddha*? There are behavioral tendencies wherein people take pleasure in recounting various tales and anecdotes about Sannyasins who attain *Siddhis* in this manner. Such stories are particularly heard in southern Travancore. One such story goes like this:

In a certain place, there were two brothers. One was educated and a scholar. The other was uneducated and a fool. Both took turns guarding the banana plantation. One day, the uneducated one went to guard. Hearing hymns being chanted here and there, the elder brother approached and asked the younger brother how he had learned this. He replied that someone gave him two bananas, and the hymns dawned upon him when he ate them. The elder brother, who picked up and ate the banana peels from the base of the banana plant, also became a poet. There are people who believe even this. One has heard claims of seeing a Swami observed at one location simultaneously at another location. These are all illusions manifested through the application of *Gaunamani*, *Sthambhanamani*, and *Rasamani*. These are anomalies that occur in action when all of this is misinterpreted as true wisdom (*Jnana*). These are the paths we adopt.

Haven't you seen some people playing with snakes draped around their necks? If he has not extracted the fangs or kept medicine in hand, he has indeed plunged into a fatal error. There was an instance in Koorkanchery, Thrissur, where a person known as Pampu Swami used to walk around with a snake around his neck. None of this should be mistaken for true wisdom (*Jnana*). A true *Jnani* will not exhibit specialized *Siddhis*. Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa has stated that *Siddhis* should be discarded like dog excrement.

Thus, through the prolonged habit of being born and dying over many eras, that soul's inherent tendency (*Vasana*) becomes exactly that. Consequently, whatever course of action and course of duty was practiced by the soul residing within the body composed of the five elements, that soul can only return, fall back into it, and become the possessor of a life that exhibits various distortions. None of this constitutes true wisdom (*Jnana*).
Question: Then, are you also advocating the theory of evolution?

Guru: Yes, this is indeed evolution. We must remember that if the convergence of the lights of the earth, the sun, and the moon does not occur, not only animals, reptiles, termites, and other living beings, but also the marvels of creation—ranging from the aforementioned *Navapashana* to medicinal paths that cannot be categorized by name or number—would be unable to exist or survive in their respective forms and efficacies. Even electricity, which claims to stand at the zenith of growth and progress, is significantly affected by the changes in nature. Therefore, the only desire here is that one should not become the master of actions that seek to intimidate humanity by further chasing after such *Siddhis*, esoteric techniques, and theories of action like *Mayavada*.
Question: Having said all this, how will the people learn about our path and the duties that must be performed, or will they not learn?
Guru: People with faith, that is, those who believe and pray with faith in a lineage of Gurus (*Guru Parampara*), do indeed attain fruition, do they not?
Question: Fruition is attained by those who believe in other paths as well. Then why single out and specify our path in particular?

Guru: Our path has not emerged from reading about or following the footsteps of any categorized path such as Yoga, Bhakti, Karma, or Jnana. This is my own direct experience. I have clearly realized through experience that everything mentioned by name truly exists and that nothing is non-existent.
Question: But it is said that others have also realized it through experience, is it not?

Guru: What we call our experience has been shown in the philosophical aspect regarding the greatness of the Manvantaras, the great souls, the origin of the Trimurti system, and its efficacy in the Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga. The Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga are periods when one could reach as far as possible by worshiping, praying, and practicing Yoga in the Deva system. However, in Kali Yuga, not only is that system ineffective, but those who follow that system will not attain liberation in Kali Yuga either. That is why it is said that they have reached and stand in that path. The path advised by Shiva to Parvati in the Skanda Purana confirms this experiential truth - the Guru Gita.

In this Gita, Parvati asks Shiva, even though you exist as the life of all living beings and are the greatest ascetic and the most supreme among the Trimurtis, whom are you meditating upon? The subject matter discussed in the Guru Gita is Shiva's response to this question from Parvati in the form of advice. The Guru Gita discusses the subjects that even the Trimurtis do not have liberation, how the karma and knowledge of that Supreme Being are attained, how the disciple understands it, and how it helps in liberation.

All human souls have been caught up in the karmas of the Trimurti system or the Manu lineage for a long time. It has been proven beyond doubt that no matter which karma one is involved in, one's karma will not go to anything else beyond what one does. It is believed that this belongs to the original path of Manu.

The human souls have been believing in any one of these paths like the path of Devas, path of Acharyas, or path of Prophets till today. We have been shown all these paths, and the karmas that have come according to the order of gross, subtle, and causal in everything, the balance of good and evil existing in each, the deviations that caused the errors, and the corrections for them. Having experienced the meaning of what has been called chanting of names from time to time, and taking the matter which is its gross, subtle, and causal, Deva, Acharya, Prophet, Sage, Ascetic ٹ. Thus, whatever exists in the form of noun, and its karma, and the karmas that are gross, subtle, and causal which connect those karmas, our path is to correct the disciple in the field of experience and action.

There are few paths that correct as far as the gross, subtle, causal, and effect. That is our path. Our path is the Guru's path which corrects without error the method by which the gurus and wise men who have come so far correct our mistakes from their compassionate greatness. Here, some may see and hear certain things in the states of waking (Jagrat), dream (Svapna), and deep sleep (Sushupti). The Guru-disciple relationship here, or the greatness known as the Guru's compassion, is to elevate the disciple to the heights of a wise man by distinguishing and convincing them of what it is when the waking-deep sleep occurs in the two states of Turiya and Turiyatita.

Kali Yuga is the time when liberation is equally ordained for the Shudra, who does not grasp the meaning of the distinction of true Varnashrama Dharma but is entitled to complete self-knowledge in Kali Yuga, the Brahmin, the Kshatriya, and the Vaishya, who always wishes to be a merchant and a wealthy worker. That is why even the sages prayed, "O Lord, give me birth and let me see the Kali Yuga once." And the birth should be in India itself. India is the fertile land of knowledge of all types of sage lineages. The path of knowledge mentioned in texts like the Guru Gita should be acquired by man through karma.

This Guru's greatness has come as evidence revealed through the words of the perceptive sages that man can reach much higher levels from the knowledge that has come so far. That is why our path is delivered in the form of Guru-disciple dialogue through knowledge by thought, word, and deed without any web of magical powers. I pray to that treasure of compassion who has shown and told this lineage as a way to untie the knots of karma and dharma that have been entangled in life for lifetimes through the acquired karmas that are the gross, subtle, causal, and effects of the entire human lineage, not just this lineage, and to guide them to liberation, and to complete the dharma of the next yuga by coming in this yuga, so that it may be bestowed upon the human world to put an end to births and deaths forever.
Guru Vani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarppanappathippu 2002
The Divine Will Vested in Santhigiri

In the world, the influence of human history is upon Asia, and especially upon India. It is India that gives the complete account of the four Yugas and the Manvantaras. It still exists today in a way that cannot go wrong.

The duration of the *Yuga* system is determined by five visionary Gurus. There is a transitional period (*Sandhikal*) between the end of one *Yuga* and the beginning of the next. This transitional period acts as both an end and a beginning. It is impossible to determine the exact duration of this transitional phase when entering one *Yuga* from another. However, the *Manusmriti* states: the duration of the transitional period between the *Krita Yuga* and the beginning of the *Treta Yuga* is equal to the length of the *Krita Yuga* itself. Similarly, the durations of other *Yuga* transitions have also been specified. A *Chaturyuga*, comprising all four *Yugas*, is said to last for twelve thousand divine years. This calculation originates from the lineage of Manu. Yet, this calculation does not account for the transitional periods. The transitional period is of special significance as it is an era when countless great souls manifest and act. In a single *Yuga*, there are visionary Gurus whose foresight spans from five hundred to five thousand or even ten thousand years. When considering the total calculation of a lineage, it extends to ten thousand years and beyond; certain religious doctrines, establishing rules both old and new, even span from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand years.

According to the Hindu calculation of the fourteen *Manvantaras*, the combined duration of these fourteen *Manvantaras* is depicted as a single day of Brahma. Once that day concludes, the deluge (*Pralaya*) follows. The duration of the deluge is also equal to fourteen *Manvantaras*. However, it is also stated that somewhere in between, an obstacle arose and the action of the four-faced entity (*Nanmukhan*) went awry. In the works of certain artists who navigated through the Puranas, the concept of the four-faced entity was altered and instead depicted as the faces of Brahma. Through an alternative narrative route, various limbs of Brahma were similarly portrayed. The fictional tale of Brahma thus emerged to complete the *Trimurti* system. Lord Subrahmanya, who represents the path of wisdom, is known by the name *Arumukhan* (the six-faced one). When *Arumukhan* engaged in conversation with the faces of Brahma, the Brahma-conceived tale of the four-faced entity completely dissolved! When imagination and poetic fancies intertwined, leading to errors in the *Yuga Dharma* and the *Trimurti* system, the face of wisdom (*Jñānamukham*) ceased to speak. In the history of the four-faced entity, which became entangled in poetic imagination or Puranic lapses, it was depicted that Subrahmanya, in a fit of anger, pinched off the fourth face, the face of wisdom. Subsequently, when the depiction was restricted to the *Trimurtis*, the face of wisdom vanished entirely. The conceptual deities of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva were thus established by depicting them over these fundamental errors.

Proceeding along that path, the concept of the *Saptarshis* and the history of the lineage of Manu were lost. Returning to the present, wherever the Vedas were codified into four, the Shastras into six, and the Puranas into eighteen, they established the boundaries of rivers and artificially created oceans of knowledge. Even one who merely marked the boundaries of a lake or a stream attempted to articulate it with the profundity of oceanic wisdom. Thus, scholars sitting in royal assemblies crafted narratives favored by scholarly councils, thereby creating an ocean of wisdom. They brought it to completion by adding sounds, vowels, and consonants to impart meaning. When every meaning was formalized according to the scholar's rhetoric, an ocean-like knowledge seemed to emerge. This is essentially the poetic stage of historical scholars.

But this alone is insufficient for us. When human dharma, which ought to have provided light and righteousness to the eras, faltered, historians attempted to gloss over it by attributing it to the Stone Age and the like. All these efforts turned out to be like trying to straighten a tangled thread that had been thrown into the sea and had begun to rot and unravel.

Be that as it may, can we utilize the opportunity we have been given? If so, how? The given time refers to the era of the incarnation of great souls. That is, as mentioned earlier, from the great visionaries who foresaw five hundred years ahead, to Moses who came after Sri Krishna and his accompanying lineage, and subsequently the Buddha who appeared in India (Gautama Buddha, among the numerous Buddhas mentioned) - all offer specific calculations. Furthermore, the principles of *Siddhi* that emerged during certain intervals, and the various systems transmitted through them such as *Yoga Nyaya*—*Karma Yoga*, *Hatha Yoga*, *Chandrika Yoga*, and *Hamsa Yoga*—also created distortions, performing deeds that generated various miracles. When Dr. Somervell traveled through the outskirts of the Himalayas, he happened to see a person sitting like a skeleton. Upon approaching, this figure asked: "Is Henry IV currently ruling England?" Thus, through practices like *Kayakalpha* therapies, surviving for centuries and fulfilling actions described as miraculous penance exist here. The ascetic action that dictates the qualifications of an ascetic has been reduced to mere completion of rituals. This is not true penance; it is a form of yogic *Siddhi*.

Will human consciousness towards wisdom be awakened by recounting such miracles? Alternatively, if one fulfills the aphoristic points of Patanjali's Yoga and completes the ritualistic aspects of Yogic science, will it serve human dharma? The story of Ramanuja's disciple, Kabir Das, speaks of a Gorakshan (Gorakh) possessing miraculous powers. However, not only was he unable to defeat Kabir Das, but history also records that he eventually vanished. Then, what is the actual benefit of such miracles?

Now, let me narrate what was imparted at Santhigiri. It has been experienced as a truth that whatever must occur according to the divine will (*Brahmanishchaya*) exists in the *Trimurti* system exactly as it should. But upon deeper elaboration, dharma only persists where these three faces are mentioned. The face of wisdom is conspicuously absent there. There is no way to describe the course of events that unfold when visionaries arrive in those realms. We must understand one thing. Studying Sri Krishna, the architect of the Gita, will clarify a few aspects. History proves that Sri Krishna was deliberately brought forth by divine will. The sorrow Sri Krishna endured during his final days is beyond description. Subsequently, numerous great souls arrived bearing various doctrines. They all met the same fate that befell Krishna. This was the exact experience of Moses who followed Krishna, of the Buddha in India, and of countless other great souls who came, with or without the confines of caste and religion.

If we consider around twenty-five historical figures, the Prophet is one such great soul. The Prophet, who arrived through the very same path as Jesus, encountered the exact same destiny. What can anyone say bypassing this truth? The Prophet did not speak for any specific caste or religion. He spoke for the entirety of mankind. It was the Prophet, attaining Samadhi in the seventh state, who proclaimed: "Oh Lord, what is this that you have done to me, who believed that there is nothing but You, and that God and Truth are one? It is the *Jinn*s who rule the world." Did he speak a lie, or did he state this for the sake of the world? Other than worshipping these *Jinn*s, what else have we been able to accomplish to this day? Each religion, in its own language, worships a god, a goddess, a yogi, a rishi, an ascetic, or a sage; however, in reality, what we worship are the *Jinn*s. Even after that, we have seen so many great souls who have remained unacknowledged to this day. Radha Swami is one among them. However, there is no Guru-disciple relationship in that system.
What is the Guru-disciple relationship?

The guru-disciple relationship corrects the changes in states in various ways by elevating the states of waking (jagrat), dreaming (swapna), and vision (darshana) to the transcendent state of turiya. For one state, there are seven thousand four hundred and forty-four visions. He who completes the seven states in this manner is the one who has fully realized the presence of God. Then comes the realization of God, the realization of Brahman, and the realization of the Supreme Brahman. It is because there exists a particular state about which nothing can be explained that the sorrow of these great souls cannot be resolved. First, they must be liberated. After that, their lineage must be liberated. However, only a Guru who comes with the permission of Brahman to liberate them can recognize whether the aforementioned ethereal voice is true or not, without utilizing sleight of hand, mystical powers, or acquired knowledge. Those who dismiss both knowledge and ignorance, who speak of duality and non-duality and then settle into a comfortable state, do not realize this. Only a soul that is born having inherently completed the eighth state, having taken crores of births and thirsted solely for wisdom, can actualize the word of Brahman.

Another thing to be done for this is to show in a vision who all these aforementioned great souls were and how they came, and thereby realize who stands where in the changed states of those times. It is our destined duty to discover the self-sacrifice each of such great souls has made for our sake, and to knock and open those doors. Duty is not a buffoonery of arguing and winning by debating whether something exists or not.

Vision (darshana) is the harmonious uniting of the ascetic and the wise one who have led the soul to a virtuous path, showing and correcting the mistakes and good deeds that have occurred. The transition of states (avasthantara) is the categorization of the stream of light by seven, seven thousand, and seven thousand four hundred and forty-four, upon reaching the state where the soul makes an offering of the soul.

Believing without a doubt that we all are indebted to the divine decree that proved this to be true, one should pronounce as Guru the one who reaches the soul-vision of 'Jagrat swapna sushuptinam sakshipoorthi namonamah' (Salutations to the complete witness of the waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states) and makes corrections. This should not be fulfilled merely through the words of an eminent scholar. This is the measure of the stream of light completed through self-realization. For this, the language of the Vedic scholar is as follows:
The inner light, the outer light,
The inward light, the Supreme Beyond,
The light of lights, the self-effulgent light,
The light of the self, I am Shiva.

This is the Tantric aspect. However, none of this is our sorrow. Let us begin to study at least from the time of Sri Krishna. Honoring the words of the great souls who had the wisdom to humbly prostrate and express their sorrow to that great power that sent them to act upon this, before finally leaving their bodies after working within the systems of Hindu knowledge that have existed from then until today, we must highlight the Dharma of Kali (Kalidharma) that has passed until yesterday and which exists today.

What is written down stating that Kali is acceptable and not acceptable? It would be a pitiful sight to see scholars, who logically assign meanings even to vowels and consonants, rotting and falling here. The cycle of time to recognize this Dharma of Kali, imparted by that divine decree so as to be passed on to at least the coming generations, has caught up with us. That is, by presenting to our grandchildren or the future generation the truth that has shown us, along with cause and effect, the Dharma that came, or has come, or is yet to come to implement the divinely ordained action denoted by the four epochs, complete the duty of a householder.

If one can present the sacrifice, love, and respect of the wise and the learned, each person becomes a special manifestation of Dharma that reveals the truth. The wheel of time is returning to us the brilliant sacrifices of the selfless, so that seekers of all kinds of knowledge can study and verify each truth through experience. The intention here is to give our little ones the opportunity to open and examine that brilliantly colorful sacrifice that has passed, is present, and is yet to come. Kali is the unique cycle of time that the divine decree has opened up for us for this purpose. This Kali is a special Dharma that can be experienced by the people of the world and all living beings.

I am informing you repeatedly—of all epochs, Kali is the good one. Our life's goal should be to fulfill the path of Dharma, defined as gross, subtle, causal, and effect, by transcribing into the atom and the infinite the brilliant sacrifice of the great prophets who shared a noble life or passed away sacrificing their lives grappling with body and soul, and of the eminent sages who shared their lives for us.

Let us share forever the pain of revealing the truth through the epoch and the life of Dharma, and the pure blessedness that has been fully experienced. The divine purpose is to show us the revered life of the Guru and disciple, which is our nectar of pure consciousness and is of an absorptive nature. This is the path of salvation of Santhigiri, ordained by the Divine. This is the truth of truths, the source of blessedness, and pure, brilliant genius!
Guruvani
October 2002

In what all ways have our ancestors provided guidance for our sake, or for the sake of this worldly knowledge, or in the financial and knowledge-related fields of the world! They have shown us by finding and applying every matter suitable for guidance. One of the most important among them is Ayurveda. It is the Veda that holds the secret of life.

According to the topography of our land, harsh administration of medicines should not be done. Ingredients like mercury, sulphur, and arsenic should not be applied as they are. However, they can be processed, brought to the practice called Gurukalpa, and used in the Gurukalpa Seva system. But the Western method of application is not like that. Today, there is a speed there akin to boiling rice in five minutes. The medicines given to us are those prepared using ashes (bhasmas) and various other such materials. They quickly affect the body. This will harm the body.

There are reasons why the way Westerners produce and apply medicine is different from ours. One is the difference in topography. Another is the lack of availability of medicinal plants. It is difficult to get plant varieties there. But we do not have that difficulty. Any kind of plant that grows in our forests is medicinal. However, there are also difficulties in utilizing these medicinal plants. Our ancestors have also shown us the ways to overcome those difficulties. The same systems that have existed since very ancient times are still in existence today. But today, that is not enough. Why?

Let us assume that someone manifested a god, someone manifested a goddess—or rather, that they even manifested and fulfilled the great sage Dhanvantari himself, who is considered the most complete figure in medical science. They might have prescribed two or four medicines to this worshipper. Taking the medicine obtained in this way, considering it together with his ascetic power and the theory he has been following, he will apply it to some people. And the disease will be cured. Does that mean we should assume that the diseases of the entire world are cured?

The disease will be cured. All those are truthful aspects. But this is not enough. What we need is a precept to act by seeing and knowing in the action that is changing momentarily. Kali is the best epoch suited to create such a thing. This is God-given. If we continue to burn and distill as was done in past times, the Dharma of this Kali will not be fulfilled. Everything that exists is true. But for which time is this to be applied? We must think about this time. That is Kali. Kali is the time we have been given to be born.

It is said that even some gods have wished to be born as at least a blade of grass in Kali. Why? That desire is because if they were born as at least a blade of grass in this Bharata, they could fulfill this karma in the growth and glory of this nature. But we have suffered some kind of loss to the extent that we are unable to be born and grow in that Bharata and honor the Dharma that has imparted vigilance and truth.

During the time of Sree Rama, Bharadwaja brought forth the science of aeronautics (Vimana Shastra). His Guru had told Bharadwaja that such a science was not needed for that era. If the flying machine (Vimana) was built, it would lead to everyone's destruction. But Bharadwaja did not obey. He went to Kubera's kingdom and had the king there build it. The war occurred because that flying machine was used to come here and abduct Sita. We all presume this to be a war between Rama and Ravana. But it was entirely a struggle between a Guru and his disciple. Consequently, the kingdom itself was destroyed. The calamities resulting from not doing what is necessary at the appropriate time have still not left us today. After that, we have never been able to regain the sanctity of that Guru-disciple relationship.

Let someone else make the goods. We will get them too. But that is not equal to the Dharma (duty/nature) of our life (Jeeva). Our birth is meant for thinking and making others think about the Dharma of life. Our soul is confined within an instinctual origin (Vasanas), having seen, heard, known, and acted upon good and bad across many births. We must absolutely possess a state of mind capable of contemplating what system is required to understand that soul.

If a scholar sees a poor man doing something, he will only treat it with contempt. The scholar has the attitude that he knows everything. But what is this poor man doing? He takes a fallen man onto his lap, nurses him, and speaks to him about good and bad. But the scholar does not know how to do this. He [the poor man] does not have the scholar's attire or education. Without these two, what else can be done!

What is this nursing? It is a task that depletes one's merit (Punya). At the same time, the other person's merit increases. There is a Karma (action) that can reclaim this lost merit. What is that dedicated work? You will not attain it by simply setting out somewhere. For that, one goes and knocks on the doors of a deity whose eyes remain closed, crying, "Oh Lord, didn't you see, haven't I been calling and doing all this for so long?" But the Lord will open His eyes. There is a way for that. That path can only be known while your soul is still residing within its cage (the body).

If we have an educated scholar, an officer, and a doctor who knows the body by dissecting it—thus various kinds of people—in our house, the children of that house will walk around with quite a bit of arrogance. Does carrying this arrogance mean that they know about their home, their land, and their country just because they have all this? By instilling this arrogance, this ego, into these children, they have become spoiled to the extent that they cannot distinguish between wealth, capability, and the actions through which these are applied. This is our situation today. By composing, fabricating, or studying Puranas, how much knowledge can we really gain to change this situation?

There lies a Karma here, taken up through immense effort over a long period, grown logically, discovered, honored with love, humbled, struggled, and sacrificed for. We have not seen the doctrine of this Karma. We have not acquired that knowledge. Without knowing whether that knowledge exists or not, what else are we doing other than amusing ourselves by arguing back and forth that it exists or it does not? What exists is not going to vanish, and what does not exist is not going to materialize. This is a matter from my own experience.

Now, regarding ghosts (Pishacha). If asked whether ghosts exist, the answer is yes. If anyone says they don't, I ask them, then why do people perform sorcery, tantric rituals, mantra worship, and death rituals invoking ghosts? Can those who perform these actions abandon the ghost? It is easy to say it does not exist, and it is easy to say it does. It was the former Acharyas who stated that everything from ghosts to the realm of vampires (Vethala Nagaram) is agony. They spoke after seeing it. It is only when one reaches the realm of vampires that one understands the special nature of the sorrow there. Beyond that, when one reaches the actions of Shaktheyam, Shaivam, and Vaishnavam, one will see the positions where gods, goddesses, sages, and ascetics stand. Even if seen, to bring it into one's experience, there must be a Guru to instruct, saying, "Do only this in this specific way," or "Manifest it thus"—"Do not do that, do this instead"; he imparts it by making it part of your experience and your fortune.

In the truth of life that comes according to our Karma and Dharma, everyone is equal. There is no other justification in this. However, if there are five children in a family, all five will have slight differences in their course of Karma. They are all indeed the children of the same father and mother. But one will not be like the other. One might have more compassion for the poor. One might want to marry from a poor family. People end up poor due to the lack of merit (Punya) in their soul. Not everyone can take that upon themselves. It will only increase the pain of the soul.

When we say 'Sadhukkal' (the gentle/poor), it should not be understood as the poor. It means 'Sathukkal' (the virtuous). Do not try to remove these flaws using your logic and intellect. What you need is a life that examines the flaws of the soul and transforms them. There is no point in showing off other justifications and arrogance. Whatever weight (arrogance) we have is ours alone. No one can steal it. Similarly, our good and bad are right in our own hands. Our children are the ones who transform it by suffering little by little, imbibing Dharma through the experience of that pain, and realizing merit. There is no point in preaching Vedanta for this. There is also no point in trying to correct children by scolding them. Without knowing the purpose for which you are getting married, what will the children born from such a marriage become? What is the Karma that correctly sustains the affairs of a household? How should our virtues be situated in that Karma, and how should this virtuous Karma be given to the land and the home? Without contemplating any of this, have we been able to show our children any action that provides satisfaction, other than bragging and recounting the magnitude of education, the magnitude of properties and possessions, and the magnitude of prosperity? This is our shortcoming.

You do not need to teach children Vedanta. It is enough to see children as children. If you find children with natural aptitudes (Vasanas), you should guide them along that path. There is no point in applying aptitude in unwanted ways; it must be applied in the right direction. This approach is needed for every one of our homes. You should not distance yourselves from believing, loving, knowing, and letting others know about this. This should be the goal of each one of you. The goal of an ascetic, a wise person, a worker, and a devotee. The path of Santhigiri is the one that unites all these paths. It is a path capable of discovering what the union of life (Jeeva) and the soul (Atma) is. This path will absolutely help you to move forward by understanding what the agony of the vampire realm (Vethala Nagaram) is.

In our habit of thinking categorized into Shaivism, Shaktism, and Vaishnavism, or in the realms of gods, goddesses, sages, ascetics, the wise, and devotees who have fulfilled the course of karma brought about by their compassionate nature, where should we position our ancestors? This must be our goal. If you cannot achieve this, at least your children must be able to. You have the absolute authority to reflect upon who you are within that karma. You should not go seeking anyone's blessings (*anugraha*) or wrath (*nigraha*). People come to me here as well, asking for blessings. The knowledge of these poor souls is an ignorance that does not comprehend what this blessing or curse truly means. It is not blessings or wrath that you should seek. Then what should you seek? The affliction in your life—in that course of karma experienced by the body and mind, what is the *vasana* (inherent tendency) of the karmic course residing deep within the mind, and how shall we eradicate this *vasana*? That *vasana* remains rooted in dharma. As long as the *vasana* remains active, you will unknowingly usurp various things. Everyone usurps in different ways; that is all. Some like their father, some like their mother, some like their elder sister, some like their elder brother—this liking itself is a form of usurpation. What is the point of criticizing our neighbours while holding on to this theft ourselves? "That girl ruined my son; otherwise, my son would have been well-behaved." What a falsehood is being uttered here? What justice will the future generations learn from the absolute form of this injustice that is practiced by speaking in such a manner?

No one ruins anyone else. That origin, which is replete with *vasana*, has manifested on its own. We lack the karmic consciousness to instill good *vasanas* in them from childhood in order to transform that innate nature. Instead, we have reached a stage of action where we curse ourselves, claiming that we are inherently bad. What is the use of such people like us finding fault with those around us?

It might be true that the girl or boy in the neighboring house has flaws. What should we do about that? Should we wish that they somehow perish in those flaws? That is a course of karma acquired from birth. We should attempt to transform that karmic course in a way known to us. What is the action that helps shift them from that mindset and bring them into another mindset? They can be transformed through that action. I received a reward for bringing about such a transformation. I shall tell you about it.
Guruvani
November 2002

While I was staying at Shantigiri in Varkala, a mother came to me and was cured of her illness. Thus, they had faith in me. During their harvest season, she would bring a portion of it to me. She would also bring enough hay to feed two or three cows for a year. A girl in that house faced a severe crisis. Then, this mother and her husband came to me and pleaded with tears that I should visit their home. I went, did what was necessary, and their distress was alleviated. Because a major affliction was resolved in this manner, they all developed great affection for me. I advised them on certain matters. The mutual misunderstandings, quarrels, and lack of prosperity in their home were resolved. A situation arose where the father, mother, and siblings lived together in mutual love. With that, they began to obey whatever I said. One day, a boy from that house sent me a letter stating that from now on, they would only listen to what the Swami says.

Three years passed. One day, an incorporeal voice (*ashariri*) spoke—saying that I should not stay in a manner visible to two people. (These things occur in a certain spiritual state. Whenever such revelations and experiences occur, major events will happen within three years.) Since the instruction was received not to stay there, the person accompanying me suggested that we could go to that family (mentioned earlier), as they had been inviting us for a long time. Then I too thought that it would serve the purpose of relocating as instructed and accepting their invitation, and so decided to go.

Thus, we went there. Upon arriving, another person had come with a car; it was his father's death anniversary ritual (*aandubali*), and I needed to go there. Saying that I would return from there later, I went with the person who came with the car. After I left, the mother found a letter that had fallen from the girl's book in that house. She gave it to the father. That letter was written to her by a boy. It was written in the letter that I was their enemy. When I counselled them and set them on the right path, their illicit relationship was severed. Therefore, I allegedly spoke in order to make enemies of them! Naturally, this girl developed an enmity towards me. The mother too felt distressed by me. This distress had befallen a family who had visited me ten to twelve times within a span of six months. That does not matter; it is a reality that can occur in human beings.

But that is not the main issue. In front of their house, there are small-scale industries and a market. All of this is situated on their property. The one associated with this girl went to these shops and had all the youths there well-prepared and stationed. They were standing with sticks, wooden clubs, and machetes. He stood hidden without coming near. As soon as the car arrived there, all of them rose up together. I could not understand what was happening. Then, the girl's father approached me and said softly, "Swami should not stay here now. I will explain the rest later." He then blocked them by spreading both his arms. Therefore, nothing happened to me. Otherwise, it would have been the end right then.
The very next day, a journalist made a speech:

"Sometimes the Swami will appear, only to aggravate the flaws of the young girls. And then he will extract as much as possible and leave." He delivered this 'journalistic speech' in many places. This is my experience.

Another similar case is that of the woman who jumped into the well at the Pothencode ashram and died. That woman had a mental illness. Her illness was a convenience for her husband. When her illness was cured, she became an inconvenience to him. Therefore, he forcibly brought her back and left her here again. In that despair, she jumped into the well. This case too earned me a good reputation and status. Around five thousand people gathered and came here to perform 'Pushpanjali' (floral offering). By Pushpanjali, I mean an offering of abuses similar to the Cherthala Pooram songs. It even became a Crime Branch case.

Numerous such truths that have been experienced are before me. My entire life consists of numerous experiences like this. It is these experiences that I am presenting before you. Why am I telling you this?

Where do the demon, god, goddess, sage, ascetic, the wise, the devotee, and numerous such great souls stand? In which zodiac and in which sky do they stand? What are the qualities of that sky? What are the properties of that light? Similarly, what are the characteristics of the nine worlds, and what are the effects produced when these nine worlds revolve? The factual aspects of having experienced all these are before me. We must also understand that this has the nature of revolving through epochs. Then, we must experience those epochs themselves. Along with that, we must also reflect upon the evolution of our soul.

The tendency (*vasana*) is what contemplates the evolution of the soul. This *vasana* is equally essential for the father, the mother, and the children. If you are convinced that this is necessary, you should not speak of arguments, doctrines, or individuality. If you waste time talking like that, the children will become sinners to such an extent that you will be unable to do anything. When they become sinners, their arrogance will inflate, and they will cease to respect anything. No weapon will have the power to cut through the core of this arrogance. What follows will be a wrestling match involving wealth, power, and education. Furthermore, there is caste, and upon that, a religion. You are hiding behind such ideologies.

Another thing to understand is the state of your ancestors who existed in the karmic path of your past, and the state of the karmic course that has evolved over the subsequent ten thousand years. There is an experiential aspect of perceiving this here. I wish to share what I see with you. When I say this, those who are receptive will accept it, and others will not. Let them accept or discard it. That is not my concern. Even if only one person attains goodness, that is sufficient. That one person is of great significance to me. I am certain that it will eventually multiply into six, thousands, hundreds of thousands, and tens of millions. When this occurs, the karmic course that encompasses those tens of millions will enter your home. This is my objective. The primary source of this is my own experience.

We must thoroughly comprehend the paths of the deity, goddess, sage, and ascetic, and traverse through them. Similarly, ranging from malevolent spirits to the king of jinns, or entities referred to in doctrines as Brahmarakshas and Gandharvas, one must identify their abodes and understand what must be done to intercept and alter that karmic course. I shall impart no other reasoning to you but this. I am conveying to you the logic derived from the experience of perceiving this karmic path.

I am finding solutions to certain incurable diseases caused by this karmic course. This is the mission entrusted to me by God. No one else can perform this task. To execute this duty, permission is required. Furthermore, that permission must be granted by that supremely authorized entity itself. Otherwise, there will be no enduring resolution to this.

It is inadequate to merely term this as the purification of ancestors or deities. Regarding these ancestors, if they are meant to evolve, they must be nurtured; if they are to be sustained, they must be maintained; or if they are destined for destruction, they must be eliminated. Having done so, whatever is necessary must be infused into your life. Likewise, whatever needs to be imparted to the deity, sage, ascetic, enlightened being, and devotee must be transmitted. Consequently, each of your homes will become a receptacle for this transmission. However, when it is infused into a thousand homes in this manner, only one or two may prove suitable for such a state. Yet, from those two, it can be transmitted to hundreds of thousands. That will require generations. When a hundred such generations have passed, the dharma of this Kali Yuga will be fulfilled.

What is the dharma of Kali Yuga? It is the dharma of direct manifestation. It involves witnessing the manifestation of spirits, gods, goddesses, sages, and ascetics; observing their variations in form; perceiving their colors and attributes; identifying the causes behind these colors and attributes; and thereby envisioning the solar system intricately linked with the twenty-seven stars, twelve zodiac signs, and nine planets. None of these elements we discover were created by us. If the calculations of every solar system positioned in the corners of this universe—indeed, of countless thousands of such solar systems—reside with you and me, then we are inevitably bound to preserve them. If we fail to preserve this, there is no purpose in discoursing in this manner.

Your children must be capable of preserving this. Studying Vedanta will not suffice for this, nor will the practice of sorcery achieve it. It cannot be attained merely by purifying a deity or adorning one's chosen deity with a full coating of sandalwood paste. Even the complete manifestation of Shakta, Shaiva, and Vaishnava traditions will be of no avail.

Let us weigh the profound words spoken by the Prophet in his final days: 'Jinns rule the world.' If you believe that his personality transcends you all, you must respect the gravity of those words. Similarly, figures like Sree Narayana Guru, Swami Rama Tirtha, and Jesus—why do we bear the burden of unrighteous actions conjured by mere intellect, instead of acknowledging the powerful karmic deeds of such supreme renunciates? If it is out of your own sheer ignorance that you bear the weight of this supposed salvation and logic, at the very least, refrain from dragging your children into it. If this affliction strikes the children, it will grow within them to an extent where no one can do anything about it. Thereafter, even if one despairs, weeps helplessly, and abandons life itself in anguish, that wrongful karmic course cannot be reversed.

This very issue resides within each of your homes. Through which doctrine are you going to convince whom? First, introduce this to your children and convince them. To achieve this, fully believe in the words of Jesus, who urged us to seek and to knock so that the door may be opened. The words he uttered in anguish, 'Father, have you too forsaken me?', are absolutely true. In the heavens he witnessed, that karmic action remains fully pervasive. However, no one comprehends that heaven or that karma. Standing within that realm, in the parlance of those times, bestow your love upon deities, spirits, or whatever you prefer. Yet, the fact that the people crucified Jesus remains an enduring truth.

According to the divine will, we must attain a resolution. Santhigiri has been bestowed with a path to instruct our children, the generations to come, and their lineage on what must be done to fulfill this resolution. However, you are not acquainted with this path. Therefore, if explained, you will not grasp it easily. You will only understand it through the familiarity gained over a period of time. It is enough to proceed with faith and love for this. Nothing else is required. Those who rely on pure logic will only feel inclined to dismiss it. They will not be inspired to connect this with their lives. Convincing someone that a matter disconnected from life can be accomplished is futile. Nevertheless, it might be possible to bring them into faith by revealing certain aspects rooted in their past lives.

Some individuals, during their childhood, may witness certain lights and forms. Some might consider this experience to be demonic. Others may believe it to be some extraordinary divine attribute. There are also those who dismiss it as mere ignorance. None of these assumptions are correct. Regarding this, there are specific causes and effects involved. What we need is a karmic process to elucidate these causes and effects. If one can comprehend these causes and seek a resolution, there is no need to depend on anything else.

What we have accumulated through the merits of our past lives has grasped us as both good and evil. When it takes hold of the mind, it manifests as disease. Therefore, one can only contemplate a remedy after identifying the malevolent thoughts or errors associated with the karmic course that have entered the mind's resolutions and hesitations. It cannot be resolved by a single word or even a hundred words. This has occurred through life. It can only be transformed through life itself. For that, one must understand what each individual needs to do.

For some, certain issues are resolved through faith. That is not my doing. It is entirely their own faith. There is no necessity here for me to instruct and make them believe. However, there are numerous cases that have been resolved through my counsel. Certain cases that I thought would never be resolved have indeed been resolved. There are ample examples demonstrating that if an opportunity is created to guide someone by saying, 'Doing this will remove this specific deficiency,' a solution can be found for any case. If asked how this happens, I would say it is your faith itself.
Guruvani
December 2002

What is the first thing that you, as householders (Grihasthashramis), should consider? Instead of reflecting upon what must essentially be considered, you are creating chaos by feigning utter cleverness. You are exhibiting that reckless exuberance even in certain wedding celebrations. Instead of understanding the true essence of marriage and demonstrating the dharma that must be imparted to children, husbands, and wives, you are merely displaying reckless exuberance.

Struggling to educate and raise your children is your fundamental duty. You are the ones who have come to fulfill that duty. There is nothing extraordinary to claim after having done it. However, when you perform this, the spiritual merit to transform that action into *Dharma* (righteousness) must become ingrained in you. You should not assume that this nobility can be attained from anywhere else other than through the ashram. If you attempt to achieve it from elsewhere, you will end up losing your children and your wife. Whether you perform actions from your home, from your homeland, or by traveling across the entire world, you will suffer loss. If it leads to such a loss, you must abandon that action altogether. Instead, you should not desire to gather and hoard everything in your hands. Due to the lack of this knowledge, the actions performed by some people under the guise of devotion are fraught with numerous errors, ultimately turning them into entities unfit to exist either at home or in society.

You are oblivious to this. You do nothing other than conducting your own spectacle alongside the grand spectacle of the world. Only if you possess the realization that you are doing nothing, will you be able to recognize what you have actually done. To what extent does our action measure up to our knowledge, what is its utility, how much of a model has it been for others, and how much *Dharma* have we envisioned and imparted to our children through our lives? You neither find the time nor possess the capability to contemplate such matters. On the contrary, you display your arrogance by exaggerating the magnitude of your deeds while making your wife and children sit as an audience. This is the greatest betrayal you inflict upon your wife and children. Alternatively, it is the ignorance of leading a life unfit for this world by heedlessly following the words of a wife, and then taking immense pride in rambling about every single word of that life. If you fail to understand that this is what resides within each of you, who can do anything to help?

Your attitude and knowledge are not inclined towards understanding this. You do not even learn to walk a single step on that path. Those who come here try to learn it to a small extent. However, that is insufficient. It is not that I have not shared this knowledge with you. I am imparting it to you to the best of my ability. But the moment you turn away, you brush it all off, just as one brushes off dust. If you discard it in such a manner, what can I possibly do?

You bring your children and leave them here (in the ashram). You are bringing and leaving here those who are unfit to be kept at home. These children are a burden to the house. It is this burden that you are imposing upon the ashram. Why do you bring and dump those who are useless at home here? What would be the outcome if one who is incapable of behaving in accordance with one's own home, who cannot live in harmony with any other home, and who has grown up with the wretched habit of treating the entire land as their personal property, is brought and dumped in the ashram? Having grown up with this wretched habit, they preach numerous ideologies. They merely put forth justifications attempting to rationalize the wrongdoings they have been committing. However, having understood that this is your habit, has anyone undertaken any action to prevent it? At the same time, you possess a peculiar tendency to remain silent even after knowing, seeing, or hearing things. You lack the words to speak against it. You do not have the habit; nor do you have the capability to act. Or, if you do act, it goes astray.

This has been part of your experience to this day. Understand this and act accordingly. A great *Dharma* that must be cultivated by you, your children, and your children's children is being followed here. You must not attach any other justifications to this *Dharma*. There may be numerous justifications. But none of them can be appended to this. Why?

You are undertaking and executing actions ranging from the realm of demons to the city of phantoms. There is one who has become the leader of the city of phantoms. Let it be anyone. Transcending the city of phantoms to become divine, one observes how many demons, deities, sages, and visionaries have existed, acting out of entanglements, both good and bad, everywhere. It is only after transcending this that one imbibes the distinct state of gods and goddesses. This is precisely why it is said that a Guru is necessary. While providing guidance for this, the Guru might act sternly towards us. However, in ashram life, that would be an established precedent. One requires the power of endurance to comply with this. Otherwise, staying in the ashram will make you corrupt. Furthermore, you will also bring disrepute to the ashram. This is what I have been able to earn from you. Understanding this, if you do not contemplate and live in a manner to prevent this danger from gripping the children who live without comprehending the will of the ashram, there is no point in bringing and tying them up in the ashram. Instead of contemplating this, what are you doing? To accommodate your justifications and to achieve your objectives, you associate with various people in various places, grasping onto the very same old destruction, establishing it within your home, your land, and your inner self, and attempting to systematize it. How will you transform this ignorance? It is only after attaining this awareness that you should come, go, and stay in the ashram, and seek all aspects of existence.

Thousands of families, including those who have believed in this place from the early days, complete their knowledge at teashop gatherings. They go and drink black coffee in teashops that operate with fires burning, without opening doors or windows. If one listens from outside to four people drinking black coffee, it sounds like a thousand people drinking *payasam*. This is the sound of swallowing heat. And sitting there, they decree words intended to purify the land and its people. Then, once dawn breaks, it becomes their collective, desire-driven action. They cannot return from there until they have celebrated it at least until eight o'clock. In the next phase, after somehow passing the time until five in the evening, they will wander around cities and slums. Thus, there is a constant struggle involving the city and the slum. Who have you become through such acts of completion? If they are employed professionals, they have discovered greater pretense. Both husband and wife have jobs. Their sole thought is how many marks their jointly raised children can attain by providing tuition for every subject. It is precisely when they have exhausted all avenues for this that the boy in the neighboring house scores one mark higher. Then, this mother cannot sit still due to the agony. When the father returns, the rest of the quarrel is directed at him: "You are nowhere to be found around here, just lying around." If necessary, they will fight among themselves, and both will attempt to find completion by blaming each other. As these children grow up, they will turn out in a multitude of divergent ways.

It is the *Dharma* of the householder stage that performs such actions that you have studied and internalized. In some households, if there are five children, they hold jobs and govern in five different countries. Thus, having learned disasters disguised as the ornaments of Western nations, these wealthy individuals are propagating their version of *Dharma*. These are the misdeeds you are committing. To whom will you answer for all of this? Does your life possess any spiritual merit after committing so much? Is the trajectory of your life's actions capable of upholding *Dharma*? What is the tragedy of a life? Having to raise fools, barbarians, and the vile is indeed due to the tragedy of one's own life.

It is seen everywhere that householders lack the habit of thinking about what work they are doing. If you grow up like this, you and your children will waste the opportunity given by God and go astray on another path. I know that even thousands of experienced householders have gone wrong. I am not just saying this as empty words. Having established the system of Gurupooja here, explaining its merits and demerits, and telling you how to reach the path of attaining merit through the duty of the times, I am trying to direct you towards it. But you do not have the persistence for that. You are showing the same antics towards this as you showed to a sorcerer, a tantric, or a scholar.

What you need are not these antics. I am neither a scholar nor an ignorant person. If asked whether I am something else, I am not that either. I am entrusting you with the work God entrusted to me. You have not understood this yet. I do not know when you will understand. Standing beneath the mess created by everyone, you are managing it and pretending to complete the karma.

Only a Guru can tell the story of the city of vampires (Vethalanagara). The foresight of that Guru is the karma of repeatedly observing the Yugadharma (duty of the age) and demonstrating it in action before the people. This Vethalanagara is a terrifying realm. It will not step aside for anyone. Whoever touches it will only lie there bewildered and finally tear it away and leave. Apart from that, no one has anything else to do here. If this is to be uprooted from your life, there is only that aspect called Gurupooja.

Once, a Supreme Court judge, while talking about his wife, asked me if a ghost possession could be broken. This possession brings destruction to that life. This man is someone who travels seeking paths in science. Furthermore, he is someone who causes headaches to poor children. This man has the ability to turn people into non-believers instead of believers and to turn them into a lifeless course of karma. This is the problem of not having gained experience in living in the sacred aspect of the relationship called Guru and disciple to remove the afflictions of one's own family and loved ones.

Good books were taken from cultural centers like Nalanda and Takshashila in India, portrayed as parts of various sciences, and brought back here to be taught. This is the work the British did. Along with that, they imparted their culture here. Today's scientists and lawyers are the ones who imbibed that culture. It is that lawyer who says that even though his wife has died, her ghost is with him. That man is trying to sustain it. This is the boundary of science. There are some other boundaries like this. The stories told by Socrates' disciples are taken in parts, studied, and distributed. This is the boundary of our professors. Today's philosophers also have this boundary. The conclusion of this philosopher is the opinion of today's world.

This is not what we need. Realize through experience. We must understand that the previously mentioned scientist-lawyer, a person who is entitled to highlight India's identity as a Supreme Court judge, only has the karma of following a ghost. Then what is the difference between the educated and the uneducated? The mentioned ghost is not just an ordinary ghost. It is the ghost of a learned Brahmin's wife. No matter what science they talk about or whether they have imbibed Western culture, they know the logic and karma of this. That is that inquiry. What does a non-believer who gets their guidance know? You must understand that the philosophy they distribute is not the philosophy that belongs to their belief.

We respect everything. We do not discard anything without respect. Ghosts? They indeed exist. Demons? They too exist. If they did not exist, how did the names originate? Just as a tool is made and given a name, this is the realm of naming what exists. Only a wise person (jnani) can do that. There are many types of such wise people. Everyone knows about praying to a ghost, making it appear, and achieving desired things. The story of a ghost appearing from the stone on which feet were rubbed and washed is told in Tulsidas's story. It is enough to state what exists like this. If an educated person quotes each of these and says the path of wisdom is science, that becomes the authority here.

But this is not what we need. Stories are fine. But we need the karma that brings the essence (experience) through the story and liberation through the essence. The act of dismissing things by telling a story and laughing 'hahaha' will not do us any good either. Does the nature of a lame person mocking others—saying 'walk like me if you have the guts'—suit us when the spiritual path reaches a dead end?

If you talk about the karma that brings liberation through essence, it won't even enter the minds of ashrams. Because ashrams are entangled and completely submerged in puranas and epics. Therefore, they cannot do anything. This is not what we need. We need the karma that brings liberation to all demons—even up to Vethalanagara—through experience.
